SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2#2/r6.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2#2/r6.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2#2/r6.claim: The Quran combines different modes of expression in a carefully placed artistic composition that moves knowledgeable listeners to reverence.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2#2/r6.anchor: ثم هو يجمع بين ضروب القول المختلفة ويؤلف بينها في حشد فني عجيب

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2#2/r7.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2#2/r7.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2#2/r7.claim: Quranic expression has been extensively studied for artistic imagery, structure and music, diction, and the coherence of suras, verses, openings, and endings.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2#2/r7.anchor: فقد درس من حيث تصويره الفني فكان أجمل تصوير وأبرع لوحة فنية

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2#2/r8.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2#2/r8.speaker: الفخر الرازي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2#2/r8.claim: Al-Razi describes the Quran as like one sura because its parts connect, indeed like one verse.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2#2/r8.anchor: وكان كما قال الفخر الرازي: إن القرآن كالسورة الواحدة لاتصال بعضه ببعض بل هي كالآية الواحدة.

BURHAN:v2p67/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p67/r7.speaker: الحسين بن محمد بن حبيب النيسابوري
BURHAN:v2p67/r7.claim: A second position reported by al-Naysaburi says the entire Qur'an is mutashabih, citing 39:23.
BURHAN:v2p67/r7.anchor: وقد حكى الحسين بن محمد بن حبيب النيسابوري في هذه المسألة ثلاثة أقوال

ITQAN:v2p566/r20.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p566/r20.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p566/r20.claim: المثاني is the plural of مثنى.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p196/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p196/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p196/r1.claim: When God and His mercy are mentioned, the believers' skins soften and their hearts become hopeful; “soften” also carries the sense of becoming tranquil.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p196/r1.anchor: ثم إذا ذكروا لله ورحمته لانت جلودهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p196/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p196/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p196/r2.claim: The mention of hearts shows their emotional response; skin shivering stands for the fear within, while its softening implies God's mercy even when unstated.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p196/r2.anchor: وكان في ذكر القلوب في هذه الجملة دليل على تأثرها عند السماع، فاكتفى بقشعريرة الجلود

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p196/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p196/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p196/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas's father al-ʿAbbas reports from the Prophet that fear-induced shivering sheds sins like leaves from a dry tree.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p196/r3.anchor: وقال العباس بن عبد المطلب: قال النبي عليه السلام

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p196/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p196/r4.speaker: ابن عمر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p196/r4.claim: Ibn Umar criticizes people who collapse on hearing Qur'an, saying genuine fear of God does not make the Companions fall down.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p196/r4.anchor: وقال ابن عمر: وقدر أي ساقطا من سماع القرآن فقال: إنا لنخشى الله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p196/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p196/r5.speaker: أسماء بنت أبي بكر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p196/r5.claim: Asma says the Prophet's Companions wept and shivered when hearing Qur'an; she sought protection from Satan against people who fainted.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p196/r5.anchor: وقالت أسماء بنت أبي بكر: كان أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم تدمع أعينهم وتقشعر جلودهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p196/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p196/r6.speaker: ابن سيرين
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p196/r6.claim: Ibn Sirin challenges those who faint at recitation to hear the whole Qur'an sitting against a wall and see whether they throw themselves down.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p196/r6.anchor: وقال ابن سيرين: بيننا وبين هؤلاء الذين بصرعون عند قراءة القرآن أن يجعل أحدهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p196/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p196/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p196/r7.claim: The demonstrative may point to the Book or to the paired qualities of shivering and softening, namely the effect of God's guidance.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p196/r7.anchor: والإشارة بذلك إلى الكتاب، أو إلى ذينك الوصفين من الاقشعرار واللين، أي أثر هدى الله

STUDYQURAN:39:intro/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:intro/r5.speaker: Other commentators
STUDYQURAN:39:intro/r5.claim: Others suggest verses 10 and 23 were also revealed during the Madinan period.
STUDYQURAN:39:intro/r5.anchor: Others suggest that vv. 10 and 23 were also revealed during the Madinan period

ALUSI-FULL:v24p38#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p38#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p38#2/r1.claim: When divine majesty knocks at the hearts of those who fear God, the Qur'an makes their skin tremble; longing and seeking then soften both skin and heart toward God's remembrance.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p38#2/r1.anchor: ربهم ) إذا قرعت صفات الجلال أبواب قلوبهم ( ثم تلين جلودهم وقلوبهم إلى ذكر الله ) بالشوق والطلب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p175/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p175/r8.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p175/r8.claim: After they later asked for hadith, the verse calling the Qurʾān the best speech was revealed; Ibn al-Jawzī says these requests were repeatedly directed back to the Qurʾān.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p175/r8.anchor: فقالوا يا رسول الله لو حدثتنا فأنزل الله تعالى ( الله نزل أحسن الحديث كتابا متشابها مثاني ) [ الزمر 23 ] كل ذلك يؤمرون بالقرآن

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p175/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p175/r9.speaker: عون بن عبد الله
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p175/r9.claim: When the Companions tired and asked for stories, the best-speech verse came; when they again wanted something between hadith and Qurʾān, the best-narratives verse came.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p175/r9.anchor: وقال عون بن عبد الله مل أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ملة فقالوا يا رسول الله حدثنا فأنزل الله عز وجل ( الله نزل أحسن الحديث كتابا متشابها مثاني ) [ الزمر 23 ]

RAZI-FULL:v26p232/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p232/r1.speaker: القائلون بحدوث القرآن
RAZI-FULL:v26p232/r1.claim: They argue that calling the Qur’an hadith makes it temporally originated: hadith is recent rather than ancient, and its letters and words arise successively.
RAZI-FULL:v26p232/r1.anchor: القائلون بحدوث القرآن احتجوا بهذه الآية من وجوه

RAZI-FULL:v26p232/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p232/r2.speaker: القائلون بحدوث القرآن
RAZI-FULL:v26p232/r2.claim: They argue that a revealed thing occupies a locus subject to another’s control, so the Qur’an must be originated.
RAZI-FULL:v26p232/r2.anchor: أنه تعالى وصفه بأنه نزله والمنزل يكون في محل تصرف الغير

RAZI-FULL:v26p232/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p232/r3.speaker: القائلون بحدوث القرآن
RAZI-FULL:v26p232/r3.claim: They infer that the superlative “best discourse” puts the Qur’an in the same genus as other discourse; since other speech is originated, so is it.
RAZI-FULL:v26p232/r3.anchor: قوله أحسن الحديث يقتضي أن يكون هو من جنس سائر الأحاديث

RAZI-FULL:v26p232/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p232/r4.speaker: القائلون بحدوث القرآن
RAZI-FULL:v26p232/r4.claim: They argue that kitab derives from gathering, implying a collected object subject to an agent’s disposal and therefore originated.
RAZI-FULL:v26p232/r4.anchor: وصفه بكونه كتابا والكتاب مشتق من الكتبة وهي الاجتماع

RAZI-FULL:v26p232/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p232/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p232/r5.claim: Razi limits the argument to discourse composed of letters, sounds, words, and expressions, which he regards as created.
RAZI-FULL:v26p232/r5.anchor: نحمل هذا الدليل على الكلام المؤلف من الحروف والأصوات

RAZI-FULL:v26p232/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p232/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p232/r6.claim: Razi divides the Qur’an’s excellence into two possible grounds: its wording and its meaning.
RAZI-FULL:v26p232/r6.anchor: الحديث بحسب لفظه أو بحسب معناه

RAZI-FULL:v26p233/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p233/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p233/r1.claim: The Qur’an’s verbal excellence includes its eloquence and forcefulness.
RAZI-FULL:v26p233/r1.anchor: أن يكون ذلك الحسن لأجل الفصاحة والجزالة

RAZI-FULL:v26p233/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p233/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p233/r2.claim: Its style is a distinct genre, unlike poetry, sermons, or letters, yet every sound nature finds it pleasant and delightful.

RAZI-FULL:v26p233/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p233/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p233/r3.claim: Its meanings are excellent because it is free of contradiction; a book without contradiction is miraculous, as 4:82 argues.

RAZI-FULL:v26p233/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p233/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p233/r4.claim: Another aspect of its excellence is its extensive disclosure of unseen matters about the past and future.
RAZI-FULL:v26p233/r4.anchor: اشتماله على الغيوب الكثيرة في الماضي والمستقبل

RAZI-FULL:v26p233/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p233/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p233/r5.claim: The Qur’an contains a vast range of beneficial sciences, which Razi organizes through the creed and confession in 2:285.
RAZI-FULL:v26p233/r5.anchor: العلوم النافعة هي ما ذكره الله في كتابه

RAZI-FULL:v26p233/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p233/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p233/r6.claim: Knowledge of God’s essence includes knowing that God exists, is beginningless, and endures forever.
RAZI-FULL:v26p233/r6.anchor: معرفة الذات فهي أن يعلم وجود الله وقدمه وبقاءه

RAZI-FULL:v26p233/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p233/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p233/r7.claim: God must be transcendent above being a substance, composite of parts, or confined to a place or direction; four Qur’anic negators express this transcendence.
RAZI-FULL:v26p233/r7.anchor: وهو كونه جوهرا ومركبا من الأعضاء والأجزاء

RAZI-FULL:v26p234/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p234/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p234/r1.claim: The Qur’an teaches God’s positive attributes, including creative power, omniscience, life, will, hearing and sight, speech, command, mercy, and sovereignty.
RAZI-FULL:v26p234/r1.anchor: فأولها العلم بالله ، والعلم بكونه محدثا خالقا

RAZI-FULL:v26p234#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p234#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p234#2/r1.claim: Divine acts concern spirits, which few can know, and bodies, divided into the higher and lower worlds.
RAZI-FULL:v26p234#2/r1.anchor: فاعلم أن الأفعال إما أرواح وإما أجسام

RAZI-FULL:v26p234#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p234#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p234#2/r2.claim: Among the higher-world sciences are the heavens, sun and moon, lights, shadows, day and night, stars, Paradise, Hell, the Throne, the Kursi, the Preserved Tablet, and the Pen.

RAZI-FULL:v26p234#3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p234#3/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p234#3/r1.claim: The Qur’an describes Earth as a cradle, bed, receptacle for living and dead, subdued, and spread out for travel.

RAZI-FULL:v26p234#3/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p234#3/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p234#3/r2.claim: Its lower-world sciences include the sea, air and winds, thunder, lightning, rain, clouds, plants and fruits, and animals.
RAZI-FULL:v26p234#3/r2.anchor: ومن هذا الباب ذكر الصواعق والأمطار وتراكم السحاب

RAZI-FULL:v26p234#3/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p234#3/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p234#3/r3.claim: It discusses human origins and the marvels of hearing, sight, speech, intellect, and understanding.
RAZI-FULL:v26p234#3/r3.anchor: عجائب تكوين الإنسان في أول الخلقة

RAZI-FULL:v26p234#3/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p234#3/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p234#3/r4.claim: It relates prophets, kings, and human history from creation through Judgment, then death, resurrection, and the states of the blessed and wretched.
RAZI-FULL:v26p234#3/r4.anchor: تواريخ الأنبياء والملوك وأحوال الناس من أول خلق العالم إلى آخر قيام القيامة

RAZI-FULL:v26p234#3/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p234#3/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p234#3/r5.claim: Razi concludes that the Qur’an contains ten sciences of the heavens and ten of the elemental world, all elevated fields of knowledge.
RAZI-FULL:v26p234#3/r5.anchor: فقد أشرنا إلى عشرة أنواع من العلوم

RAZI-FULL:v26p235/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p235/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p235/r1.claim: The Qur’an covers moral training, distinguishing virtues from vices, including justice, beneficence, giving to kin, and rejecting indecency, wrong, and aggression.
RAZI-FULL:v26p235/r1.anchor: فهو المسمى بعلم الأخلاق وبيان تمييز الأخلاق

RAZI-FULL:v26p235/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p235/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p235/r2.claim: The Qur’an contains the foundations of jurisprudence in the most complete form.
RAZI-FULL:v26p235/r2.anchor: وهو المسمى بعلم الفقه والقرآن مشتمل على جملة أصول هذا العلم على أكمل الوجوه

RAZI-FULL:v26p235/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p235/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p235/r3.claim: Knowledge of God’s beautiful names is another branch of knowledge about God.

RAZI-FULL:v26p235/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p235/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p235/r4.claim: The Qur’an treats angels both summarily and in detail: as messengers and cosmic administrators, ranks of worshippers, Throne-bearers and attendants, keepers of Hell, recorders, and protecting angels.
RAZI-FULL:v26p235/r4.anchor: والقرآن يشتمل على شرح صفاتهم تارة على سبيل الإجمال وأخرى على طريق التفصيل

RAZI-FULL:v26p235/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p235/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p235/r5.claim: The discussion of angels can also extend to jinn and devils.
RAZI-FULL:v26p235/r5.anchor: وقد يتصل بأحوال الملائكة أحوال الجن والشياطين

RAZI-FULL:v26p236/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p236/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p236/r1.claim: The Qur’an discusses earlier scriptures, including Adam’s words and Abraham’s trial, as well as the Torah, Gospel, and Psalms.
RAZI-FULL:v26p236/r1.anchor: شرح أحوال كتاب آدم عليه السلام

RAZI-FULL:v26p236/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p236/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p236/r2.claim: It names some messengers and leaves others unnamed, as 40:78 says.
RAZI-FULL:v26p236/r2.anchor: منهم من قصصنا عليك ومنهم من لم نقصص عليك

RAZI-FULL:v26p236/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p236/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p236/r3.claim: The faithful accept that religious duties bind them, expressed in their words, “We hear and obey.”
RAZI-FULL:v26p236/r3.anchor: أن يقروا بوجوب هذه التكاليف عليهم

RAZI-FULL:v26p236/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p236/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p236/r4.claim: As disclosure of divine majesty deepens, worshippers see their shortcomings more clearly and ask forgiveness more often.
RAZI-FULL:v26p236/r4.anchor: كانت المكاشفات في تقصير العبودية أكثر

RAZI-FULL:v26p236/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p236/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p236/r5.claim: Belief in the return to God, resurrection, and Judgment is another essential body of religious knowledge.
RAZI-FULL:v26p236/r5.anchor: معرفة المعاد والبعث والقيامة وهو المراد

RAZI-FULL:v26p236/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p236/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p236/r6.claim: The Qur’an is an inexhaustible sea of essential religious teachings; no other book contains this full range, and Razi’s own commentary captures only a drop.
RAZI-FULL:v26p236/r6.anchor: القرآن بحر لا نهاية له في تقرير هذه المطالب وتعريفها وشرحها

RAZI-FULL:v26p236#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p236#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p236#2/r1.claim: Razi directs readers to his earlier explanation of “the Book” at 2:2.

RAZI-FULL:v26p236#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p236#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v26p236#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas explains that the whole Qur’an is mutashabih because its parts resemble one another.

RAZI-FULL:v26p236#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p236#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p236#2/r3.claim: Unlike long books that vary in eloquence, every part of the Qur’an is fully eloquent.
RAZI-FULL:v26p236#2/r3.anchor: والقرآن يخالف ذلك فإنه فصيح كامل الفصاحة بجميع أجزائه

RAZI-FULL:v26p236#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p236#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p236#2/r4.claim: Repeated accounts, such as the story of Moses, remain equally eloquent throughout the Qur’an.
RAZI-FULL:v26p236#2/r4.anchor: حكى قصة موسى عليه السلام في مواضع كثيرة من القرآن وكلها متساوية متشابهة في الفصاحة

RAZI-FULL:v26p236#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p236#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p236#2/r5.claim: Its signs and explanations reinforce and confirm one another.
RAZI-FULL:v26p236#2/r5.anchor: كل ما فيه من الآيات والبيانات فإنه يقوي بعضها بعضا ويؤكد بعضها بعضا

RAZI-FULL:v26p236#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p236#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p236#2/r6.claim: Its many sciences share one purpose: calling people to religion and establishing God’s majesty, including in every narrative.
RAZI-FULL:v26p236#2/r6.anchor: متشابهة متشاركة في أن المقصود منها بأسرها الدعوة

RAZI-FULL:v26p236#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p236#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p236#2/r7.claim: Mathani points to paired patterns throughout the Qur’an: command and prohibition, general and particular, concise and expanded, heaven and earth, Paradise and Hell, darkness and light, and many other pairs.
RAZI-FULL:v26p236#2/r7.anchor: أكثر الأشياء المذكورة وقعت زوجين زوجين

RAZI-FULL:v26p236#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p236#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p236#2/r8.claim: These pairs show that all things besides the Real are subject to an opposite; only God is the one, unique, and absolute.
RAZI-FULL:v26p236#2/r8.anchor: كل ما سوى الحق زوج ويدل على أن كل شيء مبتلى بضده ونقيضه وأن الفرد الأحد الحق هو الله سبحانه

RAZI-FULL:v26p237/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p237/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p237/r1.claim: Qashʿirīrah is a shiver-like change in the skin caused by awe and fear.
RAZI-FULL:v26p237/r1.anchor: تأخذهم قشعريرة وهي تغير يحدث في جلد الإنسان

RAZI-FULL:v26p237/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p237/r2.speaker: المفسرون
RAZI-FULL:v26p237/r2.claim: The commentators say that hearing verses of mercy and beneficence brings joy and softens hearts toward God’s remembrance.
RAZI-FULL:v26p237/r2.anchor: والمعنى أنهم عند سماع آيات الرحمة والإحسان يحصل لهم الفرح

RAZI-FULL:v26p237/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p237/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p237/r3.claim: The knowers say that seekers at the beginning of reverence are overwhelmed by contemplating divine majesty but revived by glimpsing divine beauty.

RAZI-FULL:v26p237/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p237/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p237/r4.claim: Reflecting on proofs that God is beyond location and direction can make the skin shiver because conceiving a being neither inside nor outside, connected nor separate from the world is difficult.
RAZI-FULL:v26p237/r4.anchor: الدلائل الدالة على أنه يجب تنزيه الله

RAZI-FULL:v26p237/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p237/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p237/r5.claim: Contemplating God’s oneness and the divisibility of every spatial thing softens skin and heart toward remembrance.
RAZI-FULL:v26p237/r5.anchor: أنه يجب أن يكون فردا أحدا

RAZI-FULL:v26p237/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p237/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p237/r6.claim: The mind’s attempt to imagine pre-eternity fails because anything it pictures is finite; recognizing this limit produces bewilderment and a shiver.
RAZI-FULL:v26p237/r6.anchor: كل ما استحضرته في فهو متناه والأزل هو الوجود المتقدم على هذه المدة المتناهية

RAZI-FULL:v26p237/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p237/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p237/r7.claim: Reasoning from necessary and possible existence lets the mind apprehend God as beginningless and endless, bringing calm and softness toward remembrance.
RAZI-FULL:v26p237/r7.anchor: ههنا موجود والموجود إما واجب وإما ممكن

RAZI-FULL:v26p237/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p237/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p237/r8.claim: These states are not confined to hearing punishment and mercy verses; that is only an initial level, with unbounded further degrees.
RAZI-FULL:v26p237/r8.anchor: بل ذاك أول تلك المراتب وبعده مراتب لا حد لها

RAZI-FULL:v26p237#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p237#2/r1.speaker: قتادة
RAZI-FULL:v26p237#2/r1.claim: Qatada says the Qur’an portrays God’s friends shivering or softening during unveilings, without loss of reason or bodily convulsions; such disturbance would be satanic.
RAZI-FULL:v26p237#2/r1.anchor: عن قتادة أنه قال : القرآن دل على أن أولياء

RAZI-FULL:v26p237#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p237#2/r2.speaker: أبو حامد الغزالي
RAZI-FULL:v26p237#2/r2.claim: In the Ihya, al-Ghazali asks why many people show ecstasy at poems about union and separation but not when hearing Qur’anic verses; he offers several excuses.
RAZI-FULL:v26p237#2/r2.anchor: الشيخ أبا حامد الغزالي أورد مسألة في كتاب

RAZI-FULL:v26p237#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p237#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p237#2/r3.claim: Razi says Qur’anic mysteries make his skin shiver, hair stand, and heart feel awe, while love poems make him frivolous; he considers this the sound path.
RAZI-FULL:v26p237#2/r3.anchor: كلما تأملت في أسرار القرآن اقشعر جلدي وقف على شعري

RAZI-FULL:v26p237#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p237#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p237#2/r4.claim: Love poems describe union, estrangement, hatred, and love appropriate to creatures; attributing these literally to God is unbelief, and only learned scholars can translate them into meanings fitting divine majesty.
RAZI-FULL:v26p237#2/r4.anchor: كلمات مشتملة على وصل وهجر وبغض وحب تليق بالخلق

RAZI-FULL:v26p237#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p237#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p237#2/r5.claim: The speaker’s identity affects a text: the Qur’an is spoken by God through Gabriel and the infallible Messenger, while the poet is a lying, lustful advocate of immorality.
RAZI-FULL:v26p237#2/r5.anchor: القائل في القرآن هنا هو الله بواسطة جبريل بتبليغ الرسول المعصوم

RAZI-FULL:v26p237#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p237#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p237#2/r6.claim: The Qur’an calls to truth and the straight path, whereas poetry follows falsehood and wandering, as 42:52–53 and 26:224–226 show.
RAZI-FULL:v26p237#2/r6.anchor: مدار القرآن على الدعوة إلى الحق

RAZI-FULL:v26p238/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p238/r1.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
RAZI-FULL:v26p238/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhshari derives qashʿirīrah from qashʿ, a dried hide, plus an added r to make a quadriliteral; the idiom means skin contracts and hair stands from extreme fear.
RAZI-FULL:v26p238/r1.anchor: تركيبه من حروف التقشع وهو الأديم اليابس

RAZI-FULL:v26p238/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p238/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p238/r2.claim: The phrase means that skin and hearts soften as they arrive at God’s presence, a presence not perceived by sensory faculties.
RAZI-FULL:v26p238/r2.anchor: التقدير تلين جلودهم وقلوبهم حال وصولها إلى حضرة الله وهو لا يحس بالإدراك

RAZI-FULL:v26p238/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p238/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p238/r3.claim: The wording says remembrance of God rather than remembrance of mercy because the highest lover loves God for God’s own sake, not for a benefit distinct from Him.
RAZI-FULL:v26p238/r3.anchor: من أحب الله لأجل رحمته فهو ما أحب الله

RAZI-FULL:v26p238/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p238/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p238/r4.claim: The verse mentions only skin shivering in fear but both skin and heart softening in hope because disclosure is fuller in hope: good is intrinsically sought, evil only incidentally, and disclosure occurs in hearts and spirits.
RAZI-FULL:v26p238/r4.anchor: المكاشفة في مقام الرجاء أكمل منها في مقام الخوف

RAZI-FULL:v26p238/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p238/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p238/r5.claim: “That” refers to the Book: it is God’s guidance, by which He guides the servant whose chest He first opened to receive it.
RAZI-FULL:v26p238/r5.anchor: إشارة إلى الكتاب وهو هدى الله يهدي به من يشاء

RAZI-FULL:v26p238/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p238/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p238/r6.claim: God’s misled person has a hardened, dark, dull heart incompatible with guidance and therefore has no guide.
RAZI-FULL:v26p238/r6.anchor: من جعل قلبه قاسيا مظلما بليد الفهم منافيا لقبول هذه الهداية

RAZI-FULL:v26p238/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p238/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p238/r7.claim: Razi says his school’s proof here, and the Muʿtazilite objections and replies, are the same as those discussed at 6:125.
RAZI-FULL:v26p238/r7.anchor: استدلال أصحابنا بهذه الآية وسؤالات المعتزلة وجوابات أصحابنا عين ما تقدم

STUDYQURAN:39:23/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:23/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:39:23/r1.claim: The most beautiful discourse is the Quran, beautiful in both meaning and expression; its consimilar and paired verses display that beauty.
STUDYQURAN:39:23/r1.anchor: The most beautiful discourse refers to the Quran (Bḍ, IK, Q), which is considered most beautiful in both meaning and expression

STUDYQURAN:39:23/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:23/r2.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:39:23/r2.claim: One reading of consimilar is that each part of the Quran is as eloquent as every other part.
STUDYQURAN:39:23/r2.anchor: each part is as eloquent as the next (R)

STUDYQURAN:39:23/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:23/r3.speaker: IK, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:39:23/r3.claim: Another reading is that many Quranic parts resemble one another through recurring phrases.

STUDYQURAN:39:23/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:23/r4.speaker: Q
STUDYQURAN:39:23/r4.claim: Consimilarity may mean that qualities such as beauty and wisdom recur throughout the Quran.
STUDYQURAN:39:23/r4.anchor: particular qualities such as beauty and wisdom (Q)

STUDYQURAN:39:23/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:23/r5.speaker: Bḍ
STUDYQURAN:39:23/r5.claim: Consimilarity may mean that truth and inimitability are found throughout the Quran.
STUDYQURAN:39:23/r5.anchor: truth and inimitability (Bḍ) are found throughout

STUDYQURAN:39:23/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:23/r6.speaker: Q
STUDYQURAN:39:23/r6.claim: A further explanation is that each part confirms the other parts.
STUDYQURAN:39:23/r6.anchor: each part confirms the other parts (Q)

STUDYQURAN:39:23/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:23/r7.speaker: IK
STUDYQURAN:39:23/r7.claim: Mutashābih also describes some Quranic verses in 3:7, where it carries a distinct technical meaning.
STUDYQURAN:39:23/r7.anchor: used to describe some verses of the Quran in 3:7, but with a very different, more technical meaning of the word (IK)

STUDYQURAN:39:23/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:23/r8.speaker: IK
STUDYQURAN:39:23/r8.claim: Paired refers to Quranic juxtapositions of opposites, such as Heaven and Hell, believers and disbelievers, and reward and punishment.
STUDYQURAN:39:23/r8.anchor: many opposites are juxtaposed in the Quran, such as Heaven and Hell

STUDYQURAN:39:23/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:23/r9.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:39:23/r9.claim: The paired contrast is illustrated by skin quivering in fear of divine might and punishment, then skin and hearts softening in hope of mercy and forgiveness.
STUDYQURAN:39:23/r9.anchor: skin that quivers out of fear of God’s Might and Punishment and the skins and hearts that soften

STUDYQURAN:39:23/r10.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:23/r10.speaker: Aj
STUDYQURAN:39:23/r10.claim: The Quran’s power to make skins quiver and then soften with hearts is another attribute of its beauty.
STUDYQURAN:39:23/r10.anchor: That the Quran makes skins quiver and then soften along with hearts is another attribute that makes it most beautiful (Aj)

STUDYQURAN:39:23/r11.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:23/r11.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:39:23/r11.claim: Other verses mention hearts responding to Quran recitation or God’s mention, but this is the only verse that describes skins quivering and softening.
STUDYQURAN:39:23/r11.anchor: this is the only verse to mention those whose skins quiver and soften unto the remembrance of God

STUDYQURAN:39:23/r12.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:23/r12.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:39:23/r12.claim: Some commentators identify the people described as the Prophet’s Companions, whose eyes watered and skins quivered when the Quran was recited.
STUDYQURAN:39:23/r12.anchor: According to some commentators, this is a description of the Companions of the Prophet

STUDYQURAN:39:23/r13.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:23/r13.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:39:23/r13.claim: In the Companions interpretation, remembrance can mean the Quran as Reminder, one of its names being al-Dhikr.
STUDYQURAN:39:23/r13.anchor: remembrance is often understood to mean “Reminder,” as a reference to the Quran

STUDYQURAN:39:23/r14.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:23/r14.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:39:23/r14.claim: The translation takes remembrance as remembrance of God, as in the verse describing believing hearts at peace in God’s remembrance.
STUDYQURAN:39:23/r14.anchor: as translated here, it is understood as a reference to the remembrance of God referred to in such verses as 13:28

STUDYQURAN:39:23/r15.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:23/r15.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:39:23/r15.claim: Another possible sense is that when God remembers a person, that person’s heart necessarily softens.
STUDYQURAN:39:23/r15.anchor: when God remembers a person, that person’s heart cannot but soften

STUDYQURAN:39:23/r16.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:23/r16.speaker: Q
STUDYQURAN:39:23/r16.claim: That is God’s Guidance can refer to the Quran described in the verse.
STUDYQURAN:39:23/r16.anchor: That is God’s Guidance refers to the Quran as described in this verse (Q)

STUDYQURAN:39:23/r17.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:23/r17.speaker: Q
STUDYQURAN:39:23/r17.claim: Alternatively, it can refer to the fear of God’s punishment and hope for His reward that He grants.
STUDYQURAN:39:23/r17.anchor: what God has granted by way of fear of His Punishment and hope for His Reward (Q)

STUDYQURAN:39:23/r18.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:23/r18.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:39:23/r18.claim: The Quran repeatedly says the astray have no way, guide, or protector; here this means one whose skin and heart do not soften has no guidance.

BURSEVI:v8p72#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p72#3/r1.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v8p72#3/r1.claim: Some say Islam is the greatest blessing, Satan its enemy; preserve it and other blessings, guarding against forgetfulness, hard-heartedness, and ingratitude.
BURSEVI:v8p72#3/r1.anchor: قال بعضهم : وأجل النعم على العبد نعمة الإسلام وعدوها إبليس ، فاحفظ هذه النعمة وسائر النعم واحذر من النسيان والقسوة والكفران

BURSEVI:v8p72#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p72#3/r2.speaker: الحسين النوري
BURSEVI:v8p72#3/r2.claim: Al-Nuri says hardness of heart amid blessings is worse than in hardship: blessing induces complacency, while hardship recalls God.
BURSEVI:v8p72#3/r2.anchor: قال الحسين النوري رحمه الله : قسوة القلب بالنعم أشد من قسوته بالشدة ، فإنه بالنعمة يسكن وبالشدة يذكر

BURSEVI:v8p72#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p72#3/r3.speaker: الحسين النوري
BURSEVI:v8p72#3/r3.claim: Al-Nuri warns that indulging in a permitted thing for pleasure wastes life, hardens the heart, and prevents attaining the ranks of the open-hearted.
BURSEVI:v8p72#3/r3.anchor: وقال : من هم بشيء مما أباحه العلم تلذذا عوقت بتضييع العمر وقسوة القلب

BURSEVI:v8p72#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p72#3/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p72#3/r4.claim: The Quran's beauty, order, and meanings are inexhaustible; it surpasses all earlier prophetic revelations in completeness and firmness.
BURSEVI:v8p72#3/r4.anchor: هو القرآن الكريم الذي لا نهاية لحسنه ولا غاية لجمال نظمه وملاحة معانيه ، وهو أحسن مما نزل على جميع الأنبياء والمرسلين وأكمله وأكثره إحكاما

BURSEVI:v8p72#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p72#3/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p72#3/r5.claim: The Quran is the best speech also because of its eloquence and inimitability.

BURSEVI:v8p72#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p72#3/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p72#3/r6.claim: It is best because it is God's eternal speech, whereas the speech of others is created and originated.
BURSEVI:v8p72#3/r6.anchor: وأيضا : لأنه كلام الله ، وهو قديم وكلام غيره مخلوق محدث

BURSEVI:v8p72#3/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p72#3/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p72#3/r7.claim: The Quran is best speech because it is wholly true.
BURSEVI:v8p72#3/r7.anchor: وأيضا : لكونه صدقا كله إلى غير ذلك

BURSEVI:v8p72#3/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p72#3/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p72#3/r8.claim: It is called hadith because the Prophet told it to his people as revelation came; the common term means report or speech and does not imply that the Quran is originated.
BURSEVI:v8p72#3/r8.anchor: سمي حديثا ؛ لأن النبي عليه السلام كان يحدث به قومه ويخبرهم بما ينزل عليه منه ، فلا يدل على حدوث القرآن

BURSEVI:v8p72#3/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p72#3/r9.speaker: الراغب
BURSEVI:v8p72#3/r9.claim: Al-Raghib defines hadith as any speech a person receives by hearing or revelation, while awake or asleep.
BURSEVI:v8p72#3/r9.anchor: قال في "المفردات" كل كلام يبلغ الإنسان من جهة السمع

BURSEVI:v8p72#3/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p72#3/r10.speaker: أصحاب رسول الله
BURSEVI:v8p72#3/r10.claim: The Companions wearied and asked the Prophet to tell them something; the verse was then revealed.
BURSEVI:v8p72#3/r10.anchor: روي أن أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ملوا ملة ، فقالوا له عليه السلام : حدثنا حديثا

BURSEVI:v8p72#3/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p72#3/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p72#3/r11.claim: The Quran offers ample sufficiency in place of other narratives.
BURSEVI:v8p72#3/r11.anchor: والمعنى : أن فيه مندوحة عن سائر الأحاديث

BURSEVI:v8p73/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p73/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p73/r1.claim: كتابا is an appositive explaining أحسن الحديث.

BURSEVI:v8p73/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p73/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p73/r2.claim: The Quran's contents agree in soundness, rulings, truth, and benefit in both lives; its eloquent words and inimitable structure also correspond.
BURSEVI:v8p73/r2.anchor: معانيه في الصحة والأحكام والابتناء على الحق والصدق واستتباع منافع الخلق في المعاد والمعاش

BURSEVI:v8p73/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p73/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p73/r3.claim: مثاني is another adjective for the singular كتاب, pluralized in view of the book's parts, as one speaks of Quranic suras and verses or human veins and bones.

BURSEVI:v8p73/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p73/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p73/r4.claim: On one derivation مثاني means repeated: the Quran repeats its stories, reports, rulings, commands, prohibitions, promises, threats, and exhortations.
BURSEVI:v8p73/r4.anchor: بمعنى مردد ومكرر لما ثنى من قصصه وأنبائه وأحكامه وأوامره ونواهيه ووعده ووعيده ومواعظه

BURSEVI:v8p73/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p73/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p73/r5.claim: It may mean that recitation is repeated without becoming tiresome: its freshness and pleasure remain unlike created speech.
BURSEVI:v8p73/r5.anchor: أو لأنه ثنى في التلاوة ، فلا يمل كما جاء في نعته لا يخلق على كثرة الترداد

BURSEVI:v8p73/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p73/r6.speaker: القصيدة البردية
BURSEVI:v8p73/r6.claim: The Burda poem says the Quran's wonders cannot be counted and frequent recitation never makes it tiresome.
BURSEVI:v8p73/r6.anchor: فلا تعد ولا تحصى عجائبها ولا تسام على الإكثار بالسأم

BURSEVI:v8p73/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p73/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p73/r7.claim: Al-Mufradat explains that suras are called mathani because they recur over time and do not fade away like other things, though paper wears out.
BURSEVI:v8p73/r7.anchor: وفي "المفردات" وسمي سور القرآن مثاني ؛ لأنها تثنى على مرور الأيام وتكرر

BURSEVI:v8p73/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p73/r8.speaker: عثمان
BURSEVI:v8p73/r8.claim: The author cites a report that Uthman burned two mushafs because of how frequently he read them.
BURSEVI:v8p73/r8.anchor: كما روي أن عثمان رضي الله عنه حرق مصحفين لكثرة قراءته فيهما

BURSEVI:v8p73/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p73/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p73/r9.claim: It can be called mathani because its benefits renew continually, and its wonders never run out.
BURSEVI:v8p73/r9.anchor: ويصح أن يقال للقرآن : مثاني لما يثنى ويتجدد حالا فحالا من فوائده

BURSEVI:v8p73/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p73/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p73/r10.claim: Another derivation makes mathani praise: the Quran continually gives grounds for praise, as reflected in its descriptions as noble and glorious.
BURSEVI:v8p73/r10.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون ذلك من الثناء تنبيها على أنه أبدا يظهر منه ما يدعو إلى الثناء عليه

BURSEVI:v8p73/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p73/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p73/r11.claim: Mathani may also derive from repetition or return, as in a gaze returned twice, meaning one turn after another.
BURSEVI:v8p73/r11.anchor: كما في قوله تعالى : {ثم ارجع البصر كرتين}

BURSEVI:v8p73/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p73/r12.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v8p73/r12.claim: Some derive it as something praised for eloquence and inimitability, so that a listener might say one should prostrate for its eloquence.
BURSEVI:v8p73/r12.anchor: حتى قال بعضهم لبعض : ألا سجدت لفصاحته

BURSEVI:v8p73/r13.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p73/r13.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p73/r13.claim: With the final n pronounced kasra, مثني عليه means praised for the attributes worthy of it.

BURSEVI:v8p74/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p74/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p74/r1.claim: This clause resumes by describing the Quran's visible effects on listeners after its qualities and status as the best speech were explained.
BURSEVI:v8p74/r1.anchor: {تقشعر منه جلود الذين يخشون ربهم} ، استئناف مسوق

BURSEVI:v8p74/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p74/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p74/r2.claim: The lexicons explain اقشعر as a shiver or tremor; the skin is the body's outer covering, and the root suggests trembling or strong contraction from sudden fear.

BURSEVI:v8p74/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p74/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p74/r3.claim: Al-Irshad describes the skin as contracting intensely and says the form adds an intensified sense of sudden fear that raises the hair.
BURSEVI:v8p74/r3.anchor: وفي "الإرشاد" : الاقشعرار التقبض يقال : اقشعر الجلد إذا تقبض تقبضا شديدا

BURSEVI:v8p74/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p74/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p74/r4.claim: The phrase may depict extreme fear figuratively or report an actual bodily state; Bursevi prefers the literal reading because fear's bodily effect is directly felt.
BURSEVI:v8p74/r4.anchor: والمراد : إما بيان إفراط خشيتهم بطريق التمثيل والتصوير أو بيان حصول تلك الحالة وعروضها لهم بطريق التحقيق

BURSEVI:v8p74/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p74/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p74/r5.claim: When they hear the Quran's threatening verses, awe and fear make their skins shiver and bristle.
BURSEVI:v8p74/r5.anchor: إذا سمعوا بالقرآن وقوارع آيات وعيده أصابتهم هيبة وخشية تقشعر منها جلودهم

BURSEVI:v8p74#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p74#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p74#2/r1.claim: Softness, opposite of roughness, is literal for bodies and metaphorical for character; skins signify bodies and hearts signify souls, which soften upon recalling God's mercy and forgiveness as fear becomes hope.
BURSEVI:v8p74#2/r1.anchor: والجلود عبارة عن الأبدان والقلوب عن النفوس كما في "المفردات" ؛ أي : ثم إذا ذكروا رحمة الله

BURSEVI:v8p74#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p74#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p74#2/r2.claim: The verb is followed by إلى because softness includes the sense of settling and becoming tranquil toward God's remembrance, in a hopeful and uncontracted state.
BURSEVI:v8p74#2/r2.anchor: وتعدية اللين بإلى لتضمنه معنى السكون والاطمئنان ؛ كأنه قيل : تسكن وتطمئن إلى ذكر الله

BURSEVI:v8p74#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p74#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p74#2/r3.claim: The verse says God's remembrance without naming mercy because mercy is the first thing that comes to mind when He is remembered.
BURSEVI:v8p74#2/r3.anchor: وإنما أطلق ذكر الله ولم يصرح بالرحمة إيذانا بأنها أول ما يخطر بالبال عند ذكره تعالى

BURSEVI:v8p74#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p74#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p74#2/r4.claim: Skin is named first because fear first affects the heart: warning makes skins bristle and hearts fear, then hope replaces fear in the heart and softens the skin.
BURSEVI:v8p74#2/r4.anchor: لتقدم الخشية التي هي من عوارض القلوب ، فكأنه قيل : تقشعر جلودهم من آيات الوعيد

BURSEVI:v8p74#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p74#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p74#2/r5.claim: The two clauses signify fear and hope, contraction and expansion, awe and intimacy, or manifestation and concealment.
BURSEVI:v8p74#2/r5.anchor: فالجملتان إشارة إلى الخوف والرجاء أو القبض والبسط أو الهيبة والأنس

BURSEVI:v8p74#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p74#2/r6.speaker: النهرجوري
BURSEVI:v8p74#2/r6.claim: Al-Nahrjurī says the verse describes the audition of seekers and knowers: the seekers manifest a state, while knowers attain calm; shivering marks beginners and softness the advanced.
BURSEVI:v8p74#2/r6.anchor: قال النهرجوري رحمه الله : وصف الله بهذه الآية سماع المريدين وسماع العارفين

BURSEVI:v8p74#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p74#2/r7.speaker: أم الدرداء
BURSEVI:v8p74#2/r7.claim: Shahr ibn Hawshab reports Umm al-Darda saying that heart-fear resembles a burning palm frond; when gooseflesh appears, pray, for the heart is drawn to the sacred realm and intimacy, and prayer then is answered.
BURSEVI:v8p74#2/r7.anchor: وعن شهر بن حوشب قالت أم الدرداء : رضي الله عنها : إنما الوجل في قلب الرجل

BURSEVI:v8p74#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p74#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p74#3/r1.claim: The book just described is God's guidance; He guides believing, God-fearing people who reflect on its hidden signs and proofs of its divine origin, as in 2:2.

BURSEVI:v8p74#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p74#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p74#3/r2.claim: God causes misguidance by creating it in a person who turns from guidance and remains unaffected by warning or promise; no guide can rescue that person from error.
BURSEVI:v8p74#3/r2.anchor: أي : يخلق فيه الضلالة لصرف قدرته إلى مباديها

BURSEVI:v8p74#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p74#3/r3.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v8p74#3/r3.claim: Al-Ta'wilat al-Najmiyya says God misguides one by leaving him to himself and his intellect and depriving him of faith in, and following, the prophets.
BURSEVI:v8p74#3/r3.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" : {ومن يضلل الله} بأن يكله إلى نفسه وعقله

BURSEVI:v8p74#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p74#3/r4.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v8p74#3/r4.claim: Al-Ta'wilat al-Najmiyya says no guide from philosophers' proofs or rational arguments can guide such a person.

BURSEVI:v8p74#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p74#3/r5.speaker: أحد الصحابة
BURSEVI:v8p74#3/r5.claim: A Companion asks why believers' faces redden when hearing Quran while hypocrites' faces blacken; the answer is that Quran lights believers and burns hypocrites.
BURSEVI:v8p74#3/r5.anchor: (يكى ازصحابه روزى بآن مهتر عالم عليه السلام كفت يا رسول الله جرا رخساره ما در استماع قرآن

BURSEVI:v8p74#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p74#3/r6.speaker: المولى الجامي
BURSEVI:v8p74#3/r6.claim: Al-Jami counsels that whoever seeks the Kaaba of realization should not wander the path without a guide.
BURSEVI:v8p74#3/r6.anchor: قال المولى الجامي قدس سره : خواهى بصوب كعبه تحقيق ره برى

BURSEVI:v8p74#3/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p74#3/r7.speaker: الخجندي
BURSEVI:v8p74#3/r7.claim: Al-Khujandi's verse contrasts hearts that receive Quran continually with false people who tire of God's speech.

BURSEVI:v8p74#3/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p74#3/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p74#3/r8.claim: Repeated Quranic admonition softens resistant souls, which naturally recoil from counsel; the Prophet repeated his exhortations three or seven times.
BURSEVI:v8p74#3/r8.anchor: لأن النفوس أنفر شيء من حديث الوعظ والنصيحة وأكثر جمودا وإباء عنه

BURSEVI:v8p74#3/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p74#3/r9.speaker: النبي
BURSEVI:v8p74#3/r9.claim: A report from the Prophet says that when a servant's skin shivers from fear of God, his sins fall away like leaves from a dry tree.
BURSEVI:v8p74#3/r9.anchor: قال عليه السلام : "إذا اقشعر جلد العبد من خشية الله تحاتت عنه ذنوبه"

BURSEVI:v8p74#3/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p74#3/r10.speaker: النبي
BURSEVI:v8p74#3/r10.claim: Another report from the Prophet says God forbids the Fire to a servant whose skin shivers from fear of Him.
BURSEVI:v8p74#3/r10.anchor: وعنه عليه السلام : "إذا اقشعر جلد العبد من خشية الله حرمه الله على النار"

BURSEVI:v8p74#3/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p74#3/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p74#3/r11.claim: When God made Abraham His intimate friend, He placed such fear in his heart that its beating could be heard from afar, like a bird's flutter in the air.
BURSEVI:v8p74#3/r11.anchor: ولما اتخذ الله إبراهيم خليلا ألقى في قلبه الوجل حتى إن خفقان قلبه يسمع من بعيد

TAB-FULL:v20p190#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p190#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p190#2/r1.claim: The best discourse God sent down is the Quran.

TAB-FULL:v20p190#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p190#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p190#2/r2.claim: The Quran's parts resemble one another, with no disagreement or contradiction.
TAB-FULL:v20p190#2/r2.anchor: يشبه بعضه بعضا، لا اختلاف فيه، ولا تضاد

TAB-FULL:v20p190#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p190#2/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v20p190#2/r3.claim: Qatada says each verse resembles another verse and each letter resembles another letter.
TAB-FULL:v20p190#2/r3.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {الله نزل أحسن الحديث

TAB-FULL:v20p190#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p190#2/r4.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v20p190#2/r4.claim: Al-Suddī glosses the description as parts of the Book resembling one another.

TAB-FULL:v20p190#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p190#2/r5.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TAB-FULL:v20p190#2/r5.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr says the Quran's parts resemble, confirm, and point to one another.
TAB-FULL:v20p190#2/r5.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير، في قوله: {كتابا متشابها}

TAB-FULL:v20p192/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p192/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p192/r1.claim: The Quran repeats accounts, reports, judgments, legal rulings, and proofs within it.
TAB-FULL:v20p192/r1.anchor: عن قتادة، {مثاني} [الزمر: 23] قال: «ثنى الله فيه الفرائض، والقضاء، والحدود»

TAB-FULL:v20p192/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p192/r2.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v20p192/r2.claim: Al-Hasan says God repeated judgments in the Book, with a verse in one surah resembling a verse in another.
TAB-FULL:v20p192/r2.anchor: عن الحسن، في قوله: {الله نزل أحسن الحديث كتابا

TAB-FULL:v20p192/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p192/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v20p192/r3.claim: Mujahid says the Quran throughout is described as recurring pairs.

TAB-FULL:v20p192/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p192/r4.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v20p192/r4.claim: Qatada says obligations, judgments, and prescribed penalties are repeated in the Quran.

TAB-FULL:v20p192/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p192/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v20p192/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says the Book repeats a matter many times.

TAB-FULL:v20p192/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p192/r6.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v20p192/r6.claim: Al-Suddī says the Book repeats matters many times and in more than one place.

TAB-FULL:v20p192/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p192/r7.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v20p192/r7.claim: Ibn Zayd says the Quran repeats material, recounting Moses, Salih, Hud, and other prophets in many places.

TAB-FULL:v20p193/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p193/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p193/r1.claim: When the God-fearing hear the Quran recited, their skins shiver; then their skins and hearts soften toward God's remembrance, meaning acting on and affirming the Book.
TAB-FULL:v20p193/r1.anchor: تقشعر من سماعه إذا تلي عليهم جلود الذين يخافون ربهم

TAB-FULL:v20p193/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p193/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v20p193/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that when the Companions asked the Prophet to tell them stories, this verse was revealed.
TAB-FULL:v20p193/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قالوا: يا رسول الله لو حدثتنا؟

TAB-FULL:v20p193/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p193/r3.speaker: عمرو بن قيس
TAB-FULL:v20p193/r3.claim: A report from ʿAmr ibn Qays likewise says people asked the Prophet for a narration and this verse followed.
TAB-FULL:v20p193/r3.anchor: عن عمرو بن قيس، قال: قالوا: يا نبي الله،

TAB-FULL:v20p193/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p193/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p193/r4.claim: The shivering and subsequent softening described are God's guidance and enabling of those people.
TAB-FULL:v20p193/r4.anchor: هذا الذي يصيب هؤلاء القوم الذين وصفت صفتهم عند سماعهم القرآن من اقشعرار جلودهم

TAB-FULL:v20p193/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p193/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p193/r5.claim: God guides whichever servants He wills by means of the Quran.
TAB-FULL:v20p193/r5.anchor: يهدي تبارك وتعالى بالقرآن من يشاء من عباده

TAB-FULL:v20p193/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p193/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p193/r6.claim: Alternatively, “that” may refer to the Quran itself: it is God's clarification, by which He guides whom He wills to believe in it.

TAB-FULL:v20p194/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p194/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p194/r1.claim: Whoever God leaves astray from belief in and affirmation of the Quran has no guide to enable or direct him to follow it.
TAB-FULL:v20p194/r1.anchor: ومن يخذله الله عن الإيمان بهذا القرآن والتصديق بما فيه،

TAB-FULL:v1p97/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p97/r1.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TAB-FULL:v1p97/r1.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr identifies the seven long sūrahs as al-Baqarah, Āl ʿImrān, al-Nisāʾ, al-Māʾidah, al-Anʿām, al-Aʿrāf, and Yūnus.
TAB-FULL:v1p97/r1.anchor: فالسبع الطول: البقرة، وآل عمران، والنساء، والمائدة، والأنعام، والأعراف، ويونس؛ في قول سعيد بن جبير

TAB-FULL:v1p97/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p97/r2.speaker: عثمان بن عفان
TAB-FULL:v1p97/r2.claim: Uthman said al-Anfāl and Barāʾah were paired without a basmala because their stories resembled each other and the Prophet died without clarifying whether they were one sūrah.
TAB-FULL:v1p97/r2.anchor: قال عثمان: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، مما يأتي عليه الزمان، وهو تنزل عليه السور ذوات العدد

TAB-FULL:v1p97/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p97/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p97/r3.claim: Al-Ṭabarī infers from the report that Uthman did not know al-Anfāl and Barāʾah belonged among the seven long sūrahs, and Ibn ʿAbbās did not count them there either.
TAB-FULL:v1p97/r3.anchor: فهذا الخبر ينبئ عن عثمان بن عفان رحمة الله عليه أنه لم يكن تبين له أن الأنفال وبراءة، من السبع الطول

TAB-FULL:v1p97/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p97/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p97/r4.claim: The seven long sūrahs are named for their greater length than the other Qur’anic sūrahs.
TAB-FULL:v1p97/r4.anchor: وإنما سميت هذه السور السبع الطول، لطولها على سائر سور القرآن

TAB-FULL:v1p97/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p97/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p97/r5.claim: The miʾūn are sūrahs with about one hundred verses, allowing a small excess or shortfall.
TAB-FULL:v1p97/r5.anchor: فهي ما كان من سور القرآن، عدد آيه مائة آية، أو تزيد عليها شيئا أو تنقص منها شيئا يسيرا

TAB-FULL:v1p97/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p97/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p97/r6.claim: Al-mathānī are the sūrahs that follow the miʾūn: the hundred-verse sūrahs come first, and the mathānī after them.
TAB-FULL:v1p97/r6.anchor: فإنها ما ثنى المئين فتلاها، وكان المئون لها أوائل، وكان المثاني لها ثواني

TAB-FULL:v1p97/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p97/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v1p97/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās offers another explanation: they are called mathānī because God repeats parables, reports, and lessons in them.
TAB-FULL:v1p97/r7.anchor: وقد قيل: إن المثاني سميت مثاني لتثنية الله جل ذكره فيها الأمثال والخبر والعبر، وهو قول ابن عباس

TAB-FULL:v1p100/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p100/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v1p100/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the mathānī are so named because legal duties and limits are repeated in them.
TAB-FULL:v1p100/r1.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير، عن ابن عباس، وروى عن سعيد بن جبير أنه كان يقول

TAB-FULL:v1p100/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p100/r2.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TAB-FULL:v1p100/r2.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr likewise explains the name mathānī by the repetition of duties and legal limits.
TAB-FULL:v1p100/r2.anchor: وروى عن سعيد بن جبير أنه كان يقول: «إنما سميت مثاني لأنها ثنيت فيها الفرائض والحدود»

TAB-FULL:v1p100/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p100/r3.speaker: جماعة يكثر تعدادهم
TAB-FULL:v1p100/r3.claim: One numerous group holds that the entire Qur’an is called mathānī.
TAB-FULL:v1p100/r3.anchor: وقد قال جماعة يكثر تعدادهم: «القرآن كله مثان»

TAB-FULL:v1p100/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p100/r4.speaker: جماعة أخرى
TAB-FULL:v1p100/r4.claim: Another group identifies al-mathānī specifically as the Fātiḥah, because it is recited twice in every prayer.
TAB-FULL:v1p100/r4.anchor: وقال جماعة أخرى: بل المثاني فاتحة الكتاب، لأنها تثنى قراءتها في كل صلاة

TAB-FULL:v1p100/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p100/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p100/r5.claim: Al-Ṭabarī postpones naming the proponents, their arguments, and his preferred conclusion about these views until his commentary on 15:87.
TAB-FULL:v1p100/r5.anchor: وسنذكر أسماء قائلي ذلك وعللهم، والصواب من القول، فيما اختلفوا فيه من ذلك، إذا انتهينا إلى تأويل قوله تعالى

TAB-FULL:v1p100/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p100/r6.speaker: قائل الأبيات
TAB-FULL:v1p100/r6.claim: A poem lists the seven long sūrahs, miʾūn, mathānī, ṭawāsīn, ḥawāmīm, and mufassal, attesting these category names.
TAB-FULL:v1p100/r6.anchor: حلفت بالسبع اللواتي طولت … وبمئين بعدها قد أمئيت

TAB-FULL:v1p100/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p100/r7.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p100/r7.claim: Al-Ṭabarī says the poem confirms the explanations he has given for these Qur’anic categories.
TAB-FULL:v1p100/r7.anchor: قال أبو جعفر: وهذه الأبيات تدل على صحة التأويل الذي تأولناه، في هذه الأسماء

TAB-FULL:v1p100/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p100/r8.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p100/r8.claim: Al-mufaṣṣal is named for the many separations between its sūrahs made by the basmala.
TAB-FULL:v1p100/r8.anchor: وأما المفصل، فإنها سميت مفصلا، لكثرة الفصول التي بين سورها ببسم الله الرحمن الرحيم

TAB-FULL:v1p100/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p100/r9.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p100/r9.claim: A Qur’anic sūrah is pluralized as suwar, following patterns like khuṭbah/khuṭab and ghurfah/ghuraf.
TAB-FULL:v1p100/r9.anchor: ثم تسمى كل سورة من القرآن سورة، وتجمع سورا، على تقدير خطبة وخطب، وغرفة وغرف

TAB-FULL:v1p100/r10.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p100/r10.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p100/r10.claim: Without hamza, sūrah means an elevated rank; the city wall is called sūr because it rises above what it encloses.
TAB-FULL:v1p100/r10.anchor: والسورة بغير همز: المنزلة من منازل الارتفاع، ومن ذلك سور المدينة، سمي بذلك الحائط الذي يحويها لارتفاعه

TAB-FULL:v1p100/r11.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p100/r11.speaker: العجاج
TAB-FULL:v1p100/r11.claim: Al-ʿAjjāj’s line uses al-sūr for a building or wall, illustrating architectural usage of the word.
TAB-FULL:v1p100/r11.anchor: قال العجاج: في جمع السورة من البناء

TAB-FULL:v1p100/r12.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p100/r12.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p100/r12.claim: Tabarī explains that collective nouns such as grain name a mass, while their feminine forms name portions; Qur’anic sūrahs are independent units, so their plural follows individual rooms and sermons.
TAB-FULL:v1p100/r12.anchor: ثم جعلت الواحدة منه كالقطعة من جميعه، فقيل: برة وشعيرة وقصبة، يراد به قطعة منه، ولم تكن سور القرآن موجودة مجتمعة اجتماع البر والشعير

TAB-FULL:v1p107/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p107/r2.speaker: أبو النجم العجلي
TAB-FULL:v1p107/r2.claim: Abū al-Najm’s poem calls al-Ḥamd both Qur’an and mathānī, supporting the Fātiḥah interpretation.
TAB-FULL:v1p107/r2.anchor: قصد أبو النجم العجلي، بقوله: [البحر السريع] الحمد لله الذي عافاني

TAB-FULL:v1p107/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p107/r3.speaker: الراجز الآخر
TAB-FULL:v1p107/r3.claim: Another rajaz poem calls Umm al-Kitāb the seven of mathānī, identifying the Fātiḥah by that title.
TAB-FULL:v1p107/r3.anchor: قول الراجز الآخر: [البحر الرجز] نشدتكم بمنزل الفرقان أم الكتاب السبع من مثاني

TABATABAI:39:23/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:23/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:23/r2.claim: The verse sums up the preceding account of guidance while also explaining the guidance provided by the Qur’an.
TABATABAI:39:23/r2.anchor: كالإجمال بعد التفصيل بالنسبة إلى الآية السابقة بالنظر إلى ما يتحصل من الآية

TABATABAI:39:23/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:23/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:23/r3.claim: “The best discourse” is the Qur’an; ḥadīth here means speech, as in 52:34 and 77:50.
TABATABAI:39:23/r3.anchor: والحديث هو القول كما في قوله تعالى

TABATABAI:39:23/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:23/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:23/r4.claim: The Qur’an is the best speech because it contains pure truth, untouched by falsehood, and is God’s majestic speech.
TABATABAI:39:23/r4.anchor: فهو أحسن القول لاشتماله على محض الحق

TABATABAI:39:23/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:23/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:23/r5.claim: Here “mutashābih” means that the Qur’an’s parts resemble one another; unlike ambiguous verses, this quality belongs to the whole book.
TABATABAI:39:23/r5.anchor: يشبه بعض أجزائه بعضا وهذا غير التشابه الذي في المتشابه

TABATABAI:39:23/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:23/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:23/r6.claim: Mathānī is the plural of mathniya, something turned back: Qur’anic verses refer back to, clarify, and interpret one another.
TABATABAI:39:23/r6.anchor: جمع مثنية بمعنى المعطوف لانعطاف بعض آياته على بعض

TABATABAI:39:23/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:23/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:23/r7.claim: The verses explain one another without contradiction, as affirmed by 4:82.
TABATABAI:39:23/r7.anchor: من غير اختلاف فيها بحيث يدفع بعضه بعضا ويناقضه

TABATABAI:39:23/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:23/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:23/r8.claim: The clause describing the skin’s shudder is an adjective of the book, not a new independent sentence.

TABATABAI:39:23/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:23/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:23/r9.claim: Iqshiʿrār is a strong contraction of the skin caused by fear on hearing or seeing something awe-inspiring.
TABATABAI:39:23/r9.anchor: والاقشعرار تقبض الجلد تقبضا شديدا لخشية عارضة

TABATABAI:39:23/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:23/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:23/r10.claim: Those who fear God understand their own position before His majesty; hearing His speech turns them toward divine greatness, bringing fear to their hearts and a shudder to their skin.
TABATABAI:39:23/r10.anchor: لأنهم على تبصر من موقف نفوسهم قبال عظمة ربهم

TABATABAI:39:23/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:23/r11.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:23/r11.claim: Talīnu carries the sense of settling and becoming tranquil, which explains its construction with ilā: their skin and hearts rest in and accept God’s remembrance.
TABATABAI:39:23/r11.anchor: مضمنة معنى السكون والطمأنينة ولذا عدي بالى

TABATABAI:39:23/r12.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:23/r12.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:23/r12.claim: Hearts are not mentioned with the shudder because “hearts” means souls, which experience fear but do not physically shudder.
TABATABAI:39:23/r12.anchor: ولم يذكر القلوب في الجملة السابقة عند ذكر الاقشعرار

TABATABAI:39:23/r13.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:23/r13.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:23/r13.claim: “That is God’s guidance” refers to the sequence of Qur’anic awe and then the settling of skin and hearts into remembrance, defining guidance by its effect.
TABATABAI:39:23/r13.anchor: أي ما يأخذهم من اقشعرار الجلود من القرآن ثم سكون

TABATABAI:39:23/r14.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:23/r14.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:23/r14.claim: God guides through this guidance servants whose readiness remains intact and who are not obstructed by wrongdoing or sin.
TABATABAI:39:23/r14.anchor: يهدي بهداه من يشاء من عباده وهو الذي لم يبطل

TABATABAI:39:23/r15.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:23/r15.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:23/r15.claim: The wording suggests that guidance is bestowed by grace, not imposed as something to which God is compelled.
TABATABAI:39:23/r15.anchor: وفي السياق إشعار بأن الهداية من فضله وليس بموجب

TABATABAI:39:23/r16.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:23/r16.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:39:23/r16.claim: An alternative takes “that” to refer to the Qur’an; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī dismisses this reading.
TABATABAI:39:23/r16.anchor: وقيل المشار إليه بقوله { ذلك هدى الله } القرآن وهو كما ترى

TABATABAI:39:23/r17.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:23/r17.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:23/r17.claim: Some infer that guidance is exclusively God’s act, but al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī says the verse does not establish that.
TABATABAI:39:23/r17.anchor: وقد استدل بالآيات على أن الهداية من صنع الله لا يشاركه فيها غيره

TABATABAI:39:23-29/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:23-29/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:23-29/r1.claim: Guidance belongs to God directly or through guides He has guided; whoever He leaves unguided in both ways has no guide.
TABATABAI:39:23-29/r1.anchor: فالهداية كلها لله إما بلا واسطة أو بواسطة الهداة المهديين من خلقه وعلى هذا

TABATABAI:39:23-29/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:23-29/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:23-29/r2.claim: The closing statement is repeated elsewhere in God’s speech.
TABATABAI:39:23-29/r2.anchor: فلا هادي له وذلك قوله في ذيل الآية { ومن يضلل الله فما له من هاد } وسيأتي الجملة بعد عدة آيات وهي متكررة في كلامه تعالى

TABATABAI:39:21-37/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:21-37/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TABATABAI:39:21-37/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that people asked the Prophet to tell them stories, after which the verse describing the Qur’an as the best discourse was revealed; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī calls this an application of the verse.
TABATABAI:39:21-37/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس قالوا يا رسول الله لو حدثتنا فنزل

TABATABAI:39:21-37/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:21-37/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
TABATABAI:39:21-37/r2.claim: The Prophet says that when a servant’s skin shudders from fear of God, sins fall away like leaves from a dry tree.
TABATABAI:39:21-37/r2.anchor: عن العباس بن عبد المطلب أن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم قال

TABRISI:39:22/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:22/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:39:22/r7.claim: Kitaban is accusative as an appositional substitute for the best discourse.
TABRISI:39:22/r7.anchor: { كتابا } منصوب لأنه بدل من قوله أحسن الحديث

TABRISI:39:22-23/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:22-23/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:39:22-23/r9.claim: The best discourse is the Quran; it is called hadith as God's speech, like the Prophet's speech, and as revelation later than earlier scriptures.
TABRISI:39:22-23/r9.anchor: { الله نزل أحسن الحديث } يعني القرآن سماه الله حديثا

TABRISI:39:22-23/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:22-23/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:39:22-23/r10.claim: The Quran is best for its extreme eloquence, inimitability, and inclusion of needed proofs, law, exhortation, prophetic stories, promise, and warning.
TABRISI:39:22-23/r10.anchor: وهو أحسن الحديث لفرط فصاحته ولإعجازه واشتماله على جميع ما يحتاج المكلف إليه

TABRISI:39:22-23/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:22-23/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:39:22-23/r11.claim: Its passages resemble and confirm one another, with no disagreement or contradiction.
TABRISI:39:22-23/r11.anchor: { كتابا متشابها } يشبه بعضه بعضا ويصدق بعضه بعضا

TABRISI:39:22-23/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:22-23/r12.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:39:22-23/r12.claim: An alternative says the Quran resembles earlier revealed books while being more comprehensive and beneficial.
TABRISI:39:22-23/r12.anchor: وقيل: معناه أنه يشبه كتب الله المتقدمة وإن كان أعم

TABRISI:39:22-23/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:22-23/r13.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:39:22-23/r13.claim: Another explanation takes its resemblance to mean consistency in fine composition, strong diction, and excellent meanings.
TABRISI:39:22-23/r13.anchor: وقيل: متشابها في حسن النظم وجزالة اللفظ وجودة المعاني

TABRISI:39:22-23/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:22-23/r14.speaker: author
TABRISI:39:22-23/r14.claim: It is called mathani because stories, reports, rulings, and exhortations recur in varied forms of expression.
TABRISI:39:22-23/r14.anchor: { مثاني } سمي بذلك لأنه يثنى فيه بعض القصص والأخبار

TABRISI:39:22-23/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:22-23/r15.speaker: author
TABRISI:39:22-23/r15.claim: Its repeated recitation does not become tiresome because of the beauty of its sound.
TABRISI:39:22-23/r15.anchor: ويثنى أيضا في التلاوة فلا يمل لحسن مسموعه

TABRISI:39:22-23/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:22-23/r16.speaker: author
TABRISI:39:22-23/r16.claim: Skin shivers at Quranic threats, then softens at promises of reward and mercy; hearts settle with God's mention of Paradise and reward, whose object is omitted.
TABRISI:39:22-23/r16.anchor: { تقشعر منه جلود الذين يخشون ربهم } أي تأخذهم قشعريرة خوفا مما في القرآن من الوعيد

TABRISI:39:23-25/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:23-25/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TABRISI:39:23-25/r1.claim: The Prophet says that when a servant's skin shivers from fear of God, sins fall away like leaves from a dry tree.
TABRISI:39:23-25/r1.anchor: إذا اقشعر جلد العبد من خشية الله تحاتت عنه ذنوبه كما يتحات عن الشجرة اليابسة ورقها

TABRISI:39:23-25/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:23-25/r2.speaker: قتادة
TABRISI:39:23-25/r2.claim: Qatāda describes God's friends as shivering and then finding calm in remembrance; loss of reason and fainting belong to innovators and come from Satan.
TABRISI:39:23-25/r2.anchor: وقال قتادة: هذا نعت لأولياء الله نعتهم بأن تقشعر جلودهم وتطمئن قلوبهم إلى ذكر الله

TABRISI:39:23-25/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:23-25/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:39:23-25/r3.claim: That guidance refers to the Quran.

TABRISI:39:23-25/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:23-25/r4.speaker: الجبائي
TABRISI:39:23-25/r4.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī says God guides by the Quran's proofs those of Muhammad's community to whom He gave it.
TABRISI:39:23-25/r4.anchor: من عباده بما نصب فيه من الأدلة وهم الذين آتاهم القرآن

TABRISI:39:23-25/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:23-25/r5.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:39:23-25/r5.claim: Another view says those who benefit from guidance are singled out as guided because those who fail to follow it cannot be described as guided.
TABRISI:39:23-25/r5.anchor: إنما خصهم بذلك لأنهم المنتفعون بالهداية ومن لم يهتد لا يوصف

TABRISI:39:23-25/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:23-25/r6.speaker: الجبائي
TABRISI:39:23-25/r6.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī explains misguidance as being turned from the path to Paradise, with no one able to guide the person there.
TABRISI:39:23-25/r6.anchor: ومن يضلل الله } عن طريق الجنة { فما له من هاد

TABRISI:39:23-25/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:23-25/r7.speaker: أبو مسلم
TABRISI:39:23-25/r7.claim: Abū Muslim explains the phrase as straying away from God and His mercy, with no guide remaining.
TABRISI:39:23-25/r7.anchor: وقيل: معناه من ضل عن الله ورحمته فلا هادي له

TABRISI:39:23-25/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:23-25/r8.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:39:23-25/r8.claim: A further explanation is deprivation of increases in guidance and grace, since the unbeliever has no such grace.
TABRISI:39:23-25/r8.anchor: وقيل: معناه من يضلله عن زيادة الهدى والألطاف

TABRISI:39:23-25/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:23-25/r15.speaker: أبو مسلم
TABRISI:39:23-25/r15.claim: Abū Muslim links the Quran as the best discourse to the prior command to follow the best saying, making the Quran especially worthy of following.
TABRISI:39:23-25/r15.anchor: واتصل قوله { الله نزل أحسن الحديث } بما تقدمه من قوله { فبشر عبادي

THALABI:v8p230/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p230/r2.speaker: ابن مسعود وابن عباس
THALABI:v8p230/r2.claim: Ibn Masud and Ibn Abbas say the Companions asked the Prophet to tell them something, and this verse was revealed.
THALABI:v8p230/r2.anchor:
قال ابن مسعود: وابن عباس: قال الصحابة:
يا رسول الله لو حدثتنا، فنزلت الله نزل أحسن الحديث

THALABI:v8p230/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p230/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p230/r3.claim: The Quran's passages resemble one another in beauty and affirm one another, without contradiction or discrepancy.
THALABI:v8p230/r3.anchor: يشبه بعضه بعضا في الحسن ويصدق بعضه بعضا ليس فيه تناقض ولا اختلاف فيه

THALABI:v8p230/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p230/r4.speaker: قتادة
THALABI:v8p230/r4.claim: Qatada says each verse resembles another verse, each word another word, and each letter another letter.
THALABI:v8p230/r4.anchor: وقال قتادة: تشبه الآية الآية والكلمة الكلمة والحرف الحرف

THALABI:v8p230/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p230/r5.speaker: المفسرون
THALABI:v8p230/r5.claim: Exegetes say reports, rulings, and legal limits recur in the Quran, which is repeated in recitation without becoming tiresome.
THALABI:v8p230/r5.anchor: قال المفسرون: يسمى القرآن مثاني لأنه تثنى فيه الأخبار والأحكام والحدود وثنى للتلاوة فلا يمل

THALABI:v8p230/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p230/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p230/r6.claim: The skins and hearts soften toward remembrance by acting on God's Book and affirming it.
THALABI:v8p230/r6.anchor: يعني إلى العمل بكتاب الله والتصديق به

THALABI:v8p230/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p230/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p230/r7.claim: An alternative explanation takes إلى in the sense of لام.

THALABI:v8p230/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p230/r8.speaker: أسماء بنت أبي بكر
THALABI:v8p230/r8.claim: Asma says the Prophet's Companions wept and their skins shivered when the Quran was recited.
THALABI:v8p230/r8.anchor: قالت: كانوا كما نعتهم الله تعالى تدمع أعينهم وتقشعر جلودهم.

THALABI:v8p230/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p230/r9.speaker: أسماء بنت أبي بكر
THALABI:v8p230/r9.claim: Asked about people who collapse when Quran is recited, Asma says to seek refuge from Satan.
THALABI:v8p230/r9.anchor: فقالت: أعوذ بالله من الشيطان الرجيم.

THALABI:v8p230/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p230/r10.speaker: ابن عمر
THALABI:v8p230/r10.claim: Ibn Umar says Muslims fear God without collapsing; he attributes such behavior to Satan and says it was not the Companions' practice.
THALABI:v8p230/r10.anchor: فقال ابن عمر: إنا لنخشى الله وما نسقط. وقال ابن عمر: إن الشيطان يدخل في جوف أحدهم، ما كان هذا صنيع أصحاب محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم.

THALABI:v8p231/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p231/r1.speaker: ابن سيرين
THALABI:v8p231/r1.claim: Ibn Sirin proposes testing people who faint during recitation by seating them at a rooftop edge; if they throw themselves off, they are truthful.
THALABI:v8p231/r1.anchor: قال: ذكر عند ابن سيرين الذين يصرعون إذا قرئ عليهم القرآن فقال: بيننا وبينهم أن يقعد أحدهم على ظهر بيت باسطا رجليه

THALABI:v8p231/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p231/r2.speaker: أبو عمران الجوني
THALABI:v8p231/r2.claim: Abu Imran al-Juni reports that when a man tore his shirt during Moses' preaching, God told Moses to ask whether tearing it would expose the man's heart.
THALABI:v8p231/r2.anchor: أبو عمران الجوني قال: وعظ موسى (عليه السلام) قومه فشق رجل منهم قميصه فقيل لموسى قل لصاحب القميص لا يشق قميصه

THALABI:v8p231/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p231/r3.speaker: أبي بن كعب
THALABI:v8p231/r3.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam reports that Ubayy recited to the Prophet and they were moved; the Prophet said to seize the moment for supplication, since tenderness is mercy.
THALABI:v8p231/r3.anchor: عن زيد بن أسلم قال: قرأ أبي بن كعب عند النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فرقوا فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «اغتنموا الدعاء عند الرقة فإنها رحمة»

THALABI:v8p232/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p232/r1.speaker: العباس بن عبد المطلب
THALABI:v8p232/r1.claim: Abbas reports the Prophet saying that when a servant's skin shivers from fear of God, sins fall away like leaves from a dry tree.
THALABI:v8p232/r1.anchor: إذا اقشعر جلد العبد من خشية الله تعالى تحاتت عنه ذنوبه كما تحاتت عن الشجر اليابسة ورقها

THALABI:v8p232/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p232/r2.speaker: العباس بن عبد المطلب
THALABI:v8p232/r2.claim: A second report from Abbas says God protects from the Fire a servant whose skin shivers from fear of Him.
THALABI:v8p232/r2.anchor: عن أم كلثوم بنت العباس عن أبيها قال: سمعت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: «إذا اقشعر جلد العبد من خشية الله تعالى حرمه الله تعالى على النار»

THALABI:v8p232/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p232/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p232/r3.claim: That guidance refers to the best discourse, through which God guides whomever He wills.
THALABI:v8p232/r3.anchor: ذلك يعني أحسن الحديث هدى الله يهدي به من يشاء

THALABI:v8p232/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p232/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p232/r4.claim: The statement that none can guide whom God leads astray rebuts the Qadariyya.
THALABI:v8p232/r4.anchor: ومن يضلل الله فما له من هاد وفيه رد على القدرية

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:39:21-23/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:39:21-23/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:39:21-23/r5.claim: The Quran's passages resemble one another without contradiction; it repeats accounts and stories, and mentions reward and punishment.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:39:21-23/r5.anchor: يشبه بعضه بعضا من غير اختلاف ولا تناقض { مثاني } يثني فيه الأخبار والقصص

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:39:21-23/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:39:21-23/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:39:21-23/r6.claim: The skin shivers in fear when a punishment verse is recited, then skin and heart soften toward God at a verse of mercy; fear and hope constitute God's guidance.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:39:21-23/r6.anchor: يعني: عند ذكر آية العذاب { ثم تلين جلودهم وقلوبهم إلى ذكر الله } أي: من آية الرحمة

QASHANI:39:22-24/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:39:22-24/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:39:22-24/r4.claim: The Book is consistent in truth and is repeated because it descends to the heart before and after annihilation, alternating between the Real and creation.
QASHANI:39:22-24/r4.anchor: لتنزلها عليك في مقام القلب قبل الفناء وبعده فتكون مكررة باعتبار الحق والخلق

QASHANI:39:22-24/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:39:22-24/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:39:22-24/r5.claim: The skins of God-knowing scholars shiver as luminous forms descend upon the heart and their effects reach the body.
QASHANI:39:22-24/r5.anchor: أهل الخشية من العلماء بالله لانفعالها بالهيئات النوراينة الواردة على القلب النازل أثرها إلى البدن

QASHANI:39:22-24/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:39:22-24/r6.speaker: author
QASHANI:39:22-24/r6.claim: Their skins, hearts, and limbs then soften into compliance, calm, and tranquility as they turn to God's remembrance.

QASHANI:39:22-24/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:39:22-24/r7.speaker: author
QASHANI:39:22-24/r7.claim: The limbs become compliant and tranquil as they turn toward God's remembrance; this is God's guidance, through which He guides whom He wills.
QASHANI:39:22-24/r7.anchor: الانقياد والسكينة والطمأنينة { إلى ذكر الله

QASHANI:39:22-24/r8.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:39:22-24/r8.speaker: author
QASHANI:39:22-24/r8.claim: Those God misguides are veiled from the light, cannot understand His speech or see its meaning, and have no guide.
QASHANI:39:22-24/r8.anchor: { ومن يضلل الله } يحجبه عن النور فلا يفهم كلامه ولا يرى معناه

ELMALILI:39:22-31/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:39:22-31/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:39:22-31/r2.claim: He renders the Qur’an’s description as an ‘ikizli, âhenkli’ book and says the God-fearing first shiver, then their skins and hearts soften to God’s remembrance.
ELMALILI:39:22-31/r2.anchor: ikizli, âhenkli bir kitap. Ondan Rablerine saygısı olanların derileri ürperir, sonra derileri de kalbleri de Allah’ın zikrine yumuşar.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:23/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:23/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:23/r1.claim: Mesānī is the plural of mesnā or müsennā, meaning “two by two”; here it describes statements about the Qur’an that are repeatedly said, read, or needed.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:23/r1.anchor: mesânî kelimesi, sözlükte “ikili ikili” anlamına gelen mesnâ veya müsennâ kelimesinin çoğulu olup burada “tekrar tekrar söylenen, okunan veya bildirilmesi gerekeni sık sık dile getiren sözler, açıklamalar” anlamında olmak üzere Kur’an hakkında kullanılmıştır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:23/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:23/r2.speaker: author
