KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:23/r2.claim: Because God sent the Qur’an, it is divine speech; the angel of revelation and the Prophet transmit that speech to humanity.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:23/r2.anchor: Kur’an’ı Allah indirmiştir, o ilâhî kelâmdır; vahiy meleği ve peygamber ise bu kelâmın insanlığa ileticileridir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:23/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:23/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:23/r3.claim: The Qur’an is the best of speech because its information is true, its rulings just and beneficial, and its way right and saving.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:23/r3.anchor: ondaki bilgiler ve haberler gerçek, hükümler adaletli ve yararlı; onun gösterdiği yol doğru ve kurtarıcıdır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:23/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:23/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:23/r4.claim: As a book, the Qur’an is a divine guide made into a written document so it can remain, be read, and benefit humanity until the Resurrection.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:23/r4.anchor: insanlığın kurtuluş rehberi olarak kıyamete kadar yaşatılması, okunması, istifade edilmesi için yazılı belge haline getirilmesi gereken ve öyle de yapılmış olan ilâhî bir rehberdir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:23/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:23/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:23/r5.claim: The Qur’an is internally harmonious, beautiful in wording, composition, and style, consistent in content, and free of unreasonable or inexplicable explanations.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:23/r5.anchor: kendi içinde uyumlu; sözleri, nazmı ve üslûbu güzel, ahenkli, içeriği tutarlıdır; onda mâkul ve izahı mümkün olmayan hiçbir açıklama yoktur.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:23/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:23/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:23/r6.claim: Mesānī means that the Qur’an repeats the same knowledge in identical or varied expressions to enlighten readers and listeners, or that it can be read and heard repeatedly with pleasure and without weariness.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:23/r6.anchor: aynı bilgileri bazan aynı, bazan farklı ifadelerle tekrar tekrar dile getiren veya bıkkınlık vermeden tekrar tekrar zevkle okunan, dinlenen bir kitaptır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:23/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:23/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:23/r7.claim: The commentary also reports Razi’s interpretation that mesānī refers to paired concepts and rulings that recur in the Qur’an, such as creator and created, light and darkness, promise and threat, and command and prohibition.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:23/r7.anchor: yaratıcı-yaratılan, melek-şeytan, aydınlık-karanlık, dünya-âhiret, cennet-cehennem, vaad-vaîd (tehdit), korku-ümit, buyruklar-yasaklar gibi ikişerli kavramların, hükümlerin Kur’an’da sıklıkla yer aldığını belirtmek üzere kullanıldığı yorumları da yapılmıştır (Râzî, XXVI, 271-272).

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:23/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:23/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:23/r8.claim: The Qur’an moves readers through both its expression and content, causing fear and anxiety in some places and joy and hope in others; sound-meaning harmony can affect even those who do not understand its meaning.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:23/r8.anchor: Kur’an, hem ifade ve üslûbuyla hem de içeriğiyle okuyucuyu derinden etkiler; yerine göre korkutup kaygılandırır, yerine göre sevindirip ümitlendirir.

BAQILLANI:v1p35/r1.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p35/r1.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p35/r1.claim: The Qur'an's composition lies outside familiar Arabic genres: poetry, unrhymed meter, sajʿ, mixed forms, and ordinary prose; it has a distinctive style throughout.
BAQILLANI:v1p35/r1.anchor: وقد علمنا أن القرآن خارج عن هذه الوجوه ومباين لهذه الطرق

BAQILLANI:v1p35/r2.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p35/r2.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p35/r2.claim: No Arab author produced a work of comparable length with the Qur'an's eloquence, rare expression, inventive range, subtle meanings, abundant wisdom, and rhetorical harmony.
BAQILLANI:v1p35/r2.anchor: ليس للعرب كلام مشتمل على هذه الفصاحة والغرابة والتصرف البديع والمعاني اللطيفة

BAQILLANI:v1p35/r3.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p35/r3.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p35/r3.claim: The Qur'an remains harmonious across its length; extended human speech develops variation and flaws, as the Qur'an itself says of speech from other than God.
BAQILLANI:v1p35/r3.anchor: وقد حصل القران على كثرته وطوله متناسبا في الفصاحة

BAQILLANI:v1p202/r1.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p202/r1.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p202/r1.claim: The Qur'an's distinctive evidence extends from individual words and phrases through complete stories, chapters, and the whole book, though some passages show it more clearly.
BAQILLANI:v1p202/r1.anchor: وإن كانت الدلالة في البعض أبين وأظهر والآية أكشف وأبهر

BAQILLANI:v1p202/r2.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p202/r2.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p202/r2.claim: Contemplating the Qur'an can illuminate and convince the mind while producing awe, emotional trembling, joy, and a heightened sense of certainty.

BAQILLANI:v1p202/r3.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p202/r3.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p202/r3.claim: The Qur'an's influence is visible in public life and hearts, and its required preservation and recitation in prayer demonstrate its great rank; it is opened with the commanded refuge prayer.
BAQILLANI:v1p202/r3.anchor: جعل عماد الصلاة التي هي تلو الإيمان في التأكيد وثانيه التوحيد في الوجوب

BAQILLANI:v1p203/r1.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p203/r1.speaker: الأصمعي
BAQILLANI:v1p203/r1.claim: Al-Aṣmaʿī said that masters of poetry are fewer than masters of war.
BAQILLANI:v1p203/r1.anchor: سمعت الأصمعي يقول فرسان الشعر أقل من فرسان الحرب

BAQILLANI:v1p203/r2.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p203/r2.speaker: أبو عمرو بن العلاء
BAQILLANI:v1p203/r2.claim: Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ said that scholars of poetry are rarer than red sulfur.
BAQILLANI:v1p203/r2.anchor: وقال سمعت أبا عمرو بن العلاء يقول العلماء بالشعر أعز من الكبريت الأحمر

BAQILLANI:v1p203/r3.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p203/r3.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p203/r3.claim: Ordinary speech is difficult to judge and critics often disagree about its merits; the most eloquent Arabs were bewildered by the Qur'an and answered with conjecture and dismissive labels.
BAQILLANI:v1p203/r3.anchor: وقد حير القوم الذين لم يكن أحد أفصح منهم ولا أتم بلاغة

BAQILLANI:v1p203/r4.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p203/r4.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p203/r4.claim: God's description of the Qur'an as the best speech suffices to establish its excellence; a small sample can disclose the quality of a larger work.
BAQILLANI:v1p203/r4.anchor: فليس يوقف على حسن الكلام بطوله ولا تعرف براعته بكثرة فصوله

BAQILLANI:v1p203/r5.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p203/r5.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p203/r5.claim: Only God's guidance enables recognition of the Qur'an's excellence; God guides or misguides many through it.
BAQILLANI:v1p203/r5.anchor: فلا تعلم ما وصفنا لك إلا بهداية من العزيز الحميد

BAQILLANI:v1p130/r1.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p130/r1.speaker: خطيب غير مسمى
BAQILLANI:v1p130/r1.claim: The sermon calls God's book the best and most eloquent speech and praises those whom God adorns with it and brings to Islam.
BAQILLANI:v1p130/r1.anchor: إن أحسن الحديث كتاب الله قد أفلح من زينه الله في قلبه

BAQILLANI:v1p130/r2.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p130/r2.speaker: خطيب غير مسمى
BAQILLANI:v1p130/r2.claim: The sermon urges love of God and those He loves, continued attention to God's speech and remembrance, worship without associating partners, and mutual love through God's spirit.
BAQILLANI:v1p130/r2.anchor: ولا تملوا كلام الله وذكره ولا تقسو عليه قلوبكم اعبدوا الله ولا تشركوا به شيئا

QUSHAYRI:v3p116/r12.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p116/r12.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p116/r12.claim: The Qur’an is the best discourse because it is uncreated.

QUSHAYRI:v3p116/r13.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p116/r13.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p116/r13.claim: The Book is called mutually similar because of its inimitability and eloquence.

QUSHAYRI:v3p116/r14.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p116/r14.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p116/r14.claim: The repeated passages set out judgments without tiring the reader and include praise of God’s sovereignty and beneficence, descriptions of Paradise and Hell, and promises and threats.
QUSHAYRI:v3p116/r14.anchor: يثني فيها الحكم ولا يمل بتكرار القراءة ، ويشتمل على نوعين : الثناء عليه بذكر سلطانه وإحسانه

QUSHAYRI:v3p116/r15.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p116/r15.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p116/r15.claim: Warnings make those who fear their Lord shudder, while promises make their skin and hearts soften toward remembrance of God.
QUSHAYRI:v3p116/r15.anchor: تقشعر منه جلود الذين يخشون ربهم } إذا سمعوا آيات الوعيد

QUSHAYRI:v3p116/r16.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p116/r16.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p116/r16.claim: The shuddering and softening may be read as fear and hope, contraction and expansion, awe and intimacy, or divine disclosure and concealment.
QUSHAYRI:v3p116/r16.anchor: ويقال : تقشعر وتلين بالخوف والرجاء ، ويقال بالقبض والبسط ، ويقال بالهيبة والأنس

BURHAN:v2p104/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p104/r5.speaker: الخطابي
BURHAN:v2p104/r5.claim: Al-Khattabi identifies a little-recognized facet of Qur’anic inimitability: its unmatched effect on hearts combines sweetness and delight with awe and majesty.
BURHAN:v2p104/r5.anchor: قال الخطابى وقلت فى إعجاز القرآن وجها آخر ذهب عنه الناس فلا يكاد يعرفه إلا الشاذ فى آحادهم وهو صنيعه بالقلوب وتأثيره فى النفوس

BURHAN:v1p280/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p280/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p280/r2.claim: One explanation of mathani is that the Quran's accounts of earlier scriptures provide a second exposition that clarifies the earlier account.
BURHAN:v1p280/r2.anchor: وأما تسميته مثانى فلأن فيه بيان قصص الكتب الماضية فيكون البيان ثانيا للأول الذى تقدمه فيبين الأول الثانى

BURHAN:v1p280/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p280/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p280/r3.claim: Another view derives mathani from the repeated rulings, stories, and exhortations in the Quran.
BURHAN:v1p280/r3.anchor: وقيل سمى مثانى لتكرار الحكم والقصص والمواعظ فيه

BURHAN:v1p280/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p280/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p280/r4.claim: A further view takes mathani as the name of al-Fatiha alone.

BURHAN:v1p273/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p273/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p273/r2.claim: His catalog continues with the straight path, qayyim, decisive word, great news, best discourse, revelation, spirit, inspiration, and the seven oft-repeated verses.
BURHAN:v1p273/r2.anchor: وسماه الصراط المستقيم فقال ﴿ وأن هذا

BURHAN:v1p273/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p273/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p273/r3.claim: The remaining names include Arabic, connected speech, insight, clarification, knowledge, truth, guidance, wonder, reminder, the firmest bond, similitudes, and truthfulness; Ibn ʿAbbās says the Qur’an is uncreated.
BURHAN:v1p273/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس غير مخلوق وسماه قولا فقال

BURHAN:v2p190/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p190/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p190/r2.claim: There is no contradiction between believers' tranquility at God's remembrance and their trembling when reminded: tranquility comes from settled knowledge and hope, while fear concerns straying and deserved warning.
BURHAN:v2p190/r2.anchor: لأن الاطمئنان إنما يكون عن ثلج القلب وشرح الصدر بمعرفة التوحيد والعلم

BURHAN:v2p190/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p190/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p190/r3.claim: The verse itself combines the responses: settled conviction removes doubt, while the skin's shiver registers fear of deviation and punishment before the heart and skin soften to remembrance.
BURHAN:v2p190/r3.anchor: وقد اجتمعا فى قوله تعالى ﴿ تقشعر منه جلود الذين يخشون ربهم ثم تلين جلودهم وقلوبهم إلى ذكر الله

BURHAN:v2p190/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p190/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p190/r4.claim: He distinguishes those grounded in knowledge and certainty from people who only outwardly profess Islam for protection, whose profession lacks the knowledge that settles the heart and dispels doubt.
BURHAN:v2p190/r4.anchor: الذي يعرض إن كان كلامهم فيمن أظهر الإسلام تعوذا فجعل لهم حكمة دون العلم الموجب لثلج الصدور وانتفاء الشك

BURHAN:v1p244/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p244/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p244/r1.claim: A marfuʿ report divides the Qur’an into seven long suras, the hundred-verse suras, the mathani, and the mufassal, corresponding respectively to the Torah, Gospel, Psalms, and a special gift; it is gharīb and its transmitter Saʿid b. Bashir is weak, though al-Tayalisi also transmits it.
BURHAN:v1p244/r1.anchor: عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال أعطيت السبع الطول مكان التوراة

BURHAN:v1p244/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p244/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p244/r2.claim: The seven long suras begin with al-Baqara and end with Bara’a; Anfal and Bara’a were counted as one and not separated because both descended during the Prophet’s campaigns, and they are called long for their length.
BURHAN:v1p244/r2.anchor: فالسبع الطول أولها البقرة وآخرها براءة لأنهم كانوا يعدون الأنفال وبراءة سورة واحدة

BURHAN:v1p244/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p244/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
BURHAN:v1p244/r3.claim: Saʿid b. Jubayr instead counted the seven long suras as al-Baqara through al-Aʿraf, followed by Yunus.
BURHAN:v1p244/r3.anchor: وحكى عن سعيد بن جبير أنه عد السبع الطول البقرة وآل عمران

BURHAN:v1p244/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p244/r4.speaker: أبو حيان التوحيدي
BURHAN:v1p244/r4.claim: Al-Tiwal is the plural of tulā, by analogy with kubār from kubrā; Abu Hayyan al-Tawhidi calls pronouncing the first vowel with kasra poor usage.
BURHAN:v1p244/r4.anchor: قال أبو حيان التوحيدى وكسر الطاء مرذول

BURHAN:v1p244/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p244/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p244/r5.claim: The miʾun follow the seven long suras and are named for suras exceeding or approaching one hundred verses.
BURHAN:v1p244/r5.anchor: والمئون ما ولى السبع الطول سميت بذلك لأن كل سورة منها تزيد على مائة آية

BURHAN:v1p244/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p244/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p244/r6.claim: Mathani follow the miʾun; all Qur’an suras may be called mathani because reports and stories recur, while “the seven mathani” can mean al-Fatiha, repeated in every rakʿa.
BURHAN:v1p244/r6.anchor: وإنما سمى القرآن كله مثانى لأن الأنباء والقصص تثنى فيه

BURHAN:v1p244/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p244/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p244/r7.claim: The mufassal follows the mathani and comprises short suras; its name is explained by frequent basmala divisions between suras or by having little abrogation, and it ends with Surat al-Nas.
BURHAN:v1p244/r7.anchor: سمى مفصلا لكثرة الفصول التى بين السور ببسم الله الرحمن الرحيم

BURHAN:v1p244/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p244/r8.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p244/r8.claim: Twelve views are given for the beginning of the mufassal; this passage lists al-Jathiya, Muhammad (attributed by al-Mawardi to most scholars), al-Hujurat, and Qaf, with Qaf tied to a report about the Prophet’s hizb divisions.
BURHAN:v1p244/r8.anchor: وفى أوله اثنا عشر قولا أحدها الجاثية ثانيها القتال وعزاه الماوردى للأكثرين

BURHAN:v1p244/r9.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p244/r9.speaker: الخطابي
BURHAN:v1p244/r9.claim: Al-Khattabi cites a report from a Thaqif delegation: the Prophet’s companions divided the Qur’an into hizbs and began the mufassal hizb at Qaf; Ahmad also transmitted it, and al-Mawardi says many Companions related it.
BURHAN:v1p244/r9.anchor: وفيه حديث ذكره الخطابى فى غريبه يرويه عيسى بن يونس

BURHAN:v1p269/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p269/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p269/r1.claim: Surahs can have one or several names: examples include al-Baqara as Fustat al-Qur’an, al-Imran as Tayyiba in the Torah, al-Nahl as the sura of favors, al-Shura, al-Shariʿa, and al-Qital.
BURHAN:v1p269/r1.anchor: قد يكون للسورة اسم وهو كثير وقد يكون لها اسمان كسورة البقرة

BURHAN:v1p269/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p269/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
BURHAN:v1p269/r3.claim: Bara’a is also called al-Tawba, al-Fadiha, and al-Hafira because it exposed hypocrites’ hearts; Ibn Abbas says repeated “and among them” passages made them fear nearly everyone would be named.
BURHAN:v1p269/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس ما زال ينزل ﴿ ومنهم ﴾ حتى ظننا أنه لا يبقى أحد إلا ذكر فيها

BURHAN:v1p269/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p269/r4.speaker: حذيفة
BURHAN:v1p269/r4.claim: Hudhayfa called Bara’a the sura of punishment; Ibn Umar called it al-Mushaqshiqah; al-Harith b. Yazid says it was called al-Mubaʿthira, and it is also known as al-Masura and al-Buhuth.
BURHAN:v1p269/r4.anchor: وقال حذيفة هى سورة العذاب وقال ابن عمر كنا ندعوها المشقشقة

BURHAN:v1p269/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p269/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p269/r5.claim: Al-Fatiha has more than twenty names, including al-Fatiha, Umm al-Kitab, Umm al-Qur’an, the seven mathani, al-Salah, al-Hamd, al-Wafiya, al-Kanz, al-Shafiya, al-Shifa, al-Kafiya, and al-Asas; reports establish several of these titles.
BURHAN:v1p269/r5.anchor: ذكر بعضهم لها بضعة وعشرين اسما الفاتحة وثبت فى الصحيحين وأم الكتاب

BURHAN:v1p269/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p269/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p269/r6.claim: The author asks whether surah names are fixed by revelation or inferred from apt associations; he finds the latter unlikely, since a clever reader could derive many names from every surah’s meanings.
BURHAN:v1p269/r6.anchor: وينبغى البحث عن تعداد الأسامى هل هو توقيفى أو بما يظهر من المناسبات

BURHAN:v2p74/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p74/r1.speaker: عامة المتكلمين
BURHAN:v2p74/r1.claim: Most theologians say all Qur’an must be knowable or its benefit would be lost; they read “the firmly grounded” as coordinated with “Allah” and “they say” as a circumstantial clause, as al-Raghib reports.
BURHAN:v2p74/r1.anchor: قال الراغب ( 1 ) في مقدمة تفسيره وذهب عامة المتكلمين إلى أن كل القرآن يجب أن يكون معلوما

BURHAN:v2p74/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p74/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
BURHAN:v2p74/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says revelation has four aspects: lawful and forbidden matters, what none may be ignorant of, what Arabs know, and interpretation known only to God.
BURHAN:v2p74/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس أنزل الله القرآن على أربعة أوجه حلال وحرام

BURHAN:v2p74/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p74/r3.speaker: بعضهم
BURHAN:v2p74/r3.claim: Some distinguish two senses of mutashabih: obscure meaning due to intermingled doubt, whose intent may remain inaccessible unless God graciously reveals it, or mutually confirming passages whose intent people can know.
BURHAN:v2p74/r3.anchor: وقال بعضهم المتشابه اسم لمعنيين أحدهما لما التبس من المعنى لدخون شبهة بعضه في بعض

BURHAN:v2p74/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p74/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p74/r4.claim: The second sense of mutashabih is that parts agree and confirm one another, as in the description of the Book as mutashabih and mathani.
BURHAN:v2p74/r4.anchor: والثاني اسم لما يوافق بعضه بعضا ويصدقه قوله تعالى ﴿ كتابا متشابها مثاني ﴾

BURHAN:v2p74/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p74/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p74/r5.claim: When the ambiguous can be understood, it encourages scholarly inquiry into subtle meanings, prevents unthinking imitation, tests people, and earns reward; clear passages provide a basis for interpreting it, creating effort and merit.
BURHAN:v2p74/r5.anchor: فلو كان القرآن كله محكما لا يحتاج إلى تأويل لسقطت المحنة وبطل التفاضل

BURHAN:v2p60/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p60/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p60/r6.claim: Tranquility with God’s remembrance comes from knowing divine unity; trembling comes from fearing deviation from guidance, so the settled believers’ skins first shiver and then soften without contradiction.
BURHAN:v2p60/r6.anchor: وقد جمع بينهما في قوله ﴿ تقشعر منه جلود الذين يخشون ربهم ثم تلين جلودهم وقلوبهم إلى ذكر الله ﴾

BURHAN:v1p153/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p153/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p153/r1.claim: The passage catalogs occurrences of the forms نزل and أنزل across Qur’anic suras, including Baqara, Al Imran, Nisa, Anam, Araf, Hijr, Nahl, Isra, Furqan, Shuʿara, Ankabut, Saffat, Zumar, Zukhruf, Muhammad, Hadid, and Mulk.
BURHAN:v1p153/r1.anchor: وفي الزمر ﴿ الله نزل أحسن الحديث ﴾

ITQAN:v4p321/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p321/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p321/r1.claim: The Qur'an has a distinctive effect on hearts: unlike other speech, it reaches the heart with sweetness and pleasure at times, and awe and majesty at others; the source likens this to a mountain trembling before revelation.
ITQAN:v4p321/r1.anchor: وهو صنيعه في القلوب وتأثيره في النفوس فإنك لا تسمع كلاما غير القرآن منظوما ولا منثورا

ITQAN:v3p138/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p138/r13.speaker: الزمخشري
ITQAN:v3p138/r13.claim: Al-Zamakhshari explicitly treats the named subject as restrictive in examples from al-Raʿd, al-Zumar, and al-Ahzab.

ITQAN:v3p5/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p5/r1.speaker: ابن حبيب النيسابوري
ITQAN:v3p5/r1.claim: Ibn Habib al-Nisaburi reports a first view that the whole Qur’an is muhkam, citing the verse that calls it a book whose verses were made firm.
ITQAN:v3p5/r1.anchor: حكى ابن حبيب النيسابوري في المسألة ثلاثة أقوال

ITQAN:v3p5/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p5/r2.speaker: ابن حبيب النيسابوري
ITQAN:v3p5/r2.claim: Ibn Habib reports a second view that the whole Qur’an is mutashabih, its parts resembling one another in truth, veracity, and inimitability.
ITQAN:v3p5/r2.anchor: حكى ابن حبيب النيسابوري في المسألة ثلاثة أقوال

ITQAN:v3p5/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p5/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p5/r3.claim: The author prefers the third view: the Qur’an is divided into muhkam and mutashabih, as stated in 3:7.
ITQAN:v3p5/r3.anchor: الثالث وهو الصحيح إنقسامه إلى محكم ومتشابه للآية المصدر بها

ITQAN:v3p5/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p5/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p5/r4.claim: Muhkam means perfected against defect and inconsistency; mutashabih means its parts resemble each other in truth and inimitability.
ITQAN:v3p5/r4.anchor: والجواب عن الآيتين أن المراد بإحكامه إتقانه وعدم تطرق النقص والاختلاف إليه وبتشابهه كونه يشبه بعضه بعضا

ITQAN:v3p78/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p78/r6.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p78/r6.claim: Reassurance comes from open-hearted knowledge of monotheism; awe comes from fear of straying. The shuddering then softening in 39:23 combines them.
ITQAN:v3p78/r6.anchor: وجوابه أن الطمأنينة تكون بانشراح الصدر بمعرفة التوحيد والوجل يكون عند خوف الزيغ والذهاب عن الهدى

ITQAN:v1p52/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p52/r6.speaker: ابن الجزري
ITQAN:v1p52/r6.claim: Ibn al-Jazari says others add the verse “God has sent down the best discourse” as a Medinan exception.
ITQAN:v1p52/r6.anchor: وزاد غيره ﴿ الله نزل أحسن الحديث ﴾ الآية وحكاه ابن الجزري

ITQAN:v3p161/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p161/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p161/r1.claim: Minimize ellipsis: for those who have not menstruated, the author rejects al-Farisi’s full estimate “their waiting period is three months” and prefers the shorter “likewise.”
ITQAN:v3p161/r1.anchor: ينبغي تقليل المقدر مهما أمكن لتقل مخالفة الأصل

ITQAN:v3p161/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p161/r2.speaker: عز الدين
ITQAN:v3p161/r2.claim: Izz al-Din says an omission should best fit its purpose and be most eloquent; for the Kaaba verse, “its sanctity” is better than “its construction.”
ITQAN:v3p161/r2.anchor: قال الشيخ عز الدين ولا يقدر من المحذوفات إلا أشدها موافقة للغرض وأفصحها

ITQAN:v3p161/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p161/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p161/r3.claim: The author prefers the Kaaba’s sanctity to Abu Ali’s construction, since sanctity fits references to offerings, garlands, and the sacred month more eloquently.
ITQAN:v3p161/r3.anchor: قدر غيره ( حرمة الكعبة ) وهو أولى

ITQAN:v3p161/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p161/r4.speaker: عز الدين
ITQAN:v3p161/r4.claim: When two possible ellipses are good, choose the better because the Qur’an is the best discourse; if one is general and the other explicit, choose the explicit one.
ITQAN:v3p161/r4.anchor: ومهما تردد المحذوف بين الحسن والأحسن وجب تقدير الأحسن لأن الله وصف كتابه بأنه أحسن الحديث

ITQAN:v3p161/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p161/r5.speaker: عز الدين
ITQAN:v3p161/r5.claim: For David and Solomon’s judgment, “in the compensation for the field” is better than “in the affair of the field,” because it is specific rather than general.
ITQAN:v3p161/r5.anchor: لك أن تقدر ( في أمر الحرث ) و ( في تضمين الحرث ) وهو أولى لتعينه

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p371/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p371/r1.speaker: عدي بن الرقاع
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p371/r1.claim: ʿAdī ibn al-Riqāʿ depicts composing a poem as gathering its parts and correcting its unevenness, like a craftsman straightening a spear shaft.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p371/r1.anchor: عدي بن الرقاع ، + الكامل + : ( وقصيدة قد بت أجمع بينها حتى أقوم ميلها وسنادها )

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p371/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p371/r2.speaker: كعب بن زهير
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p371/r2.claim: Kaʿb ibn Zuhayr describes the poet as weaving and correcting verses until their structure softens beyond the reach of ordinary imitation.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p371/r2.anchor: كعب بن زهير ، + الطويل + : ( فمن للقوافي شانها من يحوكها إذا ما ثوى كعب وفوز جرول )

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p371/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p371/r3.speaker: بشار
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p371/r3.claim: Bashshār presents his blindness as overcome through intelligence, while his related verses cast his poetic speech and oratory as courtly splendor and pearls offered to an audience.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p371/r3.anchor: بشار ، + الطويل + : ( عميت جنينا والذكاء من العمى فجئت عجيب الظن للعلم موئلا )

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p371/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p371/r4.speaker: أبو شريح العمير
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p371/r4.claim: Abū Shurayḥ al-ʿUmayrī says he will leave behind poems that delight reciters, with sweet endings and sound construction.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p371/r4.anchor: أبو شريح العمير ، + الوافر + : ( فإن أهلك فقد أبقيت بعدي قوافي تعجب المتمثلينا )

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p371/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p371/r5.speaker: الفرزدق
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p371/r5.claim: Al-Farazdaq boasts that his remarkable verses reach the sun and are associated with him wherever people gather.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p371/r5.anchor: الفرزدق + الوافر + : ( بلغن الشمس حين تكون شرقا ومسقط قرنها من حيث غابا )

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p371/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p371/r6.speaker: ابن ميادة
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p371/r6.claim: Ibn Mayyāda claims that only the poetry of Qays and Khindif is genuine, while other poetry is artificial and affected.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p371/r6.anchor: ابن ميادة ، من + الطويل + : ( فجرنا ينابيع الكلام وبحره فأصبح فيه ذو الرواية يسبح )

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p371/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p371/r7.speaker: عقال بن هاشم القيني
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p371/r7.claim: ʿAqqāl ibn Hāshim al-Qaynī rebuts Ibn Mayyāda: Yemenite tribes pioneered eloquence, taught later poets, and deserve the credit due to predecessors.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p371/r7.anchor: وقال عقال بن هاشم القيني يرد عليه ، + الطويل + : ( ألا بلغ الرماح نقض مقالة بها خطل الرماح أو كان يمزح )

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p371/r8.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p371/r8.speaker: أبو تمام
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p371/r8.claim: Abū Tammām pictures poetic craft as uncovering poetry’s beautiful face and releasing it from its nest.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p371/r8.anchor: أبو تمام ، + الطويل + : ( كشفت قناع الشعر عن حر وجهه وطيرته عن وكره وهو واقع )

KHATTABI:v1p70/r6.author: al-Khaṭṭābī
KHATTABI:v1p70/r6.speaker: author
KHATTABI:v1p70/r6.claim: The Qur’an’s power to move receptive hearers is among its great signs and proofs of its miraculous character, as shown by several verses describing its effects.
KHATTABI:v1p70/r6.anchor: وهو من عظيم آياته , ودلائل معجزاته.

KHATTABI:v1p69/r4.author: al-Khaṭṭābī
KHATTABI:v1p69/r4.speaker: author
KHATTABI:v1p69/r4.claim: A distinctive proof of the Qur’an’s inimitability is its effect on hearts: its sweetness and majesty can turn intended killers among the Arabs into allies and believers.
KHATTABI:v1p69/r4.anchor: قلت في إعجاز القرآن وجها آخر ذهب عنه الناس فلا يكاد يعرفه إلا الشاذ من آحادهم , وذلك صنيعه بالقلوب

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p369/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p369/r2.speaker: سعد
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p369/r2.claim: Saʿd reports that some companions asked the Prophet to tell them stories, after which God revealed that He had sent down the finest discourse.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p369/r2.anchor: عن سعد قالوا: يا رسول الله لو حدثتنا

DAMGHANI:v1p116/r24.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p116/r24.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p116/r24.claim: The best ḥadīth can mean the best stories or narratives.
DAMGHANI:v1p116/r24.anchor: الله نزل أحسن الحديث كتابا يعني أحسن القصص

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p248/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p248/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p248/r1.claim: Ḥadīth and speech are equivalent; it is named for giving the hearer previously unknown information, and ḥudūth is coming into being.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p248/r1.anchor: ( الحديث والكلام واحد ) وسمي الحديث حديثا ، لأنه يحدث للمحدث خبرا لم يكن علمه . والحدوث : كون ما لم يكن .

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p248/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p248/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p248/r2.claim: The source distinguishes ḥadath with ḍamma, a good conversationalist; with fatḥa, a young person; and ḥadath al-nisāʾ with kasra, one who speaks with women.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p248/r2.anchor: ورجل حدث بضم الدال : حسن الحديث . وحدث : بفتحها : طري السن . وهو حدث نساء بكسر الحاء : إذا كان يتحدث إليهن .

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p248/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p248/r3.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p248/r3.claim: One Qurʾanic sense of ḥadīth is the Qurʾan, including the challenge to bring a discourse like it.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p248/r3.anchor: أحدها : القرآن ومنه قوله تعالى في الطور : ﴿ فليأتوا بحديث مثله ﴾

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p248/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p248/r4.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p248/r4.claim: A second sense is narratives or stories; the verse calls the revealed Book the best of narratives.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p248/r4.anchor: والثاني : القصص ، ومنه قوله تعالى في الزمر : ﴿ الله نزل أحسن الحديث كتابا ﴾

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p248/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p248/r5.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p248/r5.claim: A third sense is an instructive tale or cautionary report, as when destroyed peoples were made into stories.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p248/r5.anchor: والثالث : العبرة ، ومنه قوله تعالى في المؤمنين : ﴿ وجعلناهم أحاديث فبعدا لقوم لا يؤمنون ﴾

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p248/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p248/r6.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p248/r6.claim: A fourth sense is a report or telling, as in asking whether people will tell others what God disclosed.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p248/r6.anchor: والرابع : الخبر ، ومنه قوله تعالى في البقرة : ﴿ أتحدثونهم بما فتح الله عليكم ﴾

FARRA:v2p418/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p418/r1.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p418/r1.claim: Mathānī means repeated: the Qur'an repeatedly mentions reward and punishment.
FARRA:v2p418/r1.anchor: أي مكررا يكرر فيه ذكر الثواب والعقاب

FARRA:v2p418/r2.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p418/r2.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p418/r2.claim: Skin shivers with fear when a punishment verse is revealed, then softens when a mercy verse comes.
FARRA:v2p418/r2.anchor: تقشعر خوفا من آية العذاب إذا نزلت (ثم تلين) عند نزول آية رحمة

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p383#2/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p383#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p383#2/r1.claim: The Book's parts resemble one another and do not differ.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p383#2/r1.anchor: {كتابا متشابها} يشبه بعضه بعضا، ولا يختلف.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p383#2/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p383#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p383#2/r2.claim: Mathānī means that reports, stories, and mentions of reward and punishment are repeated within it.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p383#2/r2.anchor: {مثاني} أي تثنى فيه الأنباء والقصص وذكر الثواب والعقاب.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p383#2/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p383#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p383#2/r3.claim: The skin shivers at verses of punishment and softens at verses of mercy.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p383#2/r3.anchor: {تقشعر منه جلود الذين يخشون ربهم} من آية العذاب وتلين من آية الرحمة.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p35#3/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p35#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p35#3/r1.claim: One sense of al-mathānī is the sūras after the miʾūn, which are under one hundred verses; the miʾūn are the first group and these come second.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p35#3/r1.anchor: ما ولي المئين من السور التي هي دون المائة.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p35#3/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p35#3/r2.speaker: قيل
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p35#3/r2.claim: Another view takes al-mathānī to mean all the Qur’an’s sūras, short and long, because its accounts and stories are repeated.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p35#3/r2.anchor: وقد تكون المثاني سور القرآن كلها قصارها وطوالها.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p35#3/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p35#3/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p35#3/r3.claim: The Qur’an is called mathānī because its reports and stories are repeated within it.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p35#3/r3.anchor: وإنما سمي القرآن مثاني لأن الأنباء والقصص تثنى فيه.

MAJAZ:v2p189/r4.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p189/r4.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p189/r4.claim: The parts of the Book confirm one another and resemble one another.
MAJAZ:v2p189/r4.anchor: «متشابها» (23) يصدق بعضه بعضا ويشبه بعضه بعضا..

MAJAZ:v1p5/r1.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p5/r1.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p5/r1.claim: In the dialect that pronounces the hamza, a sūra is a distinct portion of the Quran, explained through what is left over from something.
MAJAZ:v1p5/r1.anchor: مجاز قطعة من القرآن على حدة وفضلة منه لأنه يجعلها

MAJAZ:v1p5/r2.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p5/r2.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p5/r2.claim: An āya is so called because it is connected speech that ends at a break in meaning, with one story following another.
MAJAZ:v1p5/r2.anchor: والآية من القرآن: إنما سميت آية لأنها كلام متصل إلى انقطاعه

MAJAZ:v1p5/r3.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p5/r3.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p5/r3.claim: Al-Ḥamd is called Umm al-Kitāb because it begins the Quran and is recited again in every rakʿa.
MAJAZ:v1p5/r3.anchor: «الحمد لله» تسمى «أم الكتاب» ، لأنه يبدأ بها فى أول القرآن

MAJAZ:v1p5/r4.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p5/r4.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p5/r4.claim: Al-Ḥamd is also called Fātiḥat al-Kitāb because it opens the written codex and is recited at the start of each rakʿa.
MAJAZ:v1p5/r4.anchor: فاتحة الكتاب لأنه يفتتح بها فى المصاحف فتكتب قبل القرآن

MAJAZ:v1p5/r5.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p5/r5.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p5/r5.claim: Al-Miʾūn is the collective name for sūras with about one hundred verses, slightly more or less.
MAJAZ:v1p5/r5.anchor: اسم جامع لما بلغ عددهن مائة آية أو فويق ذلك أو دوينه

MAJAZ:v1p5/r6.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p5/r6.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p5/r6.claim: Al-Mathānī is a collective name for the verses.
MAJAZ:v1p5/r6.anchor: ومن ذلك اسم جامع للآيات وهو: «المثاني» ، وقد فرغنا

MAJAZ:v1p5/r8.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p5/r8.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p5/r8.claim: The first seven sūras, al-Baqara through al-Anfāl, are collectively called al-Sabʿ al-Ṭiwāl, “the seven long ones.”

MAJAZ:v1p5/r9.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p5/r9.speaker: سليمان
MAJAZ:v1p5/r9.claim: Sulayman's poem links Umm al-Kitāb with the seven Mathānī and calls them “the seven long ones,” supporting the sūra grouping.
MAJAZ:v1p5/r9.anchor:
قال سليمان:
نشدتكم بمنزل الفرقان ... أم الكتاب السبع من مثانى ثنين من آي من القرآن ... والسبع سبع الطول الدوانى

MAJAZ:v1p5/r10.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p5/r10.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p5/r10.claim: An unattributed poem groups Quranic portions as the seven long, miʾūn, Mathānī, ṭawāsīm, ḥawāmīm, and mufassal, using words for lengthening, repetition, and separation.
MAJAZ:v1p5/r10.anchor: حلفت بالسبع اللواتى طولت ... وبمئين بعدها قد امئيت

MAJAZ:v1p5/r11.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p5/r11.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p5/r11.claim: He introduces a further poem as evidence that al-Ḥamd is the seven Mathānī; the cited poem itself is not present in this excerpt.
MAJAZ:v1p5/r11.anchor: وقال الشاعر فيما يدل على أن «الحمد» هى السبع المثاني:

NAHHAS:v4p8/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p8/r9.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p8/r9.claim: كتابا is apposition to أحسن; مثاني is an adjective of كتاب and is diptote for its plural pattern.
NAHHAS:v4p8/r9.anchor: على البدل من أحسن ( مثاني ) نعت لكتاب ولم ينصرف لأنه جمع

NAHHAS:v4p8/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p8/r10.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p8/r10.claim: تقشعر منه is accusative as an adjective of كتاب.
NAHHAS:v4p8/r10.anchor: ( تقشعر منه ) في موضع نصب على أنه نعت لكتاب

NAHHAS:v4p8/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p8/r11.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p8/r11.claim: ذلك is a nominative subject referring to fear, hope, and softening hearts; هدى الله is its predicate.
NAHHAS:v4p8/r11.anchor: ( ذلك ) في موضع رفع بالابتداء أي ذلك الخوف والرجاء

SAMIN-DURR:39:23/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:39:23/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:39:23/r1.claim: كتابا is most clearly an apposition to أحسن الحديث; another analysis makes it circumstantial.
SAMIN-DURR:39:23/r1.anchor: أظهرهما: أنه بدل من " أحسن الحديث "

SAMIN-DURR:39:23/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:39:23/r2.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:39:23/r2.claim: Al-Shaykh says the circumstantial view assumes أحسن الحديث definite by annexation, which is disputed.
SAMIN-DURR:39:23/r2.anchor: وكأنه بناء على أن " أحسن الحديث " معرفة لإضافته إلى معرفة، وأفعل التفضيل إذا أضيف إلى معرفة فيه خلاف

SAMIN-DURR:39:23/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:39:23/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:39:23/r3.claim: Even if indefinite, it can license a circumstantial phrase; the elative's annexation is properly definite.
SAMIN-DURR:39:23/r3.anchor: وعلى تقدير كونه نكرة يحسن أيضا أن يكون حالا؛ لأن النكرة متى أضيفت ساغ مجيء الحال منها بلا خلاف. والصحيح أن إضافة أفعل محضة

SAMIN-DURR:39:23/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:39:23/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:39:23/r4.claim: متشابها modifies كتاب and licenses a substantival circumstantial phrase, or كتاب means مكتوب.
SAMIN-DURR:39:23/r4.anchor: وهو المسوغ لمجيء الجامد حالا، أو لأنه في قوة مكتوب

SAMIN-DURR:39:23/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:39:23/r5.speaker: العامة
SAMIN-DURR:39:23/r5.claim: The common reading has open ي; it can be adjective, circumstantial phrase, or transferred specification.
SAMIN-DURR:39:23/r5.anchor: وقرأ العامة " مثاني " بفتح الياء صفة ثانية أو حالا أخرى أو تمييزا منقولا من الفاعلية

SAMIN-DURR:39:23/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:39:23/r6.speaker: هشام عن ابن عامر وأبو بشر
SAMIN-DURR:39:23/r6.claim: Hisham from Ibn Amir and Abu Bishr read silent ي, which may be due to heaviness.
SAMIN-DURR:39:23/r6.anchor: وقرأ هشام عن ابن عامر وأبو بشر بسكونها، وفيها وجهان، أحدهما: أنه من تسكين حرف العلة استثقالا للحركة عليه

SAMIN-DURR:39:23/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:39:23/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:39:23/r7.claim: The reading تطعمون أهاليكم and a poetic line illustrate silent ي.

SAMIN-DURR:39:23/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:39:23/r8.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:39:23/r8.claim: Al-Shaykh parses it as predicate of omitted subject هو.
SAMIN-DURR:39:23/r8.anchor: والثاني: أنه خبر مبتدأ محذوف أي: هو مثاني، كذا ذكره الشيخ.

SAMIN-DURR:39:23/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:39:23/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:39:23/r9.claim: Al-Samin objects that it should have tanwin and lose ي to avoid adjacent sukuns, like مثان and جوار.
SAMIN-DURR:39:23/r9.anchor: فيقال: مثان، كما تقول: هؤلاء جوار

SAMIN-DURR:39:23/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:39:23/r10.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:39:23/r10.claim: A possible answer preserves the form at pause into connected speech, despite rare retention of ي.
SAMIN-DURR:39:23/r10.anchor: ثم أجري الوصل مجرى/ الوقف لكن يعترض عليه

SAMIN-DURR:39:23/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:39:23/r11.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:39:23/r11.claim: تقشعر can modify كتاب, be circumstantial, or stand independently.
SAMIN-DURR:39:23/r11.anchor: وأن تكون حالا منه لاختصاصه بالصفة، وأن تكون مستأنفة

SAMIN-DURR:39:23/r12.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:39:23/r12.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:39:23/r12.claim: اقشعر means skin contracts from fear and hair stands; الاقشعرار and القشعريرة are verbal nouns.
SAMIN-DURR:39:23/r12.anchor: واقشعر جلده إذا تقبض وتجمع من الخوف، وقف شعره. والمصدر الاقشعرار والقشعريرة أيضا

SAMIN-DURR:39:23/r13.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:39:23/r13.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:39:23/r13.claim: مثاني means repeated stories and exhortations or repetition.
SAMIN-DURR:39:23/r13.anchor: و " مثاني " جمع مثنى؛ لأن فيه تثنية القصص والمواعظ، أو جمع مثنى مفعل من التثنية بمعنى التكرير

SAMIN-DURR:39:23/r14.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:39:23/r14.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:39:23/r14.claim: Al-Zamakhshari explains the singular book with plural مثاني because it contains suras and verses.
SAMIN-DURR:39:23/r14.anchor: وإنما وصف " كتاب " وهو مفرد بمثاني، وهو جمع؛ لأن الكتاب مشتمل على سور وآيات

SAMIN-DURR:39:23/r15.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:39:23/r15.speaker: قيل
SAMIN-DURR:39:23/r15.anchor: وقيل: ثم موصوف محذوف أي: فصولا مثاني حذف للدلالة عليه

ZAJJAJ:v4p351/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p351/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p351/r1.claim: The best discourse is the Quran; its passages resemble one another in excellence and wisdom, with no contradiction.
ZAJJAJ:v4p351/r1.anchor: يعني القرآن، ومعنى متشابها، يشابه بعضه بعضا في الفضل والحكمة، لا تناقض فيه

ZAJJAJ:v4p351/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p351/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p351/r2.claim: Kitāban is accusative as a substitute for aḥsan al-ḥadīth.
ZAJJAJ:v4p351/r2.anchor: و (كتابا) منصوب على البدل من (أحسن الحديث)

ZAJJAJ:v4p351/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p351/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p351/r3.claim: Mathānī is an accusative adjective of kitāban and is diptote because it is a plural not shaped like a singular.
ZAJJAJ:v4p351/r3.anchor: وقوله: (مثاني) من نعت قوله (كتابا) منصوب على النعت

ZAJJAJ:v4p351/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p351/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p351/r4.claim: When verses of punishment are mentioned, the skins of those who fear God shiver.
ZAJJAJ:v4p351/r4.anchor: يقول: إذا ذكرت آيات العذاب اقشعرت جلود الخاشعين لله

ZAJJAJ:v4p351/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p351/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p351/r5.claim: When verses of mercy are mentioned, their skins and hearts soften.
ZAJJAJ:v4p351/r5.anchor: إذا ذكرت آيات الرحمة لأنت جلودهم وقلوبهم

ZAJJAJ:v4p351/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p351/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p351/r6.claim: Their fear of God and His punishment, together with hope for His mercy, is guidance granted by God.
ZAJJAJ:v4p351/r6.anchor: يقول: الذي وهبه الله لهم من خشيته وخوف عذابه ورجاء رحمته هدي الله

ASAD-NOTES:39:23#n27/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:39:23#n27/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:39:23#n27/r1.claim: The form nazzala conveys gradual, continuing revelation, so Asad uses the present tense for God's ongoing bestowal from on high.
ASAD-NOTES:39:23#n27/r1.anchor: The verbal form nazzala indicates both gradualness and continuity in the process of divine revelation

ASAD-NOTES:39:23#n28/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:39:23#n28/r1.speaker: Zamakhshari
ASAD-NOTES:39:23#n28/r1.claim: Asad prefers Zamakhshari's contextual sense of mathani as statements of truth repeated in manifold forms.
ASAD-NOTES:39:23#n28/r1.anchor: mathani (p1. of mathna), as explained by Zamakhshari in his commentary on the above verse

ASAD-NOTES:39:23#n28/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:39:23#n28/r2.speaker: Razi
ASAD-NOTES:39:23#n28/r2.claim: Razi offers the alternative that mathani means pairing statements, reflecting the Qur'an's many polarities such as command and prohibition, reward and punishment, and light and darkness.
ASAD-NOTES:39:23#n28/r2.anchor: Another possible meaning, preferred by Razi, is "pairing its statements", i.e., referring to the polarity stressed in all Qur'anic teachings

ASAD-NOTES:39:23#n28/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:39:23#n28/r3.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:39:23#n28/r3.claim: For the Qur'an's inner consistency, Asad points readers to 4:82 and 25:32 and their notes.
ASAD-NOTES:39:23#n28/r3.anchor: As regards the inner consistency of the Qur'an, see also 4:82 and 25:32, as well as the corresponding notes.

ASAD-NOTES:39:23#n29/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:39:23#n29/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:39:23#n29/r1.claim: The alternative rendering "He guides therewith whomever He wills" is also syntactically correct.
ASAD-NOTES:39:23#n29/r1.anchor: Or: "He guides therewith whomever He wills", either of these two formulations being syntactically correct.

ASAD-NOTES:39:23#n30/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:39:23#n30/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:39:23#n30/r1.claim: Asad refers readers to his note 4 on 14:4 for this statement about divine misguidance.

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2#2/f7.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2#2/f7.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2#2/f7.claim: The Quran's precise, varied word choices still form an integrated literary whole: each expression fits its local context and harmonizes with its other occurrences.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2#2/f7.anchor: ومع هذا الاستعمال الرياضي الإحصائي العجيب للألفاظ فالتعبير القرآني هو في قمة الأدب والفن

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2#2/f13.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2#2/f13.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2#2/f13.claim: He cites 39:23 for the Quran's devotional effect: its repeated, coherent discourse makes reverent believers' skins shiver, then their skins and hearts soften toward God's remembrance.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2#2/f13.anchor: تَقْشَعِرُّ مِنْهُ جُلُودُ الذين يَخْشَوْنَ رَبَّهُمْ ثُمَّ تَلِينُ جُلُودُهُمْ وَقُلُوبُهُمْ إلى ذِكْرِ الله

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2#2/f14.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2#2/f14.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2#2/f14.claim: Quranic expression has been studied through its imagery, sound and rhythm, word choice, and the coherence of its sūras, verses, openings, and endings; these studies reveal a tightly connected composition.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2#2/f14.anchor: ودُرسَ تناسبُ سورهِ سورةً سورة، وتناسب آياته آية آية، وتناسب فواتح السور وخواتمها

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2#2/f15.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2#2/f15.speaker: الفخر الرازي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2#2/f15.claim: Al-Razi says the Quran is like one sūra because its parts connect to one another, indeed like one verse.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2#2/f15.anchor: كما قال الفخر الرازي: إن القرآن كالسورة الواحدة لاتصال بعضه ببعض بل هي كالآية الواحدة

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p541/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p541/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p541/r1.claim: The Qur’an is a great favour: receptive people are moved by it, while the stone-hearted are deprived of it and face destruction like messenger-denying nations.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p541/r1.anchor: The stone-hearted, however, will be deprived from the Qur’ān and will face the punishment of destruction

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p541/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p541/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p541/r2.claim: The Qur’an presents all facts in the best style; its opponents will be taken to task, while those accepting its truth fear God and receive the best reward.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p541/r2.anchor: The Qur’ān has delineated all the facts in the best of styles. Those who are opposing it will be taken to task.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p544/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p544/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p544/r4.claim: The Qur’an’s parts are uniform in their basic teachings, though its groups and sūrahs differ in style and central themes; this unity manifests its majesty.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p544/r4.anchor: However, in spite of this difference, there is such all-embracing uniformity in it that from whichever instance it is viewed

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p544/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p544/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p544/r5.claim: This form of revelation serves teaching by letting readers observe the facts to which the Qur’an invites them from several angles.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p544/r5.anchor: a reader is made to observe through various angles all the facts to which the Qur’ān invites its addressees.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p545/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p545/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p545/r1.claim: “Mathānī” refers to the Qur’anic sūrahs occurring in pairs, a reading discussed at 15:87 and valued for teaching.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p545/r1.anchor: this word refers to the occurrence of the Qur’ānic sūrahs in pairs.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p545/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p545/r2.speaker: People who think that the word means “something which is repeated often”
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p545/r2.claim: The author rejects the view that “mathānī” means something often repeated, calling it contrary to linguistic principles and parallel constructions.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p545/r2.anchor: People who think that the word means “something which is repeated often” are mistaken and their view is against linguistic principles and parallel constructions.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p545/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p545/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p545/r3.claim: “Julūd” can mean the body’s skin or hair, with Arabic using a part for the whole and the whole for a part.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p545/r3.anchor: The word ُودُلُج means the hair on the skin of the body as well as the body itself.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p545/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p545/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p545/r4.claim: Because “talīnu” is followed by “ilā,” it includes the sense of inclining toward.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p545/r4.anchor: Since the word  ُنیِلَت is followed by the preposition  ىَلِإِit encompasses the meaning of لْیِمَت inclined to).

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p545/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p545/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p545/r5.claim: The Qur’an’s sūrahs differ while refreshing one another’s themes; the Torah’s successive books lack such connection, a discontinuity related to its loss or alteration.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p545/r5.anchor: On the other hand, the case of the Torah is very different.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p545/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p545/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p545/r6.claim: The Qur’an so profoundly affects those who fear God that their hairs stand on end; lack of effect signals a heart devoid of God’s light and hardened.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p545/r6.anchor: the hairs on their skins stand on their ends.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p545/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p545/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p545/r7.claim: The Qur’an’s softening makes bodies and hearts tender and turn toward God.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p545/r7.anchor: induces their bodies and hearts to become tender and turn towards God.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p545/r8.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p545/r8.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p545/r8.claim: Bodily tenderness means that no arrogance or haughtiness remains.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p545/r8.anchor: what is implied by the tenderness of the bodies is that no speck of arrogance and haughtiness remains in them.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p546/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p546/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p546/r1.claim: Fear and humility are visible in believers’ gait and gestures, while the arrogant stiffen their bodies and stamp as they walk.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p546/r1.anchor: people who have the fear of God in them are humble and down to earth. The affects of this humility are evident in their gait

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p546/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p546/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p546/r2.claim: The demonstrative ذَٰلِكَ refers to the Qur’an, the guidance God revealed and uses to guide whom He wills.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p546/r2.anchor: In other words, this Qur’ān is the guidance revealed by God; through it, He guided whomsoever He wanted.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p546/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p546/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p546/r3.claim: God follows an established practice in granting guidance according to who is worthy of receiving it; those unworthy remain deprived.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p546/r3.anchor: What is implied is that the Almighty adheres to a certain established practice regarding giving guidance.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p546/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p546/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p546/r4.claim: In keeping with that practice, no one can guide a person unworthy of guidance.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p546/r4.anchor: in accordance with the above mentioned practice of God no one can guide a person who is not worthy of being guided.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p546/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p546/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p546/r5.claim: The statement also assures the Prophet that he need not fret over such people.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p546/r5.anchor: These words actually sound an assurance to the Prophet (sws): he should not fret over such people.

QIRAAT-ER:39:23:37#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:39:23:37#1/r1.speaker: Yaʿqūb
QIRAAT-ER:39:23:37#1/r1.claim: A Yaʿqūb-style performance preserves a hādī-like form before pause or continuation while the standard surface has hādin, affecting final-glide and pause texture.
QIRAAT-ER:39:23:37#1/r1.anchor: Canonical Ya'qub-style performance preserves a hādī-like form before pause/continuation

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p172/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p172/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p172/r1.claim: Qatāda says the Qurʾān is consistent in its lawful and forbidden rulings, with each verse resembling another and each letter resembling another.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p172/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ كتابا متشابها ﴾ قال متشابها في حلاله وحرامه لا يختلف منه شيء

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p172/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p172/r2.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p172/r2.claim: Qatāda glosses “mathānī” as a text God has repeated.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p172/r2.anchor: قال معمر وقال قتادة قد ثناه الله

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p172/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p172/r3.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p172/r3.claim: Qatāda describes God's close servants as shuddering, weeping, and finding calm in God's remembrance; he says loss of reason and fainting belong to innovators and are from Satan.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p172/r3.anchor: قال تلا قتادة ﴿ تقشعر منه جلود الذين يخشون ربهم ثم تلين جلودهم وقلوبهم إلى ذكر الله ﴾ قال هذا نعت أولياء الله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p178#2/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p178#2/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p178#2/r7.claim: القشعريرة is skin contraction; fear makes the hair stand, a figure for intense fear.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p178#2/r7.anchor: القشعريرة: تقبض الجلد، يقال: اقشعر جلده من الخوف: وقف شعره، وهو مثل في شدة الخوف.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p194/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p194/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p194/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that companions asked the Prophet for good accounts and stories of the past, after which this verse was revealed.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p194/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، أن قوما من الصحابة قالوا: يا رسول الله، حدثنا بأحاديث حسان، وبأخبار الدهر، فنزل: الله نزل أحسن الحديث

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p194/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p194/r2.speaker: ابن مسعود
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p194/r2.claim: Ibn Masud reports that the companions gathered in Mecca and asked the Prophet to tell them something, prompting the revelation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p194/r2.anchor: وعن ابن مسعود، أن الصحابة ملأوا مكة، فقالوا له: حدثنا، فنزلت.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p194/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p194/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p194/r3.claim: Beginning with God's name and making it the topic before the verb exalts the revelation, as topicalizing the king does in الملك أكرم فلانا.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p194/r3.anchor: والابتداء باسم الله، وإسناد نزل لضميره مبنيا عليه فيه تفخيم للمنزل ورفع منه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p194/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p194/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p194/r4.claim: The author cites the same elevated word order in God's choosing messengers from among the angels.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p194/r4.anchor: كقوله: الله يصطفي من الملائكة رسلا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p194/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p194/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p194/r5.claim: كتابا is an appositive to أحسن الحديث.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p194/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p194/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p194/r6.claim: Al-Zamakhshari allows كتابا to be a state because أحسن الحديث may count as definite by annexation; grammarians disagree whether such superlative annexation is fully definite.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p194/r6.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: ويحتمل أن يكون حالا.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p194/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p194/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p194/r7.claim: The Qur'an's parts resemble one another: its meanings do not contradict, and its eloquent, balanced wording defeats eloquent speakers.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p194/r7.anchor: ومتشابها: مطلق في مشابهة بعضه بعضا. فمعانيه متشابهة، لا تناقض فيها ولا تعارض

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p194/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p194/r8.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p194/r8.claim: The majority read مثاني with fatḥa on the yāʾ.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p194/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p194/r9.speaker: هشام، وابن عامر، وأبو بشر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p194/r9.claim: Hisham, Ibn Amir, and Abu Bishr read مثاني with a still yāʾ; it may be a predicate of an omitted noun or accusative, with sukūn used to avoid a heavy vowel.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p194/r9.anchor: وهشام، وابن عامر، وأبو بشر: بسكون الياء، فاحتمل أن يكون خبر مبتدأ محذوف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p194/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p194/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p194/r10.claim: مثاني appears to be the plural of مثنى: the Qur'an repeats paired stories, rulings, doctrines, promises, and warnings; another view refers to repetition in prayer.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p194/r10.anchor: ومثاني يظهر أنه جمع مثنى، ومعناه: موضع تثنية القصص والأحكام والعقائد والوعد والوعيد.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p194/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p194/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p194/r11.claim: The singular كتاب is described by a plural because it contains many details, just as one says the Qur'an is chapters and verses; the implied construction is كتابا متشابها فصولا مثاني.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p194/r11.anchor: ووصف المفرد بالجمع، لأن فيه تفاصيل، وتفاصيل الشيء جملته. ألا ترى أنك تقول: القرآن سور وآيات؟

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p194/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p194/r12.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p194/r12.claim: Al-Zamakhshari allows a collective plural construction like برمة أعشار, or a specification derived from the subject, متشابها مثانيه.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p194/r12.anchor: وأجاز الزمخشري أن يكون من باب برمة أعشار وثوب أخلاق، وأن يكون تمييزا عن متشابها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p194/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p194/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p194/r13.claim: Repetition makes the message firm in souls, which are naturally reluctant to hear admonition and advice.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p194/r13.anchor: وفائدة تثنيته وتكرره رسوخه في النفوس، إذ هي أنفر شيء عن سماع الوعظ والنصيحة.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p194/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p194/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p194/r14.claim: The author prefers literal skin-shivering, a palpable bodily response caused by the heart's emotional effect.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p194/r14.anchor: والظاهر حمل القشعريرة على الحقيقة، إذ هو موجود عند الخشية، محسوس يدركه الإنسان من نفسه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p194/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p194/r15.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p194/r15.claim: Another view treats the shivering as an image for overwhelming fear when listeners hear verses of warning recited.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p194/r15.anchor: وقيل: هو تمثيل تصوير لإفراط خشيتهم

ALUSI-FULL:v23p258#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p258#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p258#2/r1.claim: The best discourse is the noble Quran.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p258#2/r1.anchor: هو القرآن الكريم وكونه حديثا بمعنى كونه كلاما محدثا به

ALUSI-FULL:v23p258#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p258#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p258#2/r2.claim: Calling the Quran hadith means discourse that is spoken of, not speech newly created in opposition to the eternal.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p258#2/r2.anchor: وكونه حديثا بمعنى كونه كلاما محدثا به لا بمعنى كونه مقابلا للقديم

ALUSI-FULL:v23p258#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p258#2/r3.speaker: الأشاعرة
ALUSI-FULL:v23p258#2/r3.claim: Asharites who hold that verbal speech is created and necessarily linked to the eternal apply descriptions implying createdness to that verbal speech.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p258#2/r3.anchor: ومن قال بالتلازم من الأشاعرة القائلين بحدوث الكلام اللفظي جعل الأوصاف الدالة على الحدوث لذلك الكلام

ALUSI-FULL:v23p258#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p258#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p258#2/r4.claim: Alusi also allows “hadith” to be applied to the Quran by way of matching expression, or mushakala.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p258#2/r4.anchor: وجوز أن يكون إطلاق الحديث هنا على القرآن من باب المشاكلة

ALUSI-FULL:v23p258#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p258#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v23p258#2/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that some Companions asked the Prophet for beautiful stories and accounts of earlier times, after which this verse was revealed.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p258#2/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس أن قوما من الصحابة قالوا : يا رسول الله حدثنا بأحاديث حسان وبأخبار الدهر فنزلت

ALUSI-FULL:v23p258#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p258#2/r6.speaker: ابن مسعود
ALUSI-FULL:v23p258#2/r6.claim: Ibn Masud reports that the Companions tired of admonition and asked the Prophet to tell them something; the verse directed them to fresh recitation and listening to the Quran.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p258#2/r6.anchor: وعن ابن مسعود أن الصحابة ملوا ملة فقالوا له عليه الصلاة والسلام حدثنا فنزلت أي إراشادا لهم

ALUSI-FULL:v23p258#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p258#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p258#2/r7.claim: Making God's name the subject and “revealed” its predicate magnifies the Quran, attests its excellence and divine source, and emphasizes that no one else could produce its like.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p258#2/r7.anchor: وفي إيقاع اسم الله تعالى مبتدأ وبناء ( نزل ) عليه تفخيم لأحسن الحديث واستشهاد على أحسنيته وتأكيد لاستناده إلى الله عز وجل

ALUSI-FULL:v23p258#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p258#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p258#2/r8.claim: Because God is unsurpassed in perfection, nothing else has comparable perfection; the most perfect discourse must necessarily come from the most perfect speaker.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p258#2/r8.anchor: لأن أكمل الحديث إنما يكون من أكمل متكلم ضرورة

ALUSI-FULL:v23p258#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p258#2/r9.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v23p258#2/r9.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says this construction conveys exclusivity, which he sees as compatible with reverent awareness.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p258#2/r9.anchor: مذهب الزمخشري أن مثل هذا التركيب يفيد الحصر وأنه لا تنافي بينه وبين التقوى جمعا

ALUSI-FULL:v23p258#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p258#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p258#2/r10.claim: “A book” may be apposition to “the best discourse” or a circumstantial accusative, as al-Zamakhshari allows.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p258#2/r10.anchor: كتابا ( بدل من ( أحسن الحديث ) أو حال منه كما قال الزمخشري

ALUSI-FULL:v23p258#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p258#2/r11.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v23p258#2/r11.claim: Alusi rejects Abu Hayyan's assumption that the circumstantial reading depends on the comparative's genitive making it definite; any genitive construction suffices.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p258#2/r11.anchor: وليس مبنيا على القول بأن إضافة أفعل التفضيل تفيده تعريفا كما ظن أبو حيان فإن مطلق الإضافة كافية في صحة الحالية

ALUSI-FULL:v23p258#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p258#2/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p258#2/r12.claim: The noun can function circumstantially because it is qualified by “mutashabih,” or because it carries the force of “written.”
ALUSI-FULL:v23p258#2/r12.anchor: ووقوعه حالا مع كونه اسما لا صفة إما لوصفه بقوله تعالى ( متشابها ( أو لكونه في قوة مكتوبا

ALUSI-FULL:v23p258#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p258#2/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p258#2/r13.claim: The Quran's meanings resemble one another in soundness, precision, truth, benefit in worldly and afterlife affairs, while its eloquent wording and arrangement mutually echo inimitably.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p258#2/r13.anchor: والمراد بكونه متشابها هنا معانيه في الصحة والإحكام والإبتناء على الحق والصدق واستتباع منافع الخلق في المعاد والمعاش

ALUSI-FULL:v23p258#2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p258#2/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p258#2/r14.claim: Alusi likens this mutual excellence to the Arab description of a perfectly beautiful face as “mutanasif,” as though each part were evenly fair.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p258#2/r14.anchor: وما أشبه هذا بقول العرب في الوجه الكامل حسنا وجه متناصف

ALUSI-FULL:v23p258#2/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p258#2/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p258#2/r15.claim: “Mathani” is another adjective or circumstantial qualifier for the book; as an irregular plural of muthanna, it means repeated in rulings, exhortations, and stories.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p258#2/r15.anchor: ( مثاني ( صفة أخرى لكتابا أو حال أخرى منه وهو جمع مثنى بضم الميم وفتح النون المشددة على خلاف القياس

ALUSI-FULL:v23p258#2/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p258#2/r16.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v23p258#2/r16.claim: One view says the Quran is called “mathani” because it is repeated in recitation.

ALUSI-FULL:v23p258#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p258#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p258#3/r1.claim: “Mathani” may be a plural of muthanna, from duality as repetition: a turn after a turn; the dual is itself the first degree of repetition and may be pluralized for emphasis.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p258#3/r1.anchor: وجوز أن يكون جمع مثنى بالفتح مخففا من التثنية بمعنى التكرير والإعادة

ALUSI-FULL:v23p258#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p258#3/r2.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v23p258#3/r2.claim: Another derivation is from praise: the verses contain praise of God or, through their eloquence and inimitability, praise their speaker; Alusi finds this less fitting beside “mutashabih” unless the latter sense is intended.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p258#3/r2.anchor: وقيل : جمع لاشتمال آياته على الثناء على الله تعالى أو لأنها تثنى ببلاغتها وإعجازها على المتكلم بها

ALUSI-FULL:v23p258#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p258#3/r3.speaker: الكشف
ALUSI-FULL:v23p258#3/r3.claim: Al-Kashf finds the form best derived from praise or repetition: muthanna can be a verbal noun made adjectival, or a noun transferred to an adjective for emphasis, like a land of predators.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p258#3/r3.anchor: وفي الكشف إلا قيس بحسب اللفظ

ALUSI-FULL:v23p258#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p258#3/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p258#3/r4.claim: As an adjective for the book, “mathani” describes its details, which constitute the whole: the Quran is composed of portions, chapters, verses, rulings, admonitions, and stories.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p258#3/r4.anchor: ووقوعه صفة لكتاب باعتبار تفاصيله وتفاصيل الشيء هي جملته لا غير

ALUSI-FULL:v23p258#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p258#3/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p258#3/r5.claim: It may instead be an accusative of specification transformed from the subject: the underlying construction is “its details resemble one another”; it is indefinite by the usual pattern.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p258#3/r5.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون تمييزا محولا عن الفاعل والأصل متشابها مثانيه فحول ونكر لأن الأكثر التنكير

ALUSI-FULL:v23p258#3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p258#3/r6.speaker: هشام وأبو بشر
ALUSI-FULL:v23p258#3/r6.claim: Hisham and Abu Bishr read “mathani” with a quiescent ya, either as the predicate of an omitted subject or as an accusative with ya quiescence from a dialect that drops its vowel.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p258#3/r6.anchor: وقرأ هشام وأبو بشر ( مثاني ) بسكون الياء فاحتمل أن يكون خبر مبتدأ محذوف

ALUSI-FULL:v23p258#3/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p258#3/r7.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v23p258#3/r7.claim: Some parse “the skins shiver” as an adjective or circumstantial clause for the book, which already has a qualifying description.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p258#3/r7.anchor: قيل صفة لكتابا أو حال منه لتخصصه بالصفة

ALUSI-FULL:v23p258#3/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p258#3/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p258#3/r8.claim: Alusi prefers to start a new sentence here: it describes the Quran's visible effects on its listeners after describing the book itself and confirms its excellence.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p258#3/r8.anchor: وقال بعض : الأظهر أنه استئناف مسوق لبيان آثاره الظاهرة في سامعيه بعد بيان أوصافه في نفسه

ALUSI-FULL:v23p258#3/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p258#3/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p258#3/r9.claim: Qashʿarīrah is severe contraction; the word derives from qashʿ, dry hide, with an added ra to form a quadriliteral and signal extra meaning, as skin contracts and hair stands from sudden fear.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p258#3/r9.anchor: وأقشعرار التقبض يقال اقشعر الجلد إذا تقبض تقبضا شديدا وتركيبه من القشع وهو الأديم اليابس قد ضم إليه الراء

ALUSI-FULL:v23p258#3/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p258#3/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p258#3/r10.claim: The description pictures the believers' fear by naming its tangible bodily signs; Alusi calls this figurative exemplification, even if it also operates through metonymy.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p258#3/r10.anchor: والمراد تصوير خوفهم بذكر لوازمه المحسوسة ويطلق عليه التمثيل وإن كان من باب الكناية

ALUSI-FULL:v23p259/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p259/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p259/r1.claim: Alusi records an alternative calling the description a true parable that compares one state with another; he prefers the account that figures fear through its tangible effects because the story-to-story metaphor is strained.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p259/r1.anchor: هو تصوير للخوف بذكر آثاره وتشبيه حالة بحالة فيكون تمثيلا حقيقة والأول أحسن

ALUSI-FULL:v23p259/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p259/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p259/r2.claim: Alusi takes the bodily change as actually occurring: warning verses make hearers fear and their skins shiver; hearing promises of mercy turns fear into hope and dread into longing.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p259/r2.anchor: بيان حصول تلك الحالة وعروضها لهم بطريق التحقيق والمعنى أنهم إذا سمعوا القرآن

ALUSI-FULL:v23p259/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p259/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p259/r3.claim: Their skins and hearts then become quiet and settled through remembrance of God's mercy, which is unstated because mercy is the first thing that comes to mind when God is mentioned.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p259/r3.anchor: أي ساكنة مطمئنة إلى ذكر رحمته تعالى وإنما لم يصرح بالرحمة إيذانا بأنها أول ما يخطر بالبال

ALUSI-FULL:v23p259/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p259/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p259/r4.claim: The implied mercy is supported by the report, “My mercy preceded My anger.”
ALUSI-FULL:v23p259/r4.anchor: كما يرشد إليه خبر سبقت رحمتي غضبي

ALUSI-FULL:v23p259/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p259/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p259/r5.claim: He mentions hearts with the softening because fear belongs to the heart and hearts can soften, while skin shivering cannot be predicated of hearts.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p259/r5.anchor: وذكر القلوب لتقدم الخشية التي هي من عوارضها ولعله إنما لم تذكر هناك على طرز ذكرها هنا لأنها لا توصف بالإقشعرار وتوصف باللين

ALUSI-FULL:v23p259/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p259/r6.speaker: عبد الله بن عروة بن الزبير
ALUSI-FULL:v23p259/r6.claim: Ibn Urwa asked his grandmother Asma how the Prophet's Companions behaved when reciting Quran; she said their eyes wept and skins shivered as described, and she sought God's protection from Satan when told some people fainted.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p259/r6.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عروة بن الزبير قال : قلت لجدتي أسماء

ALUSI-FULL:v23p259/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p259/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p259/r7.claim: The verse describes shivering and subsequent calm; it does not describe swooning, ecstatic display, or clapping, which Alusi condemns in some practitioners.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p259/r7.anchor: وليس في الآية أكثر من نعت أوليائه باقشعرار الجلود من القرآن ثم سكونهم إلى رحمته عز وجل وليس فيها نعتهم بالصعق والتواجد والصفق

ALUSI-FULL:v23p259/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p259/r8.speaker: عبد الله بن الزبير
ALUSI-FULL:v23p259/r8.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr told his mother Asma that people remembering God trembled and fainted; she told him not to sit with them and asked whether they thought themselves more fearful than the Prophet, Abu Bakr, and Umar, whom she had seen recite without this.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p259/r8.anchor: عن عامر عن عبد الله بن الزبير قال : جئت أمي فقلت وجدت قوما

ALUSI-FULL:v23p259/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p259/r9.speaker: ابن عمر
ALUSI-FULL:v23p259/r9.claim: Ibn Umar, seeing someone collapse while hearing Quran, said that they fear God without collapsing and that Satan enters such people.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p259/r9.anchor: وقال ابن عمر وقد رأى ساقطا من سماع القرآن فقال إنا لنخشى الله تعالى وما نسقط : هؤلاء

ALUSI-FULL:v23p259/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p259/r10.speaker: قتادة
ALUSI-FULL:v23p259/r10.claim: Qatada calls this the description of God's allies: their skins shiver, eyes weep, and hearts find rest in remembrance; God does not describe them as losing reason or fainting, which he associates with innovators and Satan.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p259/r10.anchor: عن قتادة أنه قال في الآية هذا نعت أولياء الله تعالى قال : تقشعر جلودهم وتبكي أعينهم

ALUSI-FULL:v23p259/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p259/r11.speaker: ابن جبير
ALUSI-FULL:v23p259/r11.claim: Ibn Jubayr says swooning is from Satan.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p259/r11.anchor: عن ابن جبير : قال الصعقة من الشيطان

ALUSI-FULL:v23p259/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p259/r12.speaker: ابن سيرين
ALUSI-FULL:v23p259/r12.claim: Ibn Sirin proposes testing people who faint at Quran recitation by seating one against a wall with legs extended and reading the whole Quran; if he throws himself down, he is truthful.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p259/r12.anchor: قال ابن سيرين : بيننا وبين هؤلاء الذين يصرعون عند قراءة القرآن أن يحمل أحدهم على حائط باسطا رجليه

ALUSI-FULL:v23p259/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p259/r13.speaker: مشايخهم
ALUSI-FULL:v23p259/r13.claim: Some Sufi shaykhs explain swooning as weak hearts unable to bear spiritual influx; Alusi counters that it signals deficiency, since a completed wayfarer grows firm and strong like the Companions.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p259/r13.anchor: ويقول مشايخهم : إن ذلك لضعف القلوب عن تحمل الوارد وليس فاعلو ذلك في الكمال كالصحابة أهل الصدر الأول

ALUSI-FULL:v23p259/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p259/r14.speaker: مشايخهم
ALUSI-FULL:v23p259/r14.claim: The Sufi defense says the verse affirms shivering and softening without excluding other states, and its relative clause describes firmly established saints rather than every believer.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p259/r14.anchor: ويقولون : ليس في الآية أكثر من إثبات الإقشعرار واللين وليس فيها نفي أن يعتريهم حال آخر بل في الآية إشعار بأن المذكور حال الراسخين الكاملين

ALUSI-FULL:v23p259/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p259/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p259/r15.claim: The relative clause indicates people deeply established in recognizable fear, so the description need not be exclusive or define others' states; involuntary reactions like sneezing need no blame, as Ibn Sirin's remark supports, and Alusi prays for the Companions' grace.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p259/r15.anchor: ومقتضى معلومية الصلة أن لهم رسوخا في الخشية حتى يعلموا بها فلا يلزم من كون حالهم ما ذكر ليس إلا على فرض دلالتها على الحصر

ALUSI-FULL:v23p259/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p259/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p259/r16.claim: “That” points to the Quran whose qualities were just described; God guides by it whom He wills by enabling reflection on its proofs of truth and divine origin.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p259/r16.anchor: شواهد الحقية ودلائل كونه من عنده عز وجل

ALUSI-FULL:v23p259/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p259/r17.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p259/r17.claim: Alusi also considers making the pronoun in “wills” refer to the person: God guides whoever wills God's guidance, but he finds this reading weak.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p259/r17.anchor: وجوز أن يكون ضمير ( يشاء ) لمن والمعنى يهدي الله تعالى من يشاء هداية الله تعالى وليس بذاك

ALUSI-FULL:v23p260/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p260/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p260/r1.claim: God creates misguidance in the person as he turns away from what directs him to truth through a bad disposition; no guide can rescue him from error.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p260/r1.anchor: أي يخلق سبحانه فيه الضلال إعراضه عما يرشده إلى الحق بسوء استعداده فما له من هاد

ALUSI-FULL:v23p260/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p260/r2.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v23p260/r2.claim: An alternative takes “that” to mean the shivering and softening just described, whose effect is guidance; whoever is unaffected because of hardness and persistent sin has no guide able to influence him. Alusi dismisses this reading.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p260/r2.anchor: وقيل : الإشارة إلى المذكور من الإقشعرار واللين والمعنى ذلك الذي ذكر من الخشية والرجاء أثر هداه تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v1p26/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p26/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p26/r1.claim: Reports that appear to make Quranic arrangement a matter of independent judgment are unreliable and contradicted by abundant evidence.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p26/r1.anchor: وما يدل بظاهره من الآثار على أنه إجتهادي معارض ساقط عن درجة الإعتبار

ALUSI-FULL:v1p26/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p26/r2.speaker: عبدالله بن الزبير عن أبيه
ALUSI-FULL:v1p26/r2.claim: Al-Harith brought the final two Bara'a verses; al-Zubayr and Umar testified the Prophet had recited them, and Umar said three verses would have formed a separate sura.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p26/r2.anchor: بسنده عن عبدالله بن الزبير عن أبيه قال أتى الحرث بن خزيمة بهاتين الآيتين

ALUSI-FULL:v1p26/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p26/r3.speaker: أبي
ALUSI-FULL:v1p26/r3.claim: Ubayy said that after the compilers mistook 9:127 for the final revelation, the Prophet recited him the last two verses of Bara'a.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p26/r3.anchor: فقال أبي أن رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم أقرأني بعد هذا آيتين

ALUSI-FULL:v1p26/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p26/r4.speaker: الجمهور
