ALUSI-FULL:v1p26/r4.claim: The majority hold that the arrangement of suras is divinely prescribed rather than the result of independent judgment.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p26/r4.anchor: في كونه إجتهاديا أو توقيفيا خلاف والجمهور على الثاني

ALUSI-FULL:v1p26/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p26/r5.speaker: أبو بكر الأنباري
ALUSI-FULL:v1p26/r5.claim: Al-Anbari says the Quran was sent down as a whole to the lowest heaven and then revealed piecemeal; Gabriel specified each verse's and sura's position, so rearranging it corrupts its order.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p26/r5.anchor: قال أبو بكر الأنباري أنزل الله تعالى القرآن كله إلى سماء الدنيا ثم فرقه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p26/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p26/r6.speaker: الكرماني
ALUSI-FULL:v1p26/r6.claim: Al-Kirmani says the sura order matches the Preserved Tablet and that the Prophet reviewed the accumulated Quran with Gabriel annually, twice in his final year.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p26/r6.anchor: وقال الكرماني بترتيب السور هكذا هو عند الله تعالى في اللوح المحفوظ

ALUSI-FULL:v1p26/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p26/r7.speaker: الطيبي
ALUSI-FULL:v1p26/r7.claim: Al-Tibi shares al-Kirmani's account, which al-Alusi says is also transmitted from a large group.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p26/r7.anchor: وقال الطيبي مثله وهو المروي عن جمع غفير إلا أنه يشكل على هذا

ALUSI-FULL:v1p26/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p26/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v1p26/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas asked Uthman why al-Anfal and Bara'a were paired without a basmala and placed among the seven long suras; Uthman explained that he presumed they belonged together because their stories resembled each other and the Prophet had not clarified.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p26/r8.anchor: عن إبن عباس قال قلت لعثمان ما حملكم على أن عمدتم إلى الأنفال

ALUSI-FULL:v1p26/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p26/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p26/r9.claim: Uthman's explanation indicates that independent judgment entered the arrangement of al-Anfal and Bara'a; al-Bayhaqi therefore exempts these two from his otherwise fully prescribed order.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p26/r9.anchor: فهذا يدل على أن الإجتهاد دخل في ترتيب السور ولهذا ذهب البيهقي

ALUSI-FULL:v1p26/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p26/r10.speaker: البيهقي
ALUSI-FULL:v1p26/r10.claim: Al-Bayhaqi holds that every sura's order is prescribed except for al-Anfal and Bara'a; al-Suyuti found this answer appealing when he could not resolve the question.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p26/r10.anchor: ذهب البيهقي إلى أن جميع السور ترتيبها توقيفي إلا براءة والأنفال

ALUSI-FULL:v1p26/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p26/r11.speaker: الإمام السيوطي
ALUSI-FULL:v1p26/r11.claim: Al-Suyuti's relief at al-Bayhaqi's answer came after he had found himself unable to resolve the issue.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p26/r11.anchor: انشرح صدر الإمام السيوطي لما ضاق ذرعا عن الجواب

ALUSI-FULL:v1p26/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p26/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p26/r12.claim: Al-Alusi prefers that the present codex matches the Quran's order in the Preserved Tablet: the Prophet must have specified or signaled the positions, and the Companions' eventual consensus shows they had certain knowledge.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p26/r12.anchor: والذي ينشرح له صدر هذا الفقير هو ما أنشرحت له صدور الجمع الغفير

ALUSI-FULL:v1p26/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p26/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p26/r13.claim: Uthman may have acted on a presumption about Bara'a and al-Anfal, while others recognized a textual indication and accepted his arrangement; Umar's inspired judgments offer a parallel.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p26/r13.anchor: وعثمان رضي الله تعالى عنه وإن لم يقف على ما يفيده القطع في براءة والأنفال

ALUSI-FULL:v1p26/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p26/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p26/r14.claim: The Ibn Abbas exchange does not conclusively prove independent arrangement: the question could seek the reason for not separating the suras, and Uthman could be stating his own initial rationale.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p26/r14.anchor: والسؤال منه وجوابه ليسا قطعيين في الدلالة على الإستقلال لجواز أن يكون السؤال

ALUSI-FULL:v1p26/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p26/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p26/r15.claim: Given the community's consensus on this codex, isolated reports and unusual narrations should not overturn its established order.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p26/r15.anchor: بعد إجماع الأمة على هذا المصحف لا ينبغي أن يصاخ إلى آحاد الأخبار

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p115#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p115#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p115#2/r1.claim: The Quran's parts resemble one another in excellence and confirm one another, without contradiction or discrepancy.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p115#2/r1.anchor: يشبه بعضه بعضا في الحسن، ويصدق بعضه بعضا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p115#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p115#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p115#2/r2.claim: Mathani means that the Quran repeats paired themes: promise and threat, command and prohibition, narratives and rulings.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p115#2/r2.anchor: {مثاني} يثنى فيه ذكر الوعد والوعيد، والأمر والنهي، والأخبار والأحكام،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p115#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p115#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p115#2/r3.claim: Taqshaʿir means to tremble and recoil; gooseflesh is a bodily change brought on by dread and fear.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p115#2/r3.anchor: {تقشعر} تضطرب وتشمئز، {منه جلود الذين يخشون ربهم} والاقشعرار تغير في جلد الإنسان

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p115#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p115#2/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p115#2/r4.claim: The verse describes the skins of those who fear their Lord shuddering.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p115#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p115#2/r5.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p115#2/r5.claim: Another explanation takes “skins” to mean the hearts of those who fear their Lord.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p115#2/r5.anchor: وقيل: المراد من الجلود القلوب، أي: قلوب الذين يخشون ربهم،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p115#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p115#2/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p115#2/r6.claim: The skins and hearts soften because of God's remembrance: punishment verses make the fearful shudder, while mercy verses soothe them; their hearts tremble in fear and soften in hope.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p115#2/r6.anchor: أي: لذكر الله، أي: إذا ذكرت آيات العذاب اقشعرت جلود الخائفين لله، وإذا ذكرت آيات الرحمة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p115#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p115#2/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p115#2/r7.claim: The soothing effect of remembrance is linked to the statement that hearts find rest in God's remembrance.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p115#2/r7.anchor: كما قال الله تعالى: "ألا بذكر الله تطمئن القلوب" (الرعد-28) .

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p115#2/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p115#2/r8.speaker: العباس بن عبد المطلب
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p115#2/r8.claim: Al-Abbas reports that the Prophet said a servant's skin shuddering from fear of God causes sins to fall away like leaves from a dry tree.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p115#2/r8.anchor: عن العباس بن عبد المطلب قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "إذا اقشعر جلد العبد من خشية الله تحاتت عنه ذنوبه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p115#2/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p115#2/r9.speaker: العباس بن عبد المطلب
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p115#2/r9.claim: A second report from al-Abbas says the Prophet stated that God will forbid the Fire to a servant whose skin shudders from fear of Him.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p115#2/r9.anchor: وقال: "إذا اقشعر جلد العبد من خشية الله حرمه الله على النار"

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p115#2/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p115#2/r10.speaker: قتادة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p115#2/r10.claim: Qatada says this describes God's friends, whose skins shudder and hearts settle through remembrance; losing reason and fainting are traits of innovators and from Satan.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p115#2/r10.anchor: قال قتادة: هذا نعت أولياء الله نعتهم الله بأن تقشعر جلودهم وتطمئن قلوبهم بذكر الله،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p116#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p116#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p116#2/r1.claim: “That” refers to the best discourse, the Quran.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p116#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p116#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p116#2/r2.claim: The Quran is God's guidance by which He guides whomever He wills; whoever God leads astray has no guide.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p116#2/r2.anchor: هدى الله يهدي به من يشاء ومن يضلل الله فما له من هاد

BAYDAWI-FULL:39:23/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:23/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:23/r2.claim: A report says the Companions had grown weary and asked the Prophet to tell them something; this verse was then revealed.
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:23/r2.anchor: روي أن أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ملوا ملة فقالوا له حدثنا فنزلت

BAYDAWI-FULL:39:23/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:23/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:23/r3.claim: Beginning with God's name and construing the verb as directly as possible emphasizes the attribution to Him, magnifies the revelation, and attests to its excellence.
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:23/r3.anchor: وفي الابتداء باسم الله وبناء نزل عليه تأكيد للإسناد إليه

BAYDAWI-FULL:39:23/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:23/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:23/r4.claim: Kitāban may be an appositive for aḥsan al-ḥadīth or a circumstantial accusative; the Qur'an's parts resemble each other in inimitability, responsive arrangement, sound meaning, and universal benefits.
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:23/r4.anchor: أو حال منه، وتشابهه تشابه أبعاضه في الإعجاز

BAYDAWI-FULL:39:23/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:23/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:23/r5.claim: Mathānī is the plural of mathnā, muthannā, or muthann, as discussed in Sūrat al-Ḥijr; it can describe the book through its constituent parts, like calling a person bones, veins, and nerves, or function as a specification of mutashābihan.
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:23/r5.anchor: جمع مثنى أو مثنى أو مثن على ما مر في

BAYDAWI-FULL:39:23/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:23/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:23/r6.claim: An alternative construction makes mathānī a specification of mutashābihan, as in the phrase “a man whose qualities are beautiful.”
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:23/r6.anchor: أو جعل تمييزا من { متشبها } كقولك:

BAYDAWI-FULL:39:23/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:23/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:23/r7.claim: Those who fear God shudder from the warnings; the skin's contraction is an image of intense fear.
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:23/r7.anchor: تشمئز خوفا مما فيه من الوعيد، وهو مثل في شدة الخوف

BAYDAWI-FULL:39:23/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:23/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:23/r8.claim: The word is built from q-sh-ʿ, the name for dry leather, with an added rāʾ to make a quadriliteral, as aqmaṭarra is built from qamaṭa, “to tie.”
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:23/r8.anchor: وتركيبه من حروف القشع وهو الأديم اليابس بزيادة الراء

BAYDAWI-FULL:39:23/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:23/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:23/r9.claim: Their skins and hearts soften through mercy and encompassing forgiveness; the unqualified wording suggests that mercy is God's fundamental way and precedes wrath.
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:23/r9.anchor: بالرحمة وعموم المغفرة، والإطلاق للإشعار بأن أصل أمره الرحمة

BAYDAWI-FULL:39:23/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:23/r10.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:23/r10.claim: The preposition ilā incorporates the sense of settling and becoming tranquil; hearts are mentioned because fear is a condition of the heart.
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:23/r10.anchor: والتعدية ب { إلى } لتضمين معنى السكون والاطمئنان

BAYDAWI-FULL:39:23/r11.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:23/r11.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:23/r11.claim: Dhālika may refer to the Qur'an itself or to the state of fear followed by hope.
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:23/r11.anchor: { ذلك } أي الكتاب أو الكائن من الخشية والرجاء

BAYDAWI-FULL:39:23/r12.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:23/r12.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:23/r12.claim: God guides whomever He wills to guide.

BAYDAWI-FULL:39:23/r13.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:23/r13.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:23/r13.claim: Whoever God abandons to error has no guide who can take him out of it.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p437/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p437/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p437/r10.claim: Because it seems unlikely that remembrance of God could harden a heart, God illustrates this in the Qur’an, which guides and heals believers but is deafness and blindness to unbelievers, as in 41:44; the next verse magnifies the revealed discourse.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p437/r10.anchor: فإنه كان للذين آمنوا هدى وشفاء , وللذين لا يؤمنون في آذانهم وقر وفي أبصارهم عمى

BIQAI-FULL:v6p438/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p438/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p438/r1.claim: God reveals the Qur’an gradually to train its hearers and answer each objection as it arises.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p438/r1.anchor: أي بالتدريج للتدريب وللجواب عن كل شبهة

BIQAI-FULL:v6p438/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p438/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p438/r2.claim: The Qur’an is the finest discourse and greatest remembrance; only God’s revelation makes it unsurpassable, and no human could match it even for a day.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p438/r2.anchor: ولولا أنه هو الذي نزله لما كان الأحسن

BIQAI-FULL:v6p438/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p438/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p438/r3.claim: The noun “book” apposes “best” and describes a revelation that gathers every good.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p438/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p438/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p438/r4.claim: The Qur’an is alike throughout in miraculous eloquence and sound admonition, with no discrepancy in wording or meaning despite descending in parts over more than twenty years; human speech inevitably varies.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p438/r4.anchor: لا تفاوت فيه أصلا في لفظ ولا معنى

BIQAI-FULL:v6p438/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p438/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p438/r5.claim: The wording avoids متشبها, which could suggest the text is unclear in meaning and thus not praiseworthy.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p438/r5.anchor: لئلا يظن أنه غير واضح الدلالة لا يمدح به

BIQAI-FULL:v6p438/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p438/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p438/r6.claim: Mathānī means repeated: stories, admonitions, rulings, and wisdom recur in varied forms and with varied degrees of evidential clarity, without contradiction in their basic meaning.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p438/r6.anchor: أي تثنى فيه القصص والمواهظ والأحكام والحكم

BIQAI-FULL:v6p438/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p438/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p438/r7.claim: The repeated material pairs opposites; each explicit promise or warning also intimates the consequence of its opposite, presenting both sides twice.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p438/r7.anchor: فلا ترتب على شيء من ذلك جزاء صريحا إلا ثني بإفهام ما لضده تلويحا

BIQAI-FULL:v6p438/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p438/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p438/r8.claim: He allows an alternative parse, تقديره متشابهة مثانيه, with مثانيه in the accusative as specification.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p438/r8.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون التقدير : متشابهة مثانيه

BIQAI-FULL:v6p438/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p438/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p438/r9.claim: Repetition suits souls resistant to admonition: what is not reiterated does not take root or produce its effect; hence the Prophet repeated statements three times or more.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p438/r9.anchor: ومن ثم كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يكرر قوله ثلاث مرات فأكثر

BIQAI-FULL:v6p438/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p438/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p438/r10.claim: Although repetition can weary, the Qur’an grows sweeter and more delightful through repeated recitation, even across night and day.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p438/r10.anchor: أنه يطرب مع التكرار , ويزداد حلاوة

BIQAI-FULL:v6p438/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p438/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p438/r11.claim: The word means to shiver, gather, and contract intensely; he derives it from القشع, described as dry, aged fat.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p438/r11.anchor: أي تهتز وتتجمع وتتقبض تقبضا شديدا

BIQAI-FULL:v6p438/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p438/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p438/r12.claim: The added and repeated consonant intensifies the meaning and signals emphatic recurrence.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p438/r12.anchor: واختير حرف التكرير إشارة إلى المبالغة فيه

BIQAI-FULL:v6p438/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p438/r13.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p438/r13.claim: The skins are the body’s outer surfaces; those who fear God fear intensely and take a delight that produces reverence.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p438/r13.anchor: أي ظواهر أجسام { الذين يخشون } أي يخافون خوفا شديدا

BIQAI-FULL:v6p438/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p438/r14.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p438/r14.claim: Their fear of their beneficent Lord heightens their praise: recollection of divine majesty makes them more fearful.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p438/r14.anchor: وزاد في مدحهم بأنهم يخافون المحسن

BIQAI-FULL:v6p438/r15.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p438/r15.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BIQAI-FULL:v6p438/r15.claim: A report from the Prophet says that when a servant’s skin shivers from fear of God, his sins fall away; al-Ṭabarānī transmits it from al-ʿAbbās, with no grading stated.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p438/r15.anchor: روى الطبراني عن العباس رضي الله عنه أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

BIQAI-FULL:v6p438/r16.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p438/r16.speaker: ابن عمر
BIQAI-FULL:v6p438/r16.claim: Ibn ʿUmar saw an Iraqi collapse when Qur’an and God’s remembrance were recited, objected that God-fearing believers do not collapse, attributed it to Satan, and said this was not the Companions’ practice.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p438/r16.anchor: وروي عن ابن عمر رضي الله عنهما أنه مر برجل من أهل العراق ساقط

BIQAI-FULL:v6p438/r17.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p438/r17.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p438/r17.claim: After the shiver, skins soften and hearts follow; the ordering moves from the dryness implied by gooseflesh back to hope, while keeping hearts away from any suggestion of hardness.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p438/r17.anchor: وقدم ما صرح فيه بالاقشعرار الذي يلزمه البيس

BIQAI-FULL:v6p438/r18.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p438/r18.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p438/r18.claim: Fear is located only in the heart, so the verse does not explicitly say that hearts shiver; this avoids wording that might imply hardness.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p438/r18.anchor: وكان سر حذف التصريح بذلك تنزيها عن ذكر ما قد يفهم القسوة

BIQAI-FULL:v6p438/r19.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p438/r19.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p438/r19.claim: The preposition إلى conveys that the restless, changeable heart settles and becomes tranquil in God’s remembrance.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p438/r19.anchor: دل على حفظه له بنافذ أمره وباهر عظمته

BIQAI-FULL:v6p438/r20.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p438/r20.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p438/r20.claim: God’s remembrance fundamentally evokes hope, because His mercy preceded His wrath.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p438/r20.anchor: فإن الأصل في ذكره الرجاء لأن رحمته سبقت غضبه

BIQAI-FULL:v6p438/r21.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p438/r21.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p438/r21.claim: The explicit name replaces a pronoun to prevent misidentifying its antecedent as the Lord in a way that could support unionist or other heresies; “remembrance of God” also magnifies the passage over “discourse” or “book.”
BIQAI-FULL:v6p438/r21.anchor: وأظهر موضع الإضمار لأحسن الحديث لئلا يوهم أن الضمير للرب

BIQAI-FULL:v6p438/r22.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p438/r22.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p438/r22.claim: Calling it God’s remembrance rather than merely discourse or book gives it greater dignity and shifts from the attribute of beneficence to the comprehensive divine name.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p438/r22.anchor: بل عدل إلى ما عرف أنه ذكره سبحانه ليكون أفخم لشأنه

BIQAI-FULL:v6p438/r23.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p438/r23.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p438/r23.claim: ذلك points to the wondrous revealed discourse and the bodily contraction and release it produces; this is God’s guidance.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p438/r23.anchor: أي الأمر العظيم الغريب من الحديث المنزل والقبض والبسط

BIQAI-FULL:v6p438/r24.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p438/r24.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p438/r24.claim: The same revelation guides some and misleads others: hardened hearts remain unmoved, so what guides one person becomes misguidance for another.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p438/r24.anchor: ومن هداه الله فما له من مضل

BIQAI-FULL:v6p438/r25.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p438/r25.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p438/r25.claim: When the sovereign God firmly misleads someone, no guide can redirect him because none can overturn God’s command or judgment.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p438/r25.anchor: لأنه لا راد لأمره ولا معقب لحكمه

BIQAI-FULL:v6p438/r26.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p438/r26.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p438/r26.claim: The verse uses ellipsis by correspondence: God’s unrestricted guiding implies the parallel action of misleading, and the stated impossibility of guiding the misled implies its omitted counterpart for the guided; the argument refutes the Qadariyya.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p438/r26.anchor: ذكر أولا إطلاق أمره في الهداية دليلا على حذف مثله في الضلال

DURR-FULL:v7p220/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p220/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p220/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas says the verse was revealed after people asked the Prophet to tell them something.
DURR-FULL:v7p220/r6.anchor: يا رسول الله لو حدثتنا فنزل

DURR-FULL:v7p220/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p220/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p220/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas says the Quran as a whole is mathānī.
DURR-FULL:v7p220/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما {الله نزل أحسن الحديث كتابا متشابها مثاني} قال: القرآن كله مثاني

DURR-FULL:v7p220/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p220/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p220/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas says the Quran's parts resemble and refer back to one another.
DURR-FULL:v7p220/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله {مثاني} قال: القرآن يشبه بعضه بعضا ويرد بعضه إلى بعض

DURR-FULL:v7p220/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p220/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p220/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas says the Quran's lawful and forbidden rulings do not conflict, verses resemble other verses, letters resemble letters, and God repeats its duties, limits, and judgments.
DURR-FULL:v7p220/r9.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما {كتابا متشابها} حلاله وحرامه لا يختلف شيء منه الآية تشبه الآية

DURR-FULL:v7p220/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p220/r10.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v7p220/r10.claim: Mujahid also describes the whole Quran as mathānī.
DURR-FULL:v7p220/r10.anchor: عن مجاهد رضي الله عنه {كتابا متشابها} قال: القرآن كله مثاني

DURR-FULL:v7p221/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p221/r1.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v7p221/r1.claim: An unattributed gloss describes the Quran's recurring discourse as extending from God's praise to His servant.
DURR-FULL:v7p221/r1.anchor: قال: من ثناء الله إلى عبده

DURR-FULL:v7p221/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p221/r2.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v7p221/r2.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr says the Quran's passages explain one another and guide to one another.
DURR-FULL:v7p221/r2.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير رضي الله عنه في قوله {متشابها} قال: يفسر بعضه بعضا ويدل بعضه على بعض

DURR-FULL:v7p221/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p221/r3.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v7p221/r3.claim: Al-Hasan says God repeats judgments in the Quran, so a verse in one surah has a counterpart in another.
DURR-FULL:v7p221/r3.anchor: عن أبي رجاء رضي الله عنه قال: سألت الحسن رضي الله عنه عن قول الله تعالى {الله نزل أحسن الحديث كتابا متشابها} قال: ثنى الله فيه القضاء

DURR-FULL:v7p221/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p221/r4.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v7p221/r4.claim: Ikrima likewise explains mathānī as God's repetition of judgments in the Quran.
DURR-FULL:v7p221/r4.anchor: سأل عكرمة رضي الله عنه عنها وأنا أسمع فقال: ثنى الله فيه القضاء

DURR-FULL:v7p221/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p221/r5.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v7p221/r5.claim: Qatada describes God's allies as shivering at the Quran, weeping, and finding their hearts settled through remembrance.
DURR-FULL:v7p221/r5.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه في قوله {تقشعر منه جلود الذين يخشون ربهم} هذا نعت أولياء الله

DURR-FULL:v7p221/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p221/r6.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v7p221/r6.claim: Qatada rejects loss of reason and fainting as a description of God's allies, attributing such states to heretics and Satan.
DURR-FULL:v7p221/r6.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه في قوله {تقشعر منه جلود الذين يخشون ربهم} هذا نعت أولياء الله

DURR-FULL:v7p221/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p221/r7.speaker: ابن جريج
DURR-FULL:v7p221/r7.claim: Ibn Jurayj says God's warning makes hearers' skin shiver, while mention of Paradise softens it as they hope for mercy.
DURR-FULL:v7p221/r7.anchor: عن ابن جريج رضي الله عنه في قوله {تقشعر منه جلود الذين يخشون ربهم} قال: إذا سمعوا ذكر الله والوعيد

DURR-FULL:v7p221/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p221/r8.speaker: عبد الله بن عروة بن الزبير
DURR-FULL:v7p221/r8.claim: Abd Allah ibn ʿUrwa says his grandmother Asma described the Prophet's companions as weeping and shivering during recitation; she sought God's protection from Satan when told some people fainted.
DURR-FULL:v7p221/r8.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عروة بن الزبير قال: قلت لجدتي أسماء رضي الله عنها كيف كان يصنع أصحاب رسول الله

DURR-FULL:v7p221/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p221/r9.speaker: عامر بن عبد الله بن الزبير
DURR-FULL:v7p221/r9.claim: Amir ibn Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr says his mother told him not to join people who trembled and fainted in remembrance, since the Prophet, Abu Bakr, and Umar recited without this happening.
DURR-FULL:v7p221/r9.anchor: عن عامر بن عبد الله بن الزبير رضي الله عنه قال: جئت أمي فقلت: وجدت قوما ما رأيت خيرا منهم قط

DURR-FULL:v7p222/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p222/r1.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v7p222/r1.claim: The continuing account has Asma challenge whether those who faint are more God-fearing than Abu Bakr and Umar.
DURR-FULL:v7p222/r1.anchor: افتراهم أخشى من أبي بكر وعمر

DURR-FULL:v7p222/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p222/r2.speaker: قيس بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v7p222/r2.claim: Qays ibn Jubayr says fainting fits come from Satan.
DURR-FULL:v7p222/r2.anchor: عن قيس بن جبير رضي الله عنه قال: الصعقة من الشيطان

DURR-FULL:v7p222/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p222/r3.speaker: إبراهيم
DURR-FULL:v7p222/r3.claim: Ibrahim says that a man seeing a light is experiencing something from Satan; if it were good, the people of Badr would have been favored with it.
DURR-FULL:v7p222/r3.anchor: عن إبراهيم رضي الله عنه في الرجل يرى الضوء قال: من الشيطان لو كان يرى خيرا لأوثر به أهل بدر

DURR-FULL:v7p222/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p222/r4.speaker: العباس بن عبد المطلب
DURR-FULL:v7p222/r4.claim: Al-Abbas says a servant's skin shivering from fear of God causes sins to fall away like leaves from a withered tree.
DURR-FULL:v7p222/r4.anchor: عن العباس بن عبد المطلب رضي الله عنه: إذا اقشعر جلد العبد من خشية الله تحاتت عنه خطاياه

DURR-FULL:v7p222/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p222/r5.speaker: أبي بن كعب
DURR-FULL:v7p222/r5.claim: Ubayy ibn Kaʿb compares a believer who follows the Sunna and shivers at remembrance to a dry tree shedding leaves, adding that tears from fear of God keep the servant from touching the Fire.
DURR-FULL:v7p222/r5.anchor: عن أبي بن كعب رضي الله عنه قال: ليس من عبد على سبيل ذكر سنة ذكر الرحمن فاقشعر جلده

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p375/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p375/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p375/r2.claim: The rain and growth passage begins the sūra’s Qur’an-and-Islam guidance theme, resumed in 39:22–23 after the excursus beginning at 39:2.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p375/r2.anchor: استئناف ابتدائي انتقل به إلى غرض التنويه بالقرآن وما احتوى عليه من هدى الإسلام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p375/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p375/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p375/r8.claim: The juxtaposition of the rain parable with 39:22–23 signals the lesson drawn from it: the Qur’an-guided response parallels the growth of vegetation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p375/r8.anchor: إشارة إلى العبرة من هذا التمثيل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p382/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p382/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p382/r4.claim: The next passage explains that Qur’anic guidance softens God-fearing hearts; hardness comes from inner rust, as with the sealed hearts in 2:6–7, not from any shortcoming in the Qur’an’s guidance.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p382/r4.anchor: مبينة أن قساوة قلوب الضالين من سماع القرآن إنما هي لرين في قلوبهم وعقولهم لا لنقص في هدايته

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p388/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p388/r1.speaker: عياض
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p388/r1.claim: In al-Shifāʾ, Qadi ʿIyāḍ counts the awe and grandeur that seize listeners as an aspect of the Qur’an’s inimitability, since its elevated rank surpasses all speech.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p388/r1.anchor: عياض في ( الشفاء ) من وجوه إعجاز القرآن : الروعة التي تلحق قلوب سامعيه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p388/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p388/r2.speaker: أسماء بنت أبي بكر
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p388/r2.claim: Asma bint Abi Bakr reports that the Prophet’s Companions wept and their skins shivered when the Qur’an was recited to them, as described here.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p388/r2.anchor: وعن أسماء بنت أبي بكر كان أصحاب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا قرىء عليهم القرآن كما نعتهم الله تدمع أعينهم وتقشعر جلودهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p388/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p388/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p388/r3.claim: The verse singles out God-fearing people for gooseflesh because it is followed by their skin and hearts softening.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p388/r3.anchor: وخص القشعريرة بالذين يخشون ربهم باعتبار ما سيردف به

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p388/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p388/r4.speaker: عياض
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p388/r4.claim: Qadi ʿIyāḍ says the Qur’an’s awe affects deniers even more intensely, so they find hearing it burdensome and turn away, as in 17:46.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p388/r4.anchor: قال عياض : ( وهي ، أي الروعة التي تلحق قلوب سامعيه عند سماعه ، على المكذبين به أعظم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p388/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p388/r5.speaker: جبير بن مطعم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p388/r5.claim: In a report the author calls authentic, Jubayr ibn Mutʿim says the Prophet’s recitation of al-Ṭūr 35–37 nearly made his heart fly; that was when Islam first took root in him.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p388/r5.anchor: عن جبير بن مطعم قال : ( سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقرأ في المغرب بالطور

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p388/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p388/r6.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p388/r6.claim: Muhammad ibn Kaʿb al-Qurazi says he was told that ʿUtba ibn Rabiʿa, deeply moved by the Prophet’s Fussilat recitation and its warning, covered the Prophet’s mouth and begged him by kinship to stop; the source gives no grading.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p388/r6.anchor: روي عن محمد بن كعب القرظي قال : ( أخبرت أن عتبة بن ربيعة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p388/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p388/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p388/r7.claim: For believers, awe during recitation keeps drawing them toward the Qur’an and gives them delight because their hearts incline to it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p388/r7.anchor: وأما المؤمن فلا تزال روعته وهيبته إياه مع تلاوته توليه انجذابا وتكسبه هشاشة لميل قلبه إليه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p391/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p391/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p391/r1.claim: Calling this God’s guidance means that God prepared the Qur’an’s qualities for guidance and added it to Himself because He revealed it for that purpose.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p391/r1.anchor: راجع إلى ما هيأه الله للهدى من صفات القرآن فإضافته إليه بأنه أنزله لذلك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p391/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p391/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p391/r2.claim: Attributing guidance and misguidance to God describes how different audiences respond to the Qur’an, which fully supplies the means to guide.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p391/r2.anchor: ومعنى إسناد الهدى والإضلال إلى الله راجع إلى مراتب تأثر المخاطبين بالقرآن وعدم تأثرهم بحيث كان القرآن مستوفيا لأسباب اهتداء الناس به

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p391/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p391/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p391/r3.claim: Alternatively, “that” refers to the Qur’an itself as God’s guidance or proof of it: those God wills to guide follow it, while those He wills to stray disbelieve it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p391/r3.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون الإشارة إلى { أحسن الحديث }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p391/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p391/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p391/r4.claim: “Whomever He wills” elides “to guide”: God’s will creates the person’s receptivity and determines guidance; the contrasting clause implies that one not willed guidance persists in error.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p391/r4.anchor: وهي إرادته بأنه يهتدي فخلقه متأثرا بتلك المشيئة فقدر له الاهتداء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p391/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p391/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p391/r5.claim: “Whoever God leads astray has no guide” is a conclusion to the explanatory passage.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p391/r5.anchor: فجملة { ومن يضلل الله فما له من هاد } تذييل للاستئناف البياني

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p527#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p527#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p527#2/r10.claim: The best discourse is the Qur'an.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p527#2/r10.anchor: وقوله تعالى: الله نزل أحسن الحديث يريد به القرآن

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p527#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p527#2/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p527#2/r11.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the verse came after some Companions asked the Prophet to tell them good stories and accounts of past times.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p527#2/r11.anchor: وروي عن ابن عباس أن سبب هذه الآية أن قوما من أصحاب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p527#2/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p527#2/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p527#2/r12.claim: متشابها means internally consistent, without contradiction; its language, proofs, and noble meanings resemble one another and express certainty about God, His attributes and acts, and His law.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p527#2/r12.anchor: وقوله: متشابها معناه: مستويا لا تناقض فيه ولا تدافع، بل يشبه بعضه بعضا في وصف اللفظ ووثاقة البراهين وشرف المعاني

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p527#2/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p527#2/r13.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p527#2/r13.claim: مثاني means that stories, rulings, and varied admonitions recur throughout the Qur'an without becoming tiresome as repeated speech might.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p527#2/r13.anchor: وقوله: مثاني معناه: موضع تثنية للقصص والأقضية، والمواعظ شتى فيه ولا تمل مع ذلك ولا يعرضها ما يعرض الحديث المعاد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p527#2/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p527#2/r14.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p527#2/r14.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the word by saying that matters are repeated in the Qur'an again and again.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p527#2/r14.anchor: قال ابن عباس: ثنى فيه الأمر مرارا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p527#2/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p527#2/r15.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p527#2/r15.claim: مثاني has no tanwin because it is an irregular plural without a comparable singular form.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p527#2/r15.anchor: ولا ينصرف مثاني لأنه جمع لا نظير له في الواحد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p528/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p528/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p528/r1.claim: Skin bristling describes the body's response to fear and a tender heart on hearing admonition or Qur'anic warning; it signals the fearful meaning taking hold in the listener.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p528/r1.anchor: عبارة عن قف شعر الإنسان عند ما يداخله خوف ولين قلب عند سماع موعظة أو زجر قرآن ونحوه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p528/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p528/r2.speaker: أبي بن كعب عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p528/r2.claim: When Ubayy ibn Kab recited before the Prophet and hearts softened, the Prophet advised making supplication during that tenderness because it is mercy.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p528/r2.anchor: أن أبي بن كعب قرأ عند النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فرقت القلوب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p528/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p528/r3.speaker: العباس بن عبد المطلب عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p528/r3.claim: The Prophet says that whoever's skin bristles from fear of God has sins shed like leaves falling from a dry tree.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p528/r3.anchor: وقال العباس بن عبد المطلب: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «من اقشعر جلده من خشية الله تحاتت عنه ذنوبه كما يتحات عن الشجرة اليابسة ورقها»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p528/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p528/r4.speaker: أسماء بنت أبي بكر
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p528/r4.claim: Asma says the Prophet's Companions wept and shivered on hearing Qur'an; when asked about people who faint at recitation, she sought refuge from Satan.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p528/r4.anchor: وقالت أسماء بنت أبي بكر: كان أصحاب الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم تدمع أعينهم وتقشعر جلودهم عند سماع القرآن

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p528/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p528/r5.speaker: ابن عمر
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p528/r5.claim: Seeing a man collapse at Qur'an recitation, Ibn Umar said that believers fear God without falling and that Satan enters those who do.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p528/r5.anchor: وقال ابن عمر: وقد رئي ساقطا عند سماع القرآن فقال: إنا لنخشى الله وما نسقط، هؤلاء يدخل الشيطان في جوف أحدهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p528/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p528/r6.speaker: ابن سيرين
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p528/r6.claim: Ibn Sirin proposes testing those who swoon during recitation: have one sit on a wall with legs outstretched while the Qur'an is read; if he throws himself down, he is sincere.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p528/r6.anchor: وقال ابن سيرين: بيننا وبين هؤلاء الذين يصرعون عند قراءة القرآن أن يجعل أحدهم على حائط باسطا رجليه ثم يقرأ القرآن كله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p528/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p528/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p528/r7.claim: ذلك هدى الله may refer to the Qur'an just described: that Qur'an is God's guidance.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p528/r7.anchor: وقوله: ذلك هدى الله يحتمل أن يشير إلى القرآن، أي ذلك الذي هذه صفته هدى الله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p528/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p528/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p528/r8.claim: Alternatively, it may refer to fear and the bristling of skin as signs of God's guidance.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p528/r8.anchor: ويحتمل أن يشير إلى الخشية واقشعرار الجلود، أي ذلك أمارة هدى الله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p528/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p528/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p528/r9.claim: If تقشعر is an adjectival description, do not pause at مثاني; if it begins a new statement, pause there, and the rest of the verse is straightforward.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p528/r9.anchor: ومن جعل تقشعر في موضع الصفة لم يقف على مثاني، ومن جعله مستأنفا وإخبارا منقطعا وقف على مثاني

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p36#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p36#2/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p36#2/r1.claim: The Prophet says that someone who regards another gift as better than the Quran has undervalued what God has exalted.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p36#2/r1.anchor: وروي عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال: «من قرأ القرآن فرأى أن أحدا أوتي أفضل مما أوتي فقد استصغر ما عظم الله»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p36#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p36#2/r2.speaker: عليه السلام
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p36#2/r2.claim: The Prophet calls the Quran the greatest intercessor with God, greater than any prophet or angel.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p36#2/r2.anchor: وقال عليه السلام: «ما من شفيع أفضل عند الله من القرآن، لا نبي ولا ملك»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p36#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p36#2/r3.speaker: عليه السلام
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p36#2/r3.claim: The Prophet describes reciting the Quran as the community’s best act of worship.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p36#2/r3.anchor: وقال عليه السلام: «أفضل عبادة أمتي القرآن»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p36#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p36#2/r4.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاصي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p36#2/r4.claim: ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr says Quran readers carry prophecy within them, though revelation does not come to them.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p36#2/r4.anchor: وقال عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاصي: «من قرأ القرآن فقد أدرجت النبوة بين جنبيه، إلا أنه لا يوحى إليه»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p36#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p36#2/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p36#2/r5.claim: Anas reports the Prophet’s promise that reciting one hundred verses makes a person counted among the devout, two hundred removes the charge of heedlessness, and three hundred leaves the Quran with no case against him.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p36#2/r5.anchor: وحدث أنس بن مالك عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال: «من قرأ مائة آية كتب من القانتين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p36#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p36#2/r6.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p36#2/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports the Prophet’s description of Quran bearers as the noblest of the community.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p36#2/r6.anchor: وروى ابن عباس عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال: «أشراف أمتي حملة القرآن»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p36#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p36#2/r7.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p36#2/r7.claim: After reciting the verse on those who inherit the Book, ʿUmar says the foremost remain foremost, the middle group is saved, and the wrongdoers are forgiven.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p36#2/r7.anchor: وروي عن عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه أنه قرأ هذه الآية: ثم أورثنا الكتاب الذين اصطفينا من عبادنا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p36#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p36#2/r8.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p36#2/r8.claim: The Prophet calls a house empty when it contains no portion of God’s Book.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p36#2/r8.anchor: وقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «ألا إن أصفر البيوت بيت صفر من كتاب الله»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p36#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p36#2/r9.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p36#2/r9.claim: Anas reports that the Quran is an accepted intercessor and a truthful adversary: its adherents are saved through its intercession, while those who abandon it face its complaint and punishment.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p36#2/r9.anchor: وروى أنس أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «القرآن شافع، مشفع، وما حل مصدق

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p36#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p36#2/r10.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p36#2/r10.claim: The Prophet promises two rewards to those who persist with difficulty in reciting the Quran, while the fluent reader is with the noble, righteous scribes.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p36#2/r10.anchor: وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم: «إن الذي يتعاهد هذا القرآن ويشتد عليه له أجران، والذي يقرأه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p36#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p36#2/r11.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p36#2/r11.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reports that after the Companions asked the Prophet for a narration when bored, God revealed the verse describing the Quran as the finest discourse.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p36#2/r11.anchor: وقال ابن مسعود: مل أصحاب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ملة فقالوا: يا رسول الله حدثنا، فأنزل الله تعالى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p36#2/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p36#2/r12.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p36#2/r12.claim: Ibn Masʿūd says the Companions later asked the Prophet for stories, after which God revealed the verse beginning “We relate to you the best of stories.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p36#2/r12.anchor: ثم ملوا ملة أخرى، فقالوا: قص علينا يا رسول الله، فأنزل الله تعالى: نحن نقص عليك أحسن القصص بما أوحينا إليك هذا القرآن

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p175/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p175/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p175/r1.claim: The “best discourse” is the Qurʾan; Ibn al-Jawzi says its occasion of revelation was discussed at the beginning of Surat Yusuf.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p175/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى ﴿ الله نزل أحسن الحديث ﴾ يعني القرآن وقد ذكرنا سبب نزولها في أول يوسف

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p175/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p175/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p175/r2.claim: One view says its parts resemble one another: verses, words, and letters correspond in kind.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p175/r2.anchor: أحدهما أن بعضه يشبه بعضا في الآي والحروف فالآية تشبه الآية

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p175/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p175/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p175/r3.claim: A second view says its parts confirm one another, with no disagreement or contradiction.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p175/r3.anchor: والثاني أن بعضه يصدق بعضا فليس فيه اختلاف ولا تناقض

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p175/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p175/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p175/r4.claim: It is called mathānī because it repeats narratives, religious duties, legal limits, reward, and punishment.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p175/r4.anchor: وإنما قيل له ﴿ مثاني ﴾ لأنه كررت فيه القصص والفرائض والحدود والثواب والعقاب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p175/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p175/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p175/r5.claim: Repeated narratives let dispersed Arab delegations and tribes hear the stories of Moses, Jesus, and Noah, spreading them across the earth.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p175/r5.anchor: فلو لم تكن الأنباء والقصص مثناة مكررة لوقعت قصة موسى إلى قوم وقصة عيسى إلى قوم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p175/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p175/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p175/r6.claim: Muslims recited some Qurʾan to visiting Arab delegations, while the Prophet sent different surahs to separate tribes.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p175/r6.anchor: أن وفود العرب كانت ترد على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فيقرئهم المسلمون شيئا من القرآن

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p175/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p175/r7.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p175/r7.claim: He defers the benefit of repeating the same expression to his commentary on Surat al-Rahman, citing examples from four surahs.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p175/r7.anchor: فأما فائدة تكرار الكلام من جنس واحد كقوله ﴿ فبأي آلاء ربكما تكذبان ﴾ الرحمن

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p175#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p175#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p175#2/r1.claim: Taqshaʿir means the skin gets goosebumps, a bodily change caused by awe.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p175#2/r1.anchor: أي تأخذهم قشعريرة وهو تغير يحدث في جلد الإنسان من الوجل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p175#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p175#2/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p175#2/r2.claim: The Prophet said that when a servant's skin shudders from fear of God, his sins fall away like leaves from a dry tree; no grading is stated.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p175#2/r2.anchor: روى العباس ابن عبد المطلب عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال إذا اقشعر جلد العبد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p175#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p175#2/r3.speaker: السدي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p175#2/r3.claim: Al-Suddi says the skin bristles at God's threat and softens at His promise.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p175#2/r3.anchor: أحدها تقشعر من وعيده وتلين عند وعده قاله السدي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p175#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p175#2/r4.speaker: الماوردي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p175#2/r4.claim: One view cited by al-Mawardi says the skin bristles from fear and softens through hope.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p175#2/r4.anchor: والثاني تقشعر من الخوف وتلين من الرجاء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p175#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p175#2/r5.speaker: الماوردي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p175#2/r5.claim: Another view cited by al-Mawardi says the skin bristles from awe of God and softens at recitation.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p175#2/r5.anchor: والثالث تقشعر الجلود لإعظامه وتلين عند تلاوته ذكرهما الماوردي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p175#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p175#2/r6.speaker: بعض أهل المعاني
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p175#2/r6.claim: Some linguists say the object of “God's remembrance” is omitted; the sense is that hearts find comfort in remembrance of Paradise and reward.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p175#2/r6.anchor: محذوف لأنه معلوم والمعنى تطمئن قلوبهم إلى ذكر الله الجنة والثواب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p175#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p175#2/r7.speaker: قتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p175#2/r7.claim: Qatada says this describes God's friends, whose skin bristles and hearts soften; swooning is associated with people of innovation and Satan.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p175#2/r7.anchor: قال قتادة هذا نعت أولياء الله تقشعر جلودهم وتلين قلوبهم ولم ينعتهم بذهاب عقولهم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p175#2/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p175#2/r8.speaker: ابن عمر
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p175#2/r8.claim: Abu Hazim reports that Ibn Umar saw an Iraqi man collapse at Qurʾan recitation and replied that they feared God without collapsing.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p175#2/r8.anchor: ابن عمر برجل ساقط من أهل العراق فقال ما شأنه فقالوا إنه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p175#2/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p175#2/r9.speaker: عامر بن عبد الله بن الزبير
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p175#2/r9.claim: After his son described people trembling and fainting during remembrance, al-Zubayr forbade him to sit with them, citing the Prophet, Abu Bakr, and Umar as counterexamples.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p175#2/r9.anchor: وقال عامر بن عبد الله بن الزبير جئت أبي فقال لي أين كنت فقلت وجدت قوما

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p175#2/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p175#2/r10.speaker: أسماء بنت أبي بكر
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p175#2/r10.claim: Asked by Ikrima whether early Muslims fainted from fear, Asma said no, they wept.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p175#2/r10.anchor: قال عكرمة سئلت أسماء بنت أبي بكر هل كان أحد من السلف يغشى عليه من الخوف قالت لا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p175#2/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p175#2/r11.speaker: أسماء بنت أبي بكر
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p175#2/r11.claim: Asma said the Prophet's Companions wept and their skin shivered at Qurʾan recitation; she sought God's protection when told some people now faint.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p175#2/r11.anchor: وقال عبد الله بن عروة بن الزبير قلت لجدتي أسماء بنت أبي بكر كيف كان أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p175#2/r12.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p175#2/r12.speaker: إبراهيم النخعي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p175#2/r12.claim: Ibrahim al-Nakhaʿi told a man who trembled at remembrance that controllable trembling was unremarkable, while uncontrollable trembling departed from earlier practice.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p175#2/r12.anchor: وكان جواب يرعد عند الذكر فقال له إبراهيم النخعي إن كنت تملكه فما أبالي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p178/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p178/r1.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p178/r1.claim: One view identifies “that” as the Qurʾan itself.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p178/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p178/r2.speaker: ابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p178/r2.claim: Ibn al-Anbari identifies “that” as the believers' response at recitation: bristling at threats and softening at promises.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p178/r2.anchor: والثاني أنه ما ينزل بالمؤمنين عند تلاوة القرآن من اقشعرار الجلود عند الوعيد

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p93#3/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p93#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p93#3/r1.claim: This verse praises the Qur'an, the great book God revealed to His noble Messenger.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p93#3/r1.anchor: هذا مدح من الله -عز وجل-لكتابه القرآن العظيم المنزل على رسوله الكريم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p93#3/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p93#3/r2.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p93#3/r2.claim: Mujahid says the entire Qur'an is mutually similar and repeatedly recurring.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p93#3/r2.anchor: قال مجاهد: يعني القرآن كله متشابه مثاني.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p93#3/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p93#3/r3.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p93#3/r3.claim: Qatada says one verse resembles another, and one letter resembles another.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p93#3/r3.anchor: وقال قتادة: الآية تشبه الآية، والحرف يشبه الحرف.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p93#3/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p93#3/r4.speaker: الضحاك
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p93#3/r4.claim: Al-Dahhak interprets mathani as repetition of the discourse so that people understand their Lord.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p93#3/r4.anchor: وقال الضحاك: {مثاني} ترديد القول ليفهموا عن ربهم عز وجل.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p93#3/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p93#3/r5.speaker: عكرمة، والحسن
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p93#3/r5.claim: Ikrima and al-Hasan say God repeated the decree in the Qur'an; al-Hasan adds that one sura's verse may resemble a verse in another.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p93#3/r5.anchor: وقال عكرمة، والحسن: ثنى الله فيه القضاء -زاد الحسن: تكون السورة فيها آية

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p93#3/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p93#3/r6.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p93#3/r6.claim: Ibn Zayd says mathani means repeated; accounts of Moses, Salih, Hud, and other prophets recur in many places in the Qur'an.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p93#3/r6.anchor: وقال عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم: {مثاني} مردد، ردد موسى في القرآن، وصالح وهود والأنبياء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p93#3/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p93#3/r7.speaker: سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p93#3/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas, as reported by Saʿid ibn Jubayr, says the Qur'an resembles itself and its parts refer back to one another.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p93#3/r7.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير، عن ابن عباس: {مثاني} قال: القرآن يشبه بعضه بعضا، ويرد (1) بعضه على بعض

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p93#3/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p93#3/r8.speaker: بعض العلماء عن سفيان بن عيينة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p93#3/r8.claim: A view reported from Sufyan ibn Uyayna calls passages with one recurring subject mutashabih and passages pairing opposites mathani; examples contrast the righteous and wicked, and this is distinct from mutashabih in 3:7.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p93#3/r8.anchor: وقال بعض العلماء: ويروى عن سفيان بن عيينة معنى قوله: {متشابها مثاني} أن سياقات القرآن تارة تكون في معنى واحد

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p94/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p94/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p94/r1.claim: When the righteous understand divine promises, threats, warnings, and admonitions, fear makes their skin shudder; hope in God's mercy and gentleness then softens their skin and hearts.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p94/r1.anchor: لما يفهمون منه من الوعد والوعيد. والتخويف والتهديد، تقشعر منه جلودهم من الخشية والخوف

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p94/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p94/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p94/r2.claim: Believers listen to Qur'anic recitation, unlike disbelievers who listen to songs performed by singing women.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p94/r2.anchor: أن سماع هؤلاء هو تلاوة الآيات، وسماع أولئك نغمات لأبيات، من أصوات القينات

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p94/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p94/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p94/r3.claim: When God's verses are recited, believers prostrate and weep with reverence, fear, hope, love, understanding, and knowledge; they listen attentively, act on the verses, and prostrate knowingly rather than merely imitate others.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p94/r3.anchor: خروا سجدا وبكيا، بأدب وخشية، ورجاء ومحبة، وفهم وعلم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p94/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p94/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p94/r4.claim: Ibn Kathir connects the believers' response to verses describing their hearts trembling and faith increasing, and their respectful, attentive response to God's signs.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p94/r4.anchor: كما قال: {إنما المؤمنون الذين إذا ذكر الله وجلت قلوبهم وإذا تليت عليهم آياته زادتهم إيمانا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p94/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p94/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p94/r5.claim: The Companions maintained composure and proper manners at the Prophet's recitation, without shouting or pretending a state; their steadiness, stillness, reverence, and fear brought them distinction in this life and the next.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p94/r5.anchor: لم يكونوا يتصارخون ولا يتكلفون ما ليس فيهم، بل عندهم من الثبات والسكون والأدب والخشية

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p94/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p94/r6.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p94/r6.claim: Qatada says this describes God's allies: their skin shudders, eyes weep, and hearts settle with God's remembrance; losing reason and fainting describe innovators, from Satan.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p94/r6.anchor: قال عبد الرزاق: حدثنا معمر قال: تلا قتادة، رحمه الله: {تقشعر منه جلود الذين يخشون ربهم ثم تلين جلودهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p95/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p95/r1.speaker: السدي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p95/r1.claim: Al-Suddī explains their skin and hearts softening toward God's remembrance as softening toward God's promise.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p95/r1.anchor: وقال السدي: {ثم تلين جلودهم وقلوبهم إلى ذكر الله} أي: إلى وعد الله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p95/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p95/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p95/r2.claim: This is the condition of one God guides; whoever is unlike this is among those God misguides, with no guide for the one He misleads.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p95/r2.anchor: هذه صفة من هداه الله، ومن كان على خلاف ذلك فهو ممن أضله الله

JISHUMI:v8p6052/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6052/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p6052/r1.claim: Blind imitation prevents knowing what is best; one may hear truth and falsehood, but should not follow falsehood.
JISHUMI:v8p6052/r1.anchor: وتدل على أن استماع الحق والباطل يحسن، وإن لم يحسن اتباع الباطل

JISHUMI:v8p6052/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6052/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p6052/r2.claim: The passage indicates the great importance of calling people to the truth.
JISHUMI:v8p6052/r2.anchor: وتدل على عظم محل الدعاء إلى الحق

JISHUMI:v8p6053/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6053/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p6053/r3.claim: Mathānī is the plural of mathnā, from two: something repeated or doubled by adding its like.
JISHUMI:v8p6053/r3.anchor: مثاني: جمع مثنى، مأخوذ من الاثنين، وهو المردد المكرر

JISHUMI:v8p6053/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6053/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p6053/r4.claim: Kitāban mutashābihan is accusative as a specification distinguishing the Quran from other discourse.
JISHUMI:v8p6053/r4.anchor: نصب (كتابا متشابها) على التمييز، فميز القرآن من جملة الأحاديث

JISHUMI:v8p6053/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6053/r5.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v8p6053/r5.claim: An alternative parses kitāban as an appositive of aḥsan al-ḥadīth.
JISHUMI:v8p6053/r5.anchor: وقيل: هو بدل من أحسن الحديث

JISHUMI:v8p6053/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6053/r13.speaker: الصحابة
JISHUMI:v8p6053/r13.claim: The Companions asked the Messenger to tell them a story, and this verse was revealed.
JISHUMI:v8p6053/r13.anchor: قالت الصحابة: يا رسول الله، لو حدثتنا، فنزل: (الله نزل أحسن الحديث ك)

JISHUMI:v8p6053/r17.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6053/r17.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v8p6053/r17.claim: Abu Muslim connects this verse to 39:17–18: those who hear and follow the best speech are told that the Quran is the best discourse and most worthy of following.
JISHUMI:v8p6053/r17.anchor: وقيل: يتصل بما تقدم من قوله

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p125/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p125/r1.speaker: ابن مسعود
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p125/r1.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reports that the Companions tired of the same routine and asked the Prophet to tell them something; this verse was then revealed.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p125/r1.anchor: عن ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه : أن أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p125/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p125/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p125/r2.claim: Making God the subject and predicating نزّل of Him magnifies the best discourse, confirms its divine source, and signals its miraculous distinction from ordinary speech.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p125/r2.anchor: وإيقاع اسم الله مبتدأ وبناء { نزل } عليه : فيه تفخيم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p125/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p125/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p125/r3.claim: كتابا can be an appositive replacing أحسن الحديث.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p125/r3.anchor: بدل من أحسن الحديث . ويحتمل أن يكون حالا منه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p125/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p125/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p125/r4.claim: Alternatively, كتابا is a circumstantial accusative describing أحسن الحديث.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p125/r4.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون حالا منه { متشابها } مطلق في مشابهة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p125/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p125/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p125/r5.claim: The Qurʾān’s parts resemble one another in soundness, firmness, truth, benefit, apt wording, precise expression, and the mutually reinforcing, inimitable structure of its composition.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p125/r5.anchor: في الصحة والإحكام ، والبناء على الحق والصدق

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p125/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p125/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p125/r6.claim: مثاني may explain how the book is متشابها, since its repeated stories resemble one another; مثاني is the plural of مثنى, meaning repeated.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p125/r6.anchor: لأن القصص المكررة لا تكون إلا متشابهة . والمثاني : جمع مثنى

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p125/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p125/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p125/r7.claim: It is called repeated because its stories, accounts, rulings, commands, prohibitions, promises, threats, and admonitions recur.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p125/r7.anchor: ولما ثنى من قصصه وأنبائه ، وأحكامه ، وأوامره

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p125/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p125/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p125/r8.claim: Another explanation is that the Qurʾān is repeatedly recited and does not grow dull or stale through frequent repetition.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p125/r8.anchor: وقيل : لأنه يثني في التلاوة ، فلا يمل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p125/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p125/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p125/r9.claim: A further derivation takes مثاني as a repeated or doubled form, like كرتين at 67:4, meaning one return after another, and paired expressions such as لبيك سعديك.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p125/r9.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون جمع مثنى مفعل ، من التثنية بمعنى التكرير

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p125/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p125/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p125/r10.claim: A singular book may take a plural description because it is a whole consisting of detailed parts; the author compares this to the Qurʾān’s divisions and to a human made of bones, veins, and nerves.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p125/r10.anchor: إنما صح ذلك لأن الكتاب جملة ذات تفاصيل ، وتفاصيل الشيء

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p125/r11.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p125/r11.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p125/r11.claim: One possible underlying construction supplies فصولا: a book resembling one another in its sections, which are repeated.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p125/r12.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p125/r12.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p125/r12.claim: Alternatively, the plural form works as a descriptive predicate like برمة أعشار or ثوب أخلاق.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p125/r12.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون كقولك : برمة أعشار ، وثوب أخلاق

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p125/r13.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p125/r13.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p125/r13.claim: Alternatively, مثاني is not an adjective but a distinguishing accusative after متشابها, meaning its aspects or qualities are repeated, like رجل حسن شمائل.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p125/r13.anchor: ويجوز أن لا يكون مثاني صفة ، ويكون منتصبا على التمييز

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p125/r14.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p125/r14.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p125/r14.claim: Repetition is needed because people resist admonition; returning to it repeatedly helps it take root in them.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p125/r14.anchor: النفوس أنفر شيء من حديث الوعظ والنصيحة ، فما لم يكرر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p125/r15.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p125/r15.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p125/r15.claim: The Prophet’s custom was to repeat admonition three or seven times so it would take root in people’s hearts.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p125/r15.anchor: عادة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أن يكرر عليهم ما كان يغط به وينصح ثلاث مرات وسبعا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p125/r16.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p125/r16.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p125/r16.claim: اقشعر describes intense contraction; its root evokes dry leather, with an added ر producing a quadriliteral form and an added sense of intensity.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p125/r16.anchor: اقشعر الجلد : إذا تقبض تقبضا شديدا ، وتركيبه من حروف القشع

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p125/r17.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p125/r17.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p125/r17.claim: The phrase is an image for intense fear, when the skin tightens and its hairs stand on end.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p125/r17.anchor: اقشعر جلده من الخوف وقف شعره ، وهو مثل في شدة الخوف

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p125/r18.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p125/r18.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p125/r18.claim: The bodily reaction may be figurative, portraying the extremity of their awe, or literal: Qurʾānic warnings make their skin shiver, then recollection of God’s mercy softens skin and hearts.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p125/r18.anchor: فيجوز أن يريد به الله سبحانه التمثيل ، تصويرا لإفراط خشيتهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p125/r19.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p125/r19.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p125/r19.claim: تلين is construed with إلى by incorporating the sense of a verb that takes إلى, such as becoming still or tranquil toward something.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p125/r19.anchor: ضمن معنى فعل متعد بإلى ، كأنه قيل : سكنت . أو اطمأنت

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p125/r20.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p125/r20.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p125/r20.claim: The verse names God rather than mercy because mercy and compassion are fundamental to His way, and His mercy precedes His anger.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p125/r20.anchor: لأن أصل أمره الرحمة والرأفة ، ورحمته هي سابقة غضبه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p125/r21.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p125/r21.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p125/r21.claim: He first mentions skin alone because fear’s location in the heart is already implicit; at the outset hearts fear and skin shivers, then remembrance replaces fear with hope and shivering with softness.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p125/r21.anchor: إذا ذكرت الخشية التي محلها القلوب ، فقد ذكرت القلوب

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p125/r22.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p125/r22.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p125/r22.claim: ذلك points to the book: God guides His pious servants through it so they fear Him and hope in His mercy.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p125/r22.anchor: إشارة إلى الكتاب ، وهو { هدى الله يهدى به } يوفق به

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p125/r23.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p125/r23.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p125/r23.claim: Alternatively, ذلك refers to the described fear and hope as the effect of God’s لطف, called guidance because it results from guidance.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p125/r23.anchor: أو ذلك الكائن من الخشية والرجاء هدي الله ، أي : أثر هداه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p125/r24.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p125/r24.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p125/r24.claim: On the alternative reading, others who see the fearful and hopeful people may be drawn to imitate their conduct and path.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p125/r24.anchor: من صحب أولئك ورآهم خاشين راجين ، فكان ذلك مرغبا لهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p125/r25.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p125/r25.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p125/r25.claim: God’s leading astray means withholding لطف from transgressors and wrongdoers.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p125/r25.anchor: من الفساق والفجرة { فما له من هاد }

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p125/r26.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p125/r26.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p125/r26.claim: Alternatively, God’s لطف has no effect on those whose hard hearts and persistence in wickedness leave them beyond influence or guidance.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p125/r26.anchor: ومن لم يؤثر فيه ألطافه لقسوة قلبه وإصراره على فجوره

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p122/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p122/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p122/r1.claim: The best discourse is the Quran.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p122/r1.anchor: يعني القرآن , ويحتمل تسميته حديثا وجهين

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p122/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p122/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p122/r2.claim: It may be called hadith because it is God's speech, as the Prophet's speech is called hadith.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p122/r2.anchor: لأنه كلام الله , والكلام يسمى حديثا

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p122/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p122/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p122/r3.claim: Alternatively, it is hadith because revelation came after earlier revealed books.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p122/r3.anchor: لأنه حديث التنزيل بعدما تقدمه من الكتب المنزلة على من تقدم من الأنبياء

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p122/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p122/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p122/r4.claim: It is best for its eloquence and inimitability.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p122/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p122/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p122/r5.claim: Alternatively, it is the most complete and firmly established revealed book.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p122/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p122/r6.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p122/r6.claim: Qatada says its parts resemble each other in verses and letters.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p122/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p122/r7.speaker: يحيى بن سلام
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p122/r7.claim: Yahya ibn Sallam says its parts resemble each other in light, truth, and justice.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p122/r7.anchor: في نوره وصدقه وعدله ، قاله يحيى بن سلام

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p122/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p122/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p122/r8.claim: It may resemble earlier books in commands, prohibitions, encouragement, and warnings, while being broader and more miraculous.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p122/r8.anchor: ترغيب وترهيب ، وإن كان أعم وأعجز

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p122/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p122/r9.speaker: الحسن وعكرمة
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p122/r9.claim: Al-Hasan and Ikrima say God repeated judgments in it.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p122/r9.anchor: أحدها : ثنى الله فيه القضاء , قاله الحسن وعكرمة

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p122/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p122/r10.speaker: ابن زيد
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p122/r10.claim: Ibn Zayd says prophetic stories are repeated in it.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p122/r10.anchor: الثاني : ثنى الله فيه قصص الأنبياء , قاله ابن زيد

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p122/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p122/r11.speaker: سفيان
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p122/r11.claim: Sufyan says Paradise and Hell are repeatedly mentioned.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p122/r11.anchor: الثالث : ثنى الله فيه ذكر الجنة والنار , قاله سفيان

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p122/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p122/r12.speaker: الكلبي
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p122/r12.claim: Al-Kalbi says verses and suras follow one another.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p122/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p122/r13.speaker: ابن عيسى
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p122/r13.claim: Ibn Isa says repeated recitation does not tire because its sound is pleasing.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p122/r13.anchor: الخامس : يثنى في التلاوة فلا يمل لحسن مسموعه , قاله ابن عيسى

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p122/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p122/r14.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p122/r14.claim: Ibn Abbas says parts explain other parts.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p122/r14.anchor: السادس : معناه يفسر بعضه بعضا , قاله ابن عباس

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p122/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p122/r15.speaker: ابن بحر
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p122/r15.claim: Ibn Bahr says mathani are verse endings; Quran is the whole, sura a section, and verse a division.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p122/r15.anchor: اسم لآخر كل آية منه , قاله ابن بحر

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p122/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p122/r16.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p122/r16.claim: Al-Suddi says skin shudders at warnings and softens at promises.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p122/r16.anchor: أحدها : أنها تقشعر من وعيده وتلين من وعده , قال السدي

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p122/r17.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p122/r17.speaker: ابن عيسى
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p122/r17.claim: Ibn Isa interprets shuddering as fear and softening as hope.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p122/r17.anchor: الثاني : أنها تقشعر من الخوف وتلين من الرجاء , قاله ابن عيسى

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p122/r18.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p122/r18.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p122/r18.claim: Skin shudders from awe and softens at recitation.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p122/r18.anchor: تقشعر الجلود لإعظامه , وتلين عند تلاوته

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p25/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p25/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p25/r1.claim: Wathila ibn al-Asqaʿ reports that God gave the Prophet the seven long surahs in place of the Torah, the mathani in place of the Gospel, the miʾun in place of the Psalms, and specially favored him with the mufassal; no grading is stated.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p25/r1.anchor: عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال : ' أعطاني ربي مكان التوراة

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p25/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p25/r2.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p25/r2.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr, with similar reports from Ibn Abbas, identifies the seven long surahs as al-Baqara, Al ʿImran, al-Nisaʾ, al-Maʾida, al-Anʿam, al-Aʿraf, and Yunus; al-Mawardi calls this correct.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p25/r2.anchor: في قول سعيد بن جبير ونحوه ، عن ابن عباس ، وهو الصحيح

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p25/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p25/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p25/r3.claim: The seven surahs are called al-tiwal because they are longer than the rest of the Quran.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p25/r3.anchor: وإنما سميت السبع الطول لطولها على سائر القرآن

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p25/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p25/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p25/r4.claim: The miʾun are surahs with one hundred verses, or somewhat more or fewer.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p25/r4.anchor: ما كان من سور القرآن عدد آية مائة آية أو تزيد عليها شيئا أو تنقص عنها شيئا

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p25/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p25/r5.speaker: عبد الله بن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p25/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas and Saʿid ibn Jubayr say the mathani are surahs containing stories, parables, prescribed duties, and legal limits.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p25/r5.anchor: القصص والأمثال والفرائض والحدود ، وهذا قول عبد الله بن عباس

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p25/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p25/r6.speaker: الحسن البصري
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p25/r6.claim: Al-Hasan al-Basri identifies the mathani as the Opening; a rajaz poem calls Umm al-Kitab the seven mathani and says they are seven Quranic verses.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p25/r6.anchor: أنها فاتحة الكتاب ، وهو قول الحسن البصري ، قال الراجز :

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p25/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p25/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p25/r7.claim: A third view defines the mathani as surahs with about two hundred verses: their two hundreds have beginnings and the second hundreds are their secondary parts, as a poet's verse suggests.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p25/r7.anchor: ما ثنيت المائة فيها من السور ، فبلغ عددها مائتي آية أو ما قاربها

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p25/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p25/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p25/r8.claim: The mufassal is named for the many divisions between its surahs, identified here with the basmala.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p25/r8.anchor: لكثرة الفصول التي بين سوره ، وهو بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p25/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p25/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p25/r9.claim: The mufassal is also called muhkam on the view that nothing in it was abrogated.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p25/r9.anchor: وسمي المفصل محكما ، لما قيل إنه لم ينسخ شيء منه

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p25/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p25/r10.speaker: الأكثرون
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p25/r10.claim: Most scholars place the beginning of the mufassal at Surat Muhammad and extend it through Surat al-Nas.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p25/r10.anchor: وهو قول الآكثرين : أنه سورة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p25/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p25/r11.speaker: عيسى بن عمر
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p25/r11.claim: A second view, transmitted by ʿIsa ibn ʿUmar from many Companions, begins the mufassal at Qaf and runs to al-Nas.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p25/r11.anchor: من سورة ق إلى الناس ، حكاه عيسى بن عمر ، عن كثير من الصحابة

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p25/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p25/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p25/r12.claim: Ibn Abbas begins the mufassal at al-Duha and recited with takbir separating each pair of surahs, a practice associated with the readers of Mecca.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p25/r12.anchor: من سورة الضحى إلى الناس ، وكان يفصل في الضحى بين كل سورتين بالتكبير

MUJAHID:v2p557#2/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p557#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p557#2/r1.claim: Mujahid identifies the “best discourse” as the Qur'an.
MUJAHID:v2p557#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد في قوله الله ﴿ نزل أحسن الحديث ﴾ يعني القرآن

MUQATIL:39:23/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:39:23/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:39:23/r1.claim: The best discourse is the Quran.
MUQATIL:39:23/r1.anchor: { الله نزل أحسن الحديث } يعنى القرآن

MUQATIL:39:23/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:39:23/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:39:23/r2.claim: The book is similar throughout, with its parts resembling one another.

MUQATIL:39:23/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:39:23/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:39:23/r3.claim: Mathānī means themes are repeated two or three times or more, including past peoples, prophets, Adam and Iblis, Paradise and Hell, resurrection and judgment, plants and rain, punishment, and Moses and Pharaoh.
MUQATIL:39:23/r3.anchor: { مثاني } يعنى يثنى الأمر فى القرآن مرتين أو ثلاثا، أو أكثر من نحو ذكر الأمم الخالية

MUQATIL:39:23/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:39:23/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:39:23/r4.claim: The warnings in the Quran make the skins of those who fear their Lord's punishment shiver.
MUQATIL:39:23/r4.anchor: { تقشعر منه } يعنى مما فى القرآن من الوعيد { جلود الذين يخشون } عذاب

MUQATIL:39:23/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:39:23/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:39:23/r5.claim: Their skins and hearts then soften toward God's remembrance, meaning Paradise and its reward.
MUQATIL:39:23/r5.anchor: ثم تلين جلودهم وقلوبهم إلى ذكر الله } يعنى إلى الجنة وما فيها من الثواب

MUQATIL:39:23/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:39:23/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:39:23/r6.claim: The Quran is God's guidance by which He guides whomever He wills to His religion; no one guides a person God leads astray from it.
MUQATIL:39:23/r6.anchor: { ذلك } الذى ذكر من القرآن { هدى الله يهدي به } يعنى بالقرآن { من يشاء } لدينه { ومن يضلل الله } عن دينه { فما له من هاد }

NASAFI-FULL:v4p52#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p52#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p52#2/r1.claim: Making God's name the subject, or foregrounding it with نزل, magnifies the excellence of the revealed discourse.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p52#2/r1.anchor: فى ايقاع اسم الله مبتدا أو بناء نزل عليه تفخيم لأحسن الحديث

NASAFI-FULL:v4p52#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p52#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p52#2/r2.claim: كتابا may be an appositive to أحسن الحديث or a circumstantial accusative describing it.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p52#2/r2.anchor: ﴿ كتابا ﴾ بدل من أحسن الحديث أو حال منه

NASAFI-FULL:v4p52#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p52#2/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p52#2/r3.claim: The Quran's parts resemble one another in truth, clarity, admonition, wisdom, inimitability, and more.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p52#2/r3.anchor: يشبه بعضه بعضا فى الصدق والبيان والوعظ والحكمة والاعجاز وغير ذلك

NASAFI-FULL:v4p52#2/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p52#2/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p52#2/r4.claim: Mathānī means repeated: stories, reports, rulings, commands, prohibitions, promises, warnings, and admonitions recur, explaining the book's resemblance.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p52#2/r4.anchor: جمع مثنى بمعنى مردد ومكرر لما ثنى من قصصه وأنبائه وأحكامه وأوامره ونواهيه ووعده ووعيده ومواعظه

NASAFI-FULL:v4p52#2/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p52#2/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p52#2/r5.claim: Another explanation is that the Quran is repeated in recitation and therefore does not become tiresome.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p52#2/r5.anchor: وقيل لأنه يثنى فى التلاوة فلا يمل

NASAFI-FULL:v4p52#2/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p52#2/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p52#2/r6.claim: The singular book takes a plural description because it is a whole made of many details, as one calls the Quran portions, suras, and verses.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p52#2/r6.anchor: وإنما جاز وصف الواحد بالجمع لأن الكتاب جملة ذات تفاصيل وتفاصيل الشىء هى جملته

NASAFI-FULL:v4p52#2/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p52#2/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p52#2/r7.claim: Alternatively, مثاني is specification of متشابها, meaning recurring features resemble one another, like a man's many beautiful qualities.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p52#2/r7.anchor: أو منصوب على التمييز من متشابها كما تقول رأيت رجلا حسنا شمائل والمعنى متشابهة مثانية

NASAFI-FULL:v4p52#2/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p52#2/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p52#2/r8.claim: The skin trembles and moves; the verb describes its intense contraction.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p52#2/r9.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p52#2/r9.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p52#2/r9.claim: Hearing the Quran's warnings makes those who fear God experience awe and gooseflesh.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p52#2/r9.anchor: إذا سمعوا بالقرآن وبآيات وعيده أصابتهم خشية تقشعر منها جلودهم
