NASAFI-FULL:v4p52#2/r10.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p52#2/r10.speaker: الحديث
NASAFI-FULL:v4p52#2/r10.claim: A hadith says when a believer's skin shudders from fear of God, sins fall like leaves from a dry tree.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p52#2/r10.anchor: وفى الحديث إذا اقشعر جلد المؤمن من خشية الله تحاتت عنا ذنوبه كما يتحات عن الشجرة اليابسة ورقها

NASAFI-FULL:v4p52#2/r11.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p52#2/r11.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p52#2/r11.claim: When mercy verses are mentioned, skin and hearts soften and fear recedes; إلى conveys settling toward remembrance.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p52#2/r11.anchor: أى إذا ذكرت آيات الرحمة لانت جلودهم وقلوبهم وزال عنها ما كان بها من الخشية والقشعريرة

NASAFI-FULL:v4p52#2/r12.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p52#2/r12.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p52#2/r12.claim: إلى is used because لين takes on the sense of a verb governing إلى: they become calm toward remembrance.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p52#2/r12.anchor: وعدى بالى لتضمنه معنى فعل متعد بالى كانه قيل اطمأنت إلى ذكر الله

NASAFI-FULL:v4p52#2/r13.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p52#2/r13.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p52#2/r13.claim: Mercy is not named after remembrance because God's mercy precedes His anger, so remembering Him evokes compassion.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p52#2/r13.anchor: واقتصر على ذكر الله من غير ذكر الرحمة لأن رحمته سبقت غضبه فلا صالة رحمته إذا ذكر الله لم يخطر بالبال إلا كونه رؤوفا رحيما

NASAFI-FULL:v4p52#2/r14.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p52#2/r14.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p52#2/r14.claim: Skin is mentioned first alone, then with hearts, because the heart is the locus of fear and was already implied.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p52#2/r14.anchor: وذكرت الجلود وحدها أولا ثم قرنت بها القلوب ثانيا لأن محل الخشية القلب فكان ذكرها يتضمن ذكر القلوب

NASAFI-FULL:v4p52#2/r15.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p52#2/r15.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p52#2/r15.claim: That points to the Book; God guides by it those He knows will choose guidance.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p52#2/r15.anchor: ﴿ ذلك ﴾ اشارة إلى الكتاب وهو ﴿ هدى الله يهدي به من يشاء

NASAFI-FULL:v4p52#2/r16.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p52#2/r16.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p52#2/r16.claim: God creates misguidance in whomever He leads astray, who then has no guide to truth.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p52#2/r16.anchor: ﴿ ومن يضلل الله ﴾ يخلق الضلالة فيه

QURTUBI-FULL:39:23/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:23/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:23/r1.claim: The best hadith is the Quran: after speaking of following the best, God clarifies that the best thing heard is what He revealed.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:23/r1.anchor: يعني القرآن لما قال: { فيتبعون أحسنه } بين أن أحسن ما يسمع ما أنزله الله

QURTUBI-FULL:39:23/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:23/r2.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص
QURTUBI-FULL:39:23/r2.claim: Saʿd reports that companions asked for stories and reminders; the Quran’s best-stories verse and the call to humility before God’s remembrance followed.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:23/r2.anchor: قال سعد بن أبي وقاص قال أصحاب رسول الله

QURTUBI-FULL:39:23/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:23/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود
QURTUBI-FULL:39:23/r3.claim: Ibn Masud reports that the companions grew weary and asked the Prophet to tell them something, after which this verse was revealed.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:23/r3.anchor: وعن ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه أن أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ملوا ملة فقالوا له:

QURTUBI-FULL:39:23/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:23/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:23/r4.claim: Hadith is what a narrator relates; the Quran is called hadith because the Prophet used to tell it to his companions and people, as in the cited verses.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:23/r4.anchor: والحديث ما يحدث به المحدث. وسمى القرآن حديثا

QURTUBI-FULL:39:23/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:23/r5.speaker: القشيري
QURTUBI-FULL:39:23/r5.claim: Al-Qushayri rejects the inference that hadith here means created divine speech: newness applies to recitation, not what is recited, like remembrance in relation to God’s remembered names.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:23/r5.anchor: قال القشيري: وتوهم قوم أن الحديث من الحدوث فليدل على أن كلامه محدث

QURTUBI-FULL:39:23/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:23/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:23/r6.claim: Kitāban can be an appositive to ahsan al-hadith or a circumstantial accusative describing it.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:23/r6.anchor: { كتابا } نصب على البدل من «أحسن الحديث»

QURTUBI-FULL:39:23/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:23/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:23/r7.claim: The Quran resembles itself in beauty and wisdom, confirms itself, and contains no contradiction or disagreement.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:23/r7.anchor: يشبه بعضه بعضا في الحسن والحكمة

QURTUBI-FULL:39:23/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:23/r8.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:39:23/r8.claim: Qatada says the Quran’s verses and letters resemble one another.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:23/r8.anchor: وقال قتادة: يشبه بعضه بعضا في الآي والحروف.

QURTUBI-FULL:39:23/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:23/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:23/r9.claim: Another view says it resembles the scriptures sent to earlier prophets in its commands, prohibitions, encouragement, and warnings, while being broader and inimitable.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:23/r9.anchor: وقيل: يشبه كتب الله المنزلة على أنبيائه لما يتضمنه من أمر ونهي وترغيب وترهيب

QURTUBI-FULL:39:23/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:23/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:23/r10.claim: Mathānī refers to repeated stories, admonitions, and rulings; the text is doubled in recitation so it does not become tiresome.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:23/r10.anchor: تثنى فيه القصص والمواعظ والأحكام وثني للتلاوة فلا يمل

QURTUBI-FULL:39:23/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:23/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:23/r11.claim: Taqshaʿirru means to tremble and shiver in fear of the warnings it contains.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:23/r11.anchor: تضطرب وتتحرك بالخوف مما فيه من الوعيد

QURTUBI-FULL:39:23/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:23/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:23/r12.claim: Their skins and hearts soften toward God’s remembrance when they hear a verse of mercy.

QURTUBI-FULL:39:23/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:23/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:23/r13.claim: Alternatively, softening toward remembrance means acting according to God’s book and affirming it, or turning to Islam.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:23/r13.anchor: وقيل: إلى العمل بكتاب الله والتصديق به. وقيل: «إلى ذكر الله» يعني الإسلام.

QURTUBI-FULL:39:23/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:23/r14.speaker: أسماء بنت أبي بكر الصديق
QURTUBI-FULL:39:23/r14.claim: Asma says the Prophet’s companions wept and shivered as God describes when Quran was recited; she sought refuge from Satan when told that people now faint at recitation.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:23/r14.anchor: عن أسماء بنت أبي بكر الصديق رضي الله عنهما قالت: كان أصحاب النبي

QURTUBI-FULL:39:23/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:23/r15.speaker: ابن عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:39:23/r15.claim: Saʿid ibn al-Rahman al-Jumahi reports that Ibn Umar saw a Quran reciter collapsed; he said they feared God without collapsing and suspected Satan’s influence, unlike the Prophet’s companions.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:23/r15.anchor: وقال سعيد بن عبد الرحمن الجمحي: مر ابن عمر برجل من أهل القرآن ساقط

QURTUBI-FULL:39:23#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:23#2/r1.speaker: ابن سيرين
QURTUBI-FULL:39:23#2/r1.claim: Ibn Sirin challenges claims of Quran-induced fainting: have the person sit on a roof with legs out and recite the whole Quran; if he throws himself down, he is truthful.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:23#2/r1.anchor: وقال عمر بن عبد العزيز: ذكر عند ابن سيرين الذين يصرعون إذا قرىء عليهم القرآن

QURTUBI-FULL:39:23#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:23#2/r2.speaker: الله
QURTUBI-FULL:39:23#2/r2.claim: Abu Imran al-Jawni recounts that after Moses preached to Israel and a man tore his shirt, God told Moses to forbid wasteful tearing and ask the man to open his heart to Him.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:23#2/r2.anchor: وقال أبو عمران الجوني: وعظ موسى عليه السلام بني إسرائيل ذات يوم

QURTUBI-FULL:39:23#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:23#2/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:39:23#2/r3.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam says Ubayy ibn Kaʿb recited before the Prophet and companions became tender; the Prophet said to seize the moment for supplication because it is mercy.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:23#2/r3.anchor: قال زيد بن أسلم: قرأ أبي بن كعب عند النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ومعه أصحابه فرقوا

QURTUBI-FULL:39:23#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:23#2/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:39:23#2/r4.claim: A report from al-Abbas says that when a believer’s skin shivers from fear of God, sins fall away like leaves from a withered tree.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:23#2/r4.anchor: وعن العباس أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال:

QURTUBI-FULL:39:23#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:23#2/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:39:23#2/r5.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas says that God forbids the Fire to any servant whose skin shivers from fear of Him.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:23#2/r5.anchor: وعن ابن عباس أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال:

QURTUBI-FULL:39:23#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:23#2/r6.speaker: أم الدرداء
QURTUBI-FULL:39:23#2/r6.claim: Umm al-Darda compares fear in a person’s heart to a burning palm frond and says shivering is a cue to pray, when supplication is answered.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:23#2/r6.anchor: عن شهر بن حوشب عن أم الدرداء قالت:

QURTUBI-FULL:39:23#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:23#2/r7.speaker: فلان
QURTUBI-FULL:39:23#2/r7.claim: Thabit al-Bunani quotes an unnamed person who recognizes answered prayer when his skin shivers, heart fears, and eyes overflow.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:23#2/r7.anchor: وعن ثابت البناني قال قال فلان: إني لأعلم متى يستجاب لي

QURTUBI-FULL:39:23#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:23#2/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:23#2/r8.claim: The verb has the verbal noun iqshiʿrār and participle muqshaʿirr; its plural qashāʿir drops the extra mīm, and the state is called qashʿarīra.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:23#2/r8.anchor: يقال: اقشعر جلد الرجل اقشعرارا فهو مقشعر

QURTUBI-FULL:39:23#2/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:23#2/r9.speaker: امرؤ القيس
QURTUBI-FULL:39:23#2/r9.claim: Imru al-Qays’s line uses muqshaʿirr for the heart shivering in fear, illustrating the word’s usage.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:23#2/r9.anchor:
قال امرؤ القيس:
فبت أكابد ليل التما
م والقلب من خشية مقشعر

QURTUBI-FULL:39:23#2/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:23#2/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:23#2/r10.claim: Another explanation is that the Quran’s unmatched eloquence makes listeners’ skins shiver: they recognize their inability to rival it and feel awe at its arrangement and content.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:23#2/r10.anchor: وقيل: إن القرآن لما كان في غاية الجزالة والبلاغة، فكانوا إذا رأوا عجزهم

QURTUBI-FULL:39:23#2/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:23#2/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:23#2/r11.claim: The shivering and softening are compared to the mountain humbled and split from fear of God in the cited verse; splitting is close to shivering and humility to softening.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:23#2/r11.anchor: وهو كقوله تعالى: لو أنزلنا هذا القرآن على جبل لرأيته خاشعا متصدعا من خشية الله

QURTUBI-FULL:39:23#2/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:23#2/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:23#2/r12.claim: The heart’s softening means tenderness, calm, and tranquility.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:23#2/r12.anchor: ومعنى لين القلب رقته وطمأنينته وسكونه

QURTUBI-FULL:39:23#2/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:23#2/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:23#2/r13.claim: That guidance refers to the Quran as God’s guidance.

QURTUBI-FULL:39:23#2/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:23#2/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:23#2/r14.claim: Alternatively, the fear of punishment and hope for reward that God grants these people is His guidance.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:23#2/r14.anchor: وقيل: أي الذي وهبه الله لهؤلاء من خشية عقابه ورجاء ثوابه

QURTUBI-FULL:39:23#2/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:23#2/r15.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:23#2/r15.claim: Whoever God abandons has no guide; this statement refutes the Qadariyya and others.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:23#2/r15.anchor: أي من خذله فلا مرشد له. وهو يرد على القدرية وغيرهم

QURTUBI-FULL:39:23#2/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:23#2/r16.speaker: ابن كثير وابن محيصن
QURTUBI-FULL:39:23#2/r16.claim: Ibn Kathir and Ibn Muhaysin pronounce the final yāʾ when pausing on hād in both locations; the other readers omit it.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:23#2/r16.anchor: ووقف ابن كثير وابن محيصن على قوله: «هاد» في الموضعين بالياء، الباقون بغير ياء.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p389/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p389/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p389/r1.claim: Believers’ hearts soften on hearing mercy after the fear raised by warnings; softness metaphorically means acceptance and joy, as opposed to the hardness condemned in 39:22.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p389/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p389/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p389/r2.claim: After warnings make believers fear and avoid what is forbidden, promises make them rejoice, recognize promised good in their deeds, and turn fear into hopeful expectation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p389/r2.anchor: فإذا عقب ذلك بآيات البشارة والوعد استبشر وفرح وعرض أعماله على تلك الآيات فرأى نفسه متحلية بالعمل الذي وعد الله عليه بالثواب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p389/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p389/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p389/r5.claim: The Quran’s wonder is that it produces both fear and desire in the same believers, fitting their conduct to God’s majesty, forbearance, and mercy.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p389/r5.anchor: والمقصود وصفهم بالتأثرين عند تعاقب آيات الرحمة بعد آيات الرهبة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p389/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p389/r6.speaker: الفخر
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p389/r6.claim: Al-Fakhr quotes perfected seekers: when they encounter divine majesty they are stunned, but when a trace of beauty appears they come alive.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p389/r6.anchor: قال الفخر : إن المحققين من أهل الكمال قالوا : ( السائرون في مبدأ جلال الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p389/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p389/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p389/r7.claim: The two responses are foregrounded here because the verse calls the Quran ‘repeated’; 8:2 mentions believers’ awe at God’s mention, while this passage concerns their response to Quran recitation.
